POSITION OVERVIEW
As a Senior Business Advisor, Strategy within BDC Advisory Services, you act as a senior strategic advisor to entrepreneurs and executive teams at pivotal moments of growth, transformation, and ownership transition. BDC is the only bank dedicated exclusively to Canadian entrepreneurs, and your work directly supports the long‑term success of small and medium‑sized businesses across Canada.
This position resides in Advisory Services (management consulting) and will serve Canadian Small and Medium Entrepreneurs through our consulting mandates. This is not a Financing role. The ideal candidate will have strong business strategy consulting experience with M&A (mergers and acquisitions) and PMI (post-merger integration) experience. The ideal candidate will have a vision for the future of business in an AI driven world and will have supported the consulting sales cycle and management of a portfolio of projects delivered by consultants.
CHALLENGES TO BE MET
Lead complex, high‑impact advisory mandates for entrepreneurs and senior leadership teams, focused on enterprise‑level strategic planning, growth acceleration, organizational effectiveness, and leadership decision‑making within SME and mid‑market environments.
Maintain full accountability for mandate outcomes across multiple concurrent engagements, ensuring delivery excellence related to scope, budget, timelines, risk management, and quality of deliverables.
Act as a trusted senior advisor during periods of ambiguity, transformation, and change, applying market insight, competitive analysis, and practical experience to guide high‑stakes decisions.
Contribute to the evolution of the Strategy Centre of Expertise by developing, refining, and scaling advisory solutions, tools, and methodologies aligned with emerging client needs and market trends.
Support business development and revenue growth by partnering with senior client managers on complex sales cycles, including executive‑level diagnostics, value articulation, and proposal development.
Enable strong internal collaboration by connecting advisors, delivery teams, and relationship managers, ensuring continuity of client strategy and effective knowledge transfer across engagements.
Represent BDC Advisory Services externally through thought leadership, content development, speaking engagements, and participation in targeted events that promote Business and Organizational Capabilities solutions. At BDC, we think and act differently, and we value inclusion, equity, and authenticity—you can be yourself at work while making a tangible impact on Canadian businesses.
WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR
Required Qualifications (Must‑Have)
Bachelor’s degree in Business, Management, Strategy, or a related discipline.
Minimum
10 years of progressive experience
in a consulting environment, with senior responsibility for:
Enterprise‑level strategic planning
Executive advisory to entrepreneurs and senior management teams
Leading complex, customized consulting mandates
Demonstrated experience advising SMEs or mid‑market organizations.
Proven experience in
business strategy consulting
, including
mergers and acquisitions (M&A)
and
post‑merger integration (PMI)
.
Ability to operate at both strategic and execution levels, translating enterprise strategy into actionable, measurable plans.
Strong engagement and project management capabilities, including oversight of
multiple concurrent mandates or portfolios of work
.
Experience managing risk, quality, governance, and stakeholder expectations across consulting engagements.
Executive‑level communication and presentation skills, with credibility to influence senior stakeholders and support high‑stakes advisory and sales conversations.
Experience supporting consulting business development activities, including diagnostics, proposal development, and client pursuits.
Preferred Qualifications (Nice‑to‑Have)
MBA or equivalent advanced degree or professional designation.
Experience contributing to the development or scaling of consulting methodologies, tools, or Centres of Expertise.
Exposure to
emerging technologies
, including
artificial intelligence
, and their impact on enterprise strategy and organizational transformation.
Experience managing or overseeing a
portfolio of consulting projects delivered by other consultants
.
Experience representing a consulting practice through thought leadership, speaking engagements, or external market visibility initiatives.

As a Business Advisor, Operations within BDC Advisory Services, you act as a trusted advisor to entrepreneurs and leadership teams seeking to improve operational performance, accelerate growth, and strengthen organizational capabilities.
This position resides within Advisory Services and serves Canadian small and medium-sized businesses through advisory mandates.
The successful candidate combines deep operational expertise with strong knowledge of the technologies that enable modern manufacturing, distribution, logistics, and service operations. They understand how business processes, management systems, operational technologies, data, automation, and artificial intelligence work together to improve productivity, scalability, decision-making, and business performance.
The Business Advisor delivers both standard and customized consulting mandates, manages end-to-end project delivery, acts as a subject matter expert, supports solution development, and contributes to business development activities.
The successful candidate understands the technologies driving modern operational performance, including ERP and operational management systems, industrial automation, robotics, smart manufacturing, Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT), advanced analytics, and artificial intelligence. Operational performance improvement
Manufacturing, supply chain, logistics, and service operations

Organizational scalability and operational maturity

Currently investing out of the 500M$ Growth Venture Fund, our participations range from $5M to 40M in late stage (>$10M in revenues) innovation-based businesses in Canada that are at an inflection point and show strong potential for meaningful scale, across a broad range of technology sectors. The Growth Venture Fund team currently manages 28 active late-stage companies.
POSITION OVERVIEW
Reporting to the managing partner of the Growth Venture Fund and working collaboratively with partners, principals, associates and analysts, the Associate is an integral member of the BDC Capital team and is involved in all aspects of the investment and portfolio management process.
They will participate in the review of investment opportunities and assist in managing an existing legacy portfolio and new investments for all of the funds we manage.

Contribute to due diligence for new and/or existing investment opportunities by conducting research and analysis on markets, financial forecasts, management, competition, etc. and follow-up on investments using appropriate databases, customer interaction, internet sites, research reports and other investment resources

Ensure the accuracy and timeliness of data by developing and maintaining appropriate information resources and contacts on industries, markets and business trends and keeping abreast of significant developments and activities in the venture capital and innovation communities
Ensure that the investment research files, business plans and other information collected by the Growth Venture Fund are maintained in conformity with BDC’s policies and procedures
Monitor the investment portfolio and individual companies by providing financial, forecast and statistical analysis to ensure timely responsiveness to strategic issues within the funds
Support other Growth Venture Fund team members across the full lifecycle of an investment

Intellectual curiosity, solid analytical and synthesis skills, ability to assess the merits of new technologies, size and adoption rates of new markets and competitive forces faces when introducing new products
Possesses high energy towards work and self-development
Ability to work under pressure, deal with abstract concepts, an unstructured environment and multi-tasking

POSITION OVERVIEW
The BDC Seed Venture Fund is an early-stage venture capital fund that seeks to invest in the next generation of built-in-Canada global leaders. The fund works with companies across all seed-stages, from as early as inception, and collaborates deeply with early-stage ecosystem stakeholders including accelerators, incubators, and angel groups.  Thematic areas of interest include sectors that are poised to be transformed in the coming decade including industrials/agriculture, climate/sustainability, defense, and computing, although we like to invest at the edges and therefore remain open to investing across all emerging trends and technologies.  Post-investment the team works closely with portfolio companies and leverages its experience and networks to assist across company operations including go-to-market, hiring, fundraising, and helping portfolio companies become Series A ready.
Who you are
You are someone who wants to be a great partner to founders, someone who will be both a thought-partner and will get their hands dirty to help founders solve their most pressing problems. You are an independent thinker and can build conviction in the midst of incomplete information. You thrive connecting with others, you are collaborative, and like to teach and learn from peers. You’re hungry and motivated to drive impact for your team and the founders you work with.
Your primary responsibility will be helping to manage the daily operations of the fund, including:
Identifying new and interesting entrepreneurs and companies that align with our areas of interest
Performing market research and due diligence for potential investments
Reporting on our portfolio companies, including preparing semi-annual updates
Working with existing portfolio companies, including helping with go-to-market, product, hiring, financial modeling, and research
Executing projects of your own creation that will help build our platform, improve our operations, or support our portfolio companies
WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR
Our future teammate is someone who demonstrates:
Native understanding of the startup ecosystem and awareness of emerging technology trends
Strong written and oral communication skills
Good fundamental business instincts – you see the full picture of a business and how all the functions work together
Strong interpersonal skills – you’ll often be talking to entrepreneurs and other investors
Data-driven thinking and good Excel modeling skills
Ideally, prior design or engineering experience (either software or hardware) or work in an investment-related position
Technical skills in either category or ideally a mix of both: software/hardware/AI/ML or product/sales/operations/GTM
What we’d like to know:
Why do you want to be in VC, why seed-stage, why now?
What areas are of interest to you when it comes to investing and why?
What is an example of a time you went above and beyond, or saw around a corner, for a customer? (A customer could be in the true sense of the word, or an internal stakeholder who was relying on your work)
What is an example of an initiative you took or side project you’ve worked on outside of work or school?
Typical Professional Background
5 years of experience in a role involving critical thinking, product/engineering, financial analysis, and/or other technical expertise.
Bachelor’s degree in science, technology, engineering, mathematics, commerce, or economics.   Philosophy and psychology also viable with demonstrated technical aptitude.
A post-graduate degree or equivalent certification is valuable, including but not limited to: Master’s in business administration (MBA), other STEM Master’s or PhD degree, Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA), Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA).

description:

Joining CPP Investments means joining one of the world’s most admired and respected institutional investors to drive a single mandate: to deliver strong, sustainable returns for generations of Canadians.
With a long-term horizon and global reach, we deploy capital at scale across public and private markets. Our size, stability, and disciplined investment philosophy allow us to pursue complex opportunities and build enduring partnerships worldwide.
For our people, this means meaningful work with tangible impact, real opportunity, and collaboration with exceptional colleagues who value partnership and performance. Here, you’ll contribute
to outcomes that matter alongside team members committed to excellence and shared success.
The Role
As an Administrative Assistant, Sustainable Energies Group, you will provide day-to-day support to investment professionals across Toronto and New York. You will manage complex calendars and international travel, coordinate meetings and events, process expenses, and help the team operate effectively across global offices and time zones.
The Team
CPP Investments’ Sustainable Energies Group includes investment professionals working across London, New York, Toronto, Mumbai and São Paulo. Based in Toronto, you will work closely with investment professionals, administrative colleagues, and internal and external partners to support the team’s day-to-day activities.
Accountabilities
Manage complex calendars, meetings and correspondence for multiple investment professionals across levels and time zones
Coordinate global travel arrangements, including detailed itineraries and related logistics
Organize internal and external meetings, presentations and events in collaboration with colleagues, partners, assistants and vendors
Reconcile corporate credit card expenses and submit accurate reports through the Global Expense Reporting System
Prepare team members for meetings, track follow-up activities and help ensure action items are carried forward
Handle sensitive and confidential information with professionalism, discretion and sound judgement
Collaborate with administrative colleagues and teams across CPP Investments to manage requests, timelines and deliverables
What You Bring
Experience working in a fast-paced professional environment and supporting multiple professionals with competing priorities
Demonstrated experience managing complex calendars, senior-level meetings, events, travel and expense reimbursement
Strong organizational and prioritization skills, with close attention to accuracy and detail
Clear written and verbal communication skills and a professional, approachable manner
Proficiency with Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook and calendar-management tools, with an interest in learning new applications
Adaptability and sound judgement, with the ability to remain composed while managing time-sensitive work
Flexibility to adjust working hours when business requirements require support across global time zones
You are motivated to contribute to something larger than yourself, approach complex challenges with rigor, and hold yourself to
high standards in a collaborative, performance-driven environment.
We provide colleagues with cutting-edge AI tools, dedicated learning time, and practical support to help them deliver with greater impact.
Inclusion & Accessibility
CPP Investments is committed to
equitable access to employment and building a workforce that reflects diverse talent and perspectives. If you require accommodation at any stage of the recruitment process, please let us know and we will work with you to meet your needs.
Attention: Protect Yourself from Fraud
CPP Investments is committed to a secure and transparent recruitment process. We will never ask candidates for payment or financial information at any stage of hiring. All legitimate opportunities are posted on our careers page, and communications will come from our applicant tracking system, Workday.
CPP Investments may use AI tools to help screen and assess applicants by analyzing resumes and applications for relevant skills and experience. These tools support, but do not replace, human decision-making.

Joining CPP Investments means joining one of the world’s most admired and respected institutional investors to drive a single mandate: to deliver strong, sustainable returns for generations of Canadians.
With a long-term horizon and global reach, we deploy capital at scale across public and private markets. Our size, stability, and disciplined investment philosophy allow us to pursue complex opportunities and build enduring partnerships worldwide.
For our people, this means meaningful work with tangible impact, real opportunity, and collaboration with exceptional colleagues who value partnership and performance. Here, you’ll contribute
to outcomes that matter alongside team members committed to excellence and shared success.
The Role
We are recruiting for a Senior Associate to join CPP Investments' Real Assets Strategy Group (“RASG”), based in Toronto. RASG is part of CPP Investments' Real Assets department (“RA”), which manages approximately $160 billion in assets across its Real Estate, Infrastructure, Sustainable Energies and Listed Real Assets investment groups.
RASG is responsible for developing top-down investment perspectives, portfolio analytics and strategic frameworks that directly impact capital allocation across the RA portfolio. Working closely with other investment teams, the group translates macroeconomic and thematic insights into portfolio actions that enhance portfolio construction and long-term alpha generation.
Reporting to the Managing Director, Head of Real Assets Strategy, the successful candidate will support thematic investing, develop quantitative investment frameworks and portfolio recommendations, and contribute to AI-enabled investment processes that strengthen investment decision-making across the department. This role is ideal for intellectually curious investors who enjoy combining macro thinking, quantitative analysis, technology and investment judgment to solve complex portfolio problems.
The Team
Accountabilities
Work with Real Assets investment teams and stakeholders across CPP Investments to develop portfolio-level analytics, relative-value insights and investment strategies that support alpha generation.
Conduct rigorous thematic research on structural, macroeconomic and industry trends affecting RA, and translate findings into differentiated and actionable investment actions that influence capital deployment priorities and portfolio construction decisions.
Build, enhance and maintain financial, statistical and portfolio models used for investment analysis, portfolio construction, risk assessment and strategic asset-allocation work.
Synthesize public and proprietary research, internal subject-matter expertise and external specialist perspectives into clear, decision-useful insights.
Support the design and implementation of portfolio actions arising from thematic and relative-value work.
Apply, and in some cases develop, AI and emerging analytical tools to enhance investment research, scenario analysis, portfolio monitoring and investment decision-making. Contribute to the design, evaluation and adoption of AI-enabled workflows that improve investment effectiveness across the department.
Prepare high-quality presentations, memoranda and other materials for senior management, investment committees and Board-related discussions.
Manage workstreams with multiple stakeholders, maintain clear project plans and communicate findings and recommendations effectively.
Qualifications
4-6 years of relevant work experience (e.g., strategy consulting or investing role)
University degree in finance, economics, engineering, mathematics or a related quantitative discipline.
Direct investment experience is preferred but not essential, but a keen interest in portfolio management, portfolio construction and an understanding of relevant asset classes is desirable
Clear and proven communication and presentation skills (oral and written)
Strong quantitative, research, financial modelling and analytical skills.
Strong interpersonal and relationship building skills both within a team as well as across different groups in an organization.
Demonstrated ability to leverage generative AI, machine learning or advanced analytical tools to improve research, modelling or investment workflows
Highly organized with strong attention to detail; ability to deliver high-quality work across competing deadlines
Self-motivated and adaptable, with the ability to thrive in a dynamic, fast-paced environment and balance shifting priorities.
You are motivated to contribute to something larger than yourself, approach complex challenges with rigor, and hold yourself to
high standards in a collaborative, performance-driven environment.

The Role
This newly created Toronto-based role combines broad legal support across Credit Investments with a targeted focus on restructuring matters.
Reporting to the Managing Director, Legal supporting Credit Investments, you will provide strategic and commercially focused legal advice across the department’s investment and asset management activities.
The Team
Credit Investments invests globally across leveraged finance, real estate and infrastructure lending, structured credit and special situations. The team manages investments throughout their lifecycle, including restructurings, workouts and other stressed and distressed situations, consistent with CPP Investments’ Guiding Principles and investment mandate.
As a member of the global Investment Legal team, you will work closely with Credit Investments deal teams, senior lawyers in CPP Investments’ international offices and partners across the organization. The role provides exposure to investments and situations across North America, Europe and other markets and may periodically involve travel.
Accountabilities

Provide senior-level legal advice on restructurings, workouts, liability management exercises, distressed exchanges, enforcement and insolvency proceedings, including negotiation strategy, lender group and intercreditor dynamics, documentation and risk allocation
Select, direct and critically engage with external legal and financial advisors while maintaining strong internal ownership of legal strategy, judgment and decision-making
Anticipate, identify and support the management of legal risks arising from evolving liability management practices, new investment strategies and changes in laws or regulations affecting CPP Investments’ credit strategies
Partner with deal teams and senior stakeholders to develop practical recommendations in complex, contested and fast-evolving situations where the legal or commercial path may not be immediately clear

Contribute to Legal Department and CPP Investments-wide initiatives and projects

Qualification to practice law in Ontario or an equivalent common law jurisdiction
8+ years of post-qualification legal experience with a major international law firm or the in-house legal department of an asset manager, credit fund, bank or other financial investor, including substantial restructuring, workout and special situations experience and broader credit and finance transactional practice
Demonstrated experience leading creditor-side strategy in complex restructurings, liability management exercises and distressed situations, including lender and steering group dynamics, intercreditor negotiations and contested outcomes
Strong knowledge of leveraged finance and private credit documentation across direct lending, structured credit and asset-backed strategies, together with practical familiarity with restructuring and insolvency regimes relevant to CPP Investments’ credit portfolio, including Canada and the United States; European experience is an asset
Strong legal and commercial judgment, with the ability to assess ambiguous or novel situations, distinguish material issues and make practical recommendations with incomplete information
Ability to operate independently and effectively in fast-moving and potentially adversarial situations while managing multiple priorities and maintaining important market relationships
Strong communication, interpersonal and organizational skills, including the credibility to advise and influence investment professionals and collaborate effectively with a broad range of stakeholders

title: Managing Director, Credit Restructuring
description:
Purpose. Performance. People.
Joining CPP Investments means joining one of the world’s most admired and respected institutional investors to drive a single mandate: to deliver strong, sustainable returns for generations of Canadians.
With a long-term horizon and global reach, we deploy capital at scale across public and private markets. Our size, stability, and disciplined investment philosophy allow us to pursue complex opportunities and build enduring partnerships worldwide.
For our people, this means meaningful work with tangible impact, real opportunity, and collaboration with exceptional colleagues who value partnership and performance. Here, you’ll contribute
to outcomes that matter alongside team members committed to excellence and shared success.
The Role
Credit Investments (CI) is seeking an experienced restructuring professional to strengthen its capability to manage underperforming, stressed and distressed credit investments as the portfolio grows in scale and complexity.
The Managing Director, Restructuring will provide dedicated senior creditor-side expertise across workouts, liability management exercises (LMEs), restructurings, liquidity solutions and other stressed situations. The role will partner with CI investment teams to preserve investment value, maximize recoveries and support effective positioning ahead of key events.
The Team
Credit Investments currently manages assets in excess of $80.5 billion; investment deal sizes range from $50M to over $1B. The Credit Investments team has over 147 investment professionals across North America, Europe and Asia.
Reporting to the Head of Credit Strategy, the role will work closely with CI investment teams, Legal, Portfolio Management and senior leadership, and will contribute to broader CPP Investments matters where restructuring expertise can add value. The role is expected to be based in Toronto or New York.
Accountabilities
Lead Restructuring Strategy and Execution
Serve as CI's senior restructuring expert and provide commercial leadership and decision-making authority on material stressed and distressed investments.
Partner with investment teams to develop and execute restructuring strategies designed to protect investment value and maximize recoveries. The restructuring lead and relevant deal team will be co-accountable, with the deal team retaining ownership of the ultimate investment outcome.
Lead negotiations involving amendments, waivers, recapitalizations, exchange offers, LMEs, rescue financings, asset sales, refinancings and formal restructuring processes.
Assess alternative restructuring pathways and advise on likely outcomes, negotiating leverage, new-money requirements, timing and execution risk, drawing on relevant market precedents and judgment on key economic terms.
Support investment teams in anticipating potential creditor actions and positioning CI effectively ahead of key events.
Provide Senior Commercial Judgment
Provide independent challenge and advice on capital structure, liquidity, valuation, recovery scenarios, financing alternatives and strategic options in distressed situations.
Help teams identify and use sources of negotiating leverage, including opportunities to build alignment with other stakeholders, while engaging constructively and credibly with borrowers, sponsors, shareholders and other creditors.
Advise on creditor-group formation, steering committees and lender-coordination processes, and support the selection and efficient direction of external restructuring bankers, financial advisers and other specialists.
Bring current restructuring market intelligence, conventions and precedents to portfolio-management decisions.
Assess proposed outcomes across recovery value, incremental capital, time to resolution, external costs, reputational considerations and demands on deal-team capacity. Success will be measured primarily through avoided losses and recoveries achieved rather than direct AUM attribution.
Partner with Deal Teams and Legal
Work alongside existing deal teams as athe lead restructuring specialist adviser rather than operating as a separate distressed-investing team; deal teams remain actively involved and accountable for the investment outcome.
Work closely with CI Legal, including dedicated restructuring legal resources, to integrate commercial, negotiating and legal strategy. Legal will advise on documentation, contractual rights and available legal pathways, while this role will lead the commercial strategy and value-maximizing trade-offs informed by that advice.
Partner with Portfolio Management and senior CI leadership to identify situations requiring early intervention and build strong working relationships across CI and, where appropriate, other CPP Investments departments.
Strengthen CI's Restructuring Platform
Play a leadership role in CI's restructuring panel, including triaging situations, challenging strategies and mobilizing resources.
Establish regular watchlist triage to identify situations where specialist involvement can add value before a formal default or restructuring.
Develop restructuring playbooks, precedent libraries, market intelligence and other institutional resources; lead post-mortems and transfer lessons across CI investment teams.
Coach and develop investment professionals to increase restructuring knowledge and judgment and help build a scalable capability for a substantially larger CI portfolio. The role will have no direct people-leadership responsibilities initially, although this may change as the portfolio and workout activity grow.
Broader Contribution
During periods of lower restructuring activity, contribute to broader CI strategic and portfolio initiatives where restructuring, capital-structure, valuation, transaction or market expertise can add value.
Where appropriate, provide restructuring expertise to other parts of CPP Investments and represent CPP Investments credibly with borrowers, sponsors, banks, advisers and institutional creditors in complex and sensitive situations.
What You Bring
Significant restructuring experience gained as a banker or adviser at a leading restructuring advisory firm, or investment bank.
Senior-level experience (approximately 15 years) consistent with a Managing Director appointment, with a demonstrated ability to lead complex restructuring processes and advise sophisticated institutional clients.
Deep creditor-side experience representing lenders, bondholders, creditor groups and/or institutional investors.
Extensive experience with LMEs, complex out-of-court restructurings and formal restructuring processes.
Strong expertise in liquidity analysis, capital structures, valuation, recovery analysis, financing alternatives and transaction execution.
Demonstrated experience negotiating with sponsors, companies, creditor groups and advisers in high-stakes situations.
Strong knowledge of restructuring market conventions, precedents and creditor dynamics.
Meaningful familiarity with restructuring documentation and legal concepts, and the ability to work effectively with counsel.
Strong executive presence and judgment, with the ability to influence senior investment professionals while operating in a collaborative, advisory capacity.
Ability to move between detailed transaction execution and broader strategic judgment, with a collaborative mindset suited to CI's deal-team ownership model.
This information for those living or expecting to live in New York City. The salary range for this position is: USD $275,000 - $460,000
US state/city legislation requires CPP investments to include a reasonable estimate of the compensation range for this role. The base salary range shown here is a reasonable expectation for the posted role and is part of a competitive total rewards package which includes comprehensive benefits, a performance-based incentive plan, a 401 (k) plan and paid time off. Actual salaries may vary and may be above or below the range based on various factors, including, but not limited to, experience and expertise.

The Portfolio Manager will work closely with teams across TFM to design, evaluate, and implement robust frameworks for Total Fund exposure management. Joining CPP Investments means joining one of the world’s most admired and respected institutional investors to drive a single mandate: to deliver strong, sustainable returns for generations of Canadians.
With a long-term horizon and global reach, we deploy capital at scale across public and private markets. Our size, stability, and disciplined investment philosophy allow us to pursue complex opportunities and build enduring partnerships worldwide.
For our people, this means meaningful work with tangible impact, real opportunity, and collaboration with exceptional colleagues who value partnership and performance. Here, you’ll contribute
to outcomes that matter alongside team members committed to excellence and shared success.
The Role
Join CPP Investments as an Analyst in our Early Investor Program, a full-time opportunity designed for exceptional new graduates to launch their career at a leading global investment organization.
You will be placed directly into one team within Credit Investments or Real Assets, where you will contribute to meaningful work from the start. From day one, you will combine the depth of being embedded in an investment team with a structured development experience designed specifically for early-career investors.
Your development will extend beyond your day-to-day role – and it doesn’t stop after initial training.  You’ll begin with CPP Investments’ LAUNCH onboarding and Wall Street Prep training, building a solid foundation in investment concepts, technical skills, and analytical frameworks. Throughout the multi-week program, you’ll continue to develop through curated learning experiences, mentorship and coaching from experienced investors, exposure to senior leaders and opportunities to learn alongside your peers.
While anchored in one team, your experience will extend across CPP Investments’ interconnected investment platform. Program-wide learning, networking and cross functional exposure will introduce you to diverse investment perspectives and help you understand how capital is deployed across global markets. You will have the opportunity to develop deep expertise in your asset class while building the broader perspective and network of a global investor.
You’ll also join a community that encourages curiosity, inclusion, and continuous learning. Through employee resource groups, early-career mentorship, online learning tools, and connections across the organization, you will have the support and resources to continue shaping your development and building a career at CPP Investments.
The Team
Participating Teams
Each investment department offers a distinct path to expertise, career growth, and impact. You will join
one team
, gain
deep asset-class knowledge
, and work on
high-impact projects
with early
responsibility

mentorship
.
Credit Investments (CI) Department
Americas Structured Credit;
Invests across asset-backed and specialty finance opportunities, delivering tailored capital solutions across debt, hybrid and equity investments. Analysts gain exposure to a diverse range of asset classes while evaluating new opportunities and supporting underwriting, due diligence and portfolio management.
Credit Strategy:
Manages investments across global public and private credit markets, with a focus on single-name fundamental credit, relative value analysis and portfolio construction for the global Credit Investments platform. The team analyzes individual companies and securities, monitors existing investments, and compares risk and return opportunities across markets to identify where capital can be most effectively deployed. These insights inform portfolio construction, asset allocation, and risk management across Credit Investments. Analysts gain broad exposure to company and industry analysis, credit markets, investment monitoring and relative value, while developing an understanding of how individual investment decisions fit within a broader portfolio.
Public
Credit;
Invests globally across public credit markets, with a strong focus on fundamental company and industry research, single-name credit analysis, and relative value. The team invests across liquid credit products and capital structures, combining investment judgement with data and technology to generate insights, monitor credits, and identify opportunities across global markets.
Real Assets (RA) Department
Sustainable Energies;
Invests globally across the full energy value chain, from power and renewables to midstream, upstream, and distributed energy opportunities. Analysts support transactions, underwriting and portfolio management across a diverse set of assets and investment structures, gaining hands-on exposure to how capital is deployed across the evolving energy sector.
Private Equity (PE) Department
Invests in private markets by backing top-performing private equity funds and investing directly alongside leading managers, spanning buyouts and growth equity across sectors and geographies. The team seeks out managers with strong, proven track records, and partners with them in their highest-conviction opportunities. Analysts gain experience of how private opportunities and sponsor relationships are originated, evaluated and monitored, developing skills in company, fund and industry analysis, financial modelling and partner diligence, while building an understanding of how investments fit together within a broader private equity portfolio.
Accountabilities
Analyzing and evaluating a wide range of industries, companies, funds, and securities, including the performance and capabilities of management teams.
Conducting valuation analysis of companies, assets, and securities to assess potential risk and return.
Performing due diligence or asset management of funds, assets, and companies, evaluating financial performance, market dynamics, competitive positioning, management quality, and expected merits and risks.
Building financial models to evaluate and compare investment positions or opportunities.
Supporting the investment process by providing insights, analysis, and recommendations that inform how we deploy capital around the world.
Collaborating with your team to prepare investment reviews, industry and market overviews, and written investment rationales.
Exploring opportunities across global markets to identify and assess new areas for investment.
Applying statistical and qualitative analysis to strengthen investment decisions and portfolio performance.
Researching and reporting on macroeconomic trends that influence markets and investment strategies.
Engaging directly with external management teams, industry experts, and other investors to gain insights and inform your analysis.
Qualifications
We’re looking for students in undergraduate programs who are ready to begin full-time in
September 2027
. Successful candidates combine a strong academic record with extracurricular involvement and leadership experience. We value analytical and financial acumen, clear and persuasive communication skills, and the ability to build strong, collaborative relationships.
The strongest applicants bring intellectual curiosity, open-mindedness, and a genuine passion for investing. If you’re eager to learn, contribute, and grow within a global, high-performing investment platform, we encourage you to apply.

Contribute to research on industries, companies, and securities to evaluate fundamentals, market positioning, and competitive dynamics.
Support valuation analysis to assess potential risks, returns, and key value drivers.
Contribute to due diligence and asset management efforts by gathering and synthesizing data on financial performance, market trends, and strategic developments.

Reporting to the Executive Producer of Live & Daily News, Weekends, you help meet CBC’s strategic goals, including working across platforms to meet audience needs no matter where they consume our content.

Live Experience:

Manage Production & Broadcast:
Exercise editorial responsibility over daily production and live broadcasting. Co-ordinate resources and determine the look, style, and pace of the lineup to maintain consistency with network mandates. Thrive under intense deadline pressures.

Change Agent:
Drives continuous improvement, agile and adaptable in transforming newsroom structures and roles and lead transitions. You understand what motivates people. You welcome feedback and carefully consider that input as you align your team around shared goals. You celebrate success.

Foster Collaboration:
Facilitate open, inclusive story meetings. Encourage story pitches and development. Collaborate across CBC News platforms to co-ordinate content, such raw sound, clipped material and packaged audio items.
●
Team Leadership:
Actively support staff development, provide ongoing constructive feedback and coaching. Connect regularly with senior leadership about staffing and scheduling requirements and team culture.
●
Champion Audience Growth:
Translate insights and data to guide content decisions to expand our reach to new and younger news consumers, and to deepen our engagement with all Canadians.
●

Strictly uphold CBC’s Journalistic Standards and Practices at all times.
●
Operational Support:
Step in to perform all or part of the functions of an equivalent or lower classification as needed.

Experience:
Minimum of seven years in broadcast journalism, with a university degree or college diploma in journalism, audio production, or a related field.

Live Broadcast Expertise:
Proven experience producing live and breaking news programming, including production planning and resource co-ordination. Demonstrated ability as a programmer with a keen ear for pacing, tone, and presentation.

Technical Proficiency:
Mandatory experience taking programs to air, alongside highly developed audio production skills. Familiarity with technology including iNews, Dalet, Avid Media Central and Google tools for content creation, distribution, and planning.

Broad Knowledge Base:

Editorial and Assignment Planning: You, working closely with your fellow executive producer of Canada newsgathering, are a key decision maker in determining what stories we cover 24/7 and across platforms. You are plugged into what’s happening across Canada, scanning the competition, digging into meeting minutes and creating calendars for upcoming events.  You can pivot quickly to cover breaking and live news; and are equally adept at planning for future events and specials in collaboration with CBC News colleagues. You are innovative in your approach with a focus on finding more opportunities to report live from the field.
Deployment & Resource Co-ordination:  You oversee assignment meetings and the pitch process, ensuring a Canadian overview is reflected in our daily news coverage. You work closely with newsroom leadership to manage deployments while prioritizing the physical and mental well-being of employees.

You create a culture of collaboration, feedback and support, ensuring the safety and well-being of the team is considered in every assignment.
Champion Audience Growth: Your decisions are focused on expanding our reach to new and younger news consumers, and to deepen our engagement with all Canadians. You understand the pulse of Canadian audiences, their habits and what they need from your coverage. You are able to translate insights and data into actionable content strategies for all platforms.
Uphold Journalistic Excellence: You have a deep understanding of CBC’s rigorous Journalistic Standards and Practises. You help your team navigate complex ethical and legal considerations with grace and precision.

You inspire your team to think inclusively, always asking whose voice is missing and you work diligently to close that gap. You collaborate with journalistic leaders across CBC News, ensuring our daily coverage is reflective of the stories and issues that help Canadians make sense of their world.
Innovate & Strategize: You demonstrate daily the role of a public broadcaster in a media landscape proliferated with misinformation, disinformation and rapidly evolving technologies. Verification is a core value. You lean into data, and use it to drive audience-focused strategies for your team. You translate big ideas into tangible actions.

Has a minimum of seven years of leadership experience in a fast-paced news environment, particularly in roles involving breaking news, national coverage and overseeing large teams through times of change. Experience risk assessment and management is an asset, experience in change management.

Finds solutions to a variety of technical, resource and operational issues and can make decisions on tight deadlines; can effectively juggle multiple short and long term tasks and projects.

Risk Technology is part of the Data Technology group and partners primarily with Investment Risk to deliver technology, data, analytics, reporting, and production-support capabilities through small and medium-sized initiatives, multi-year programs, and ongoing operational services.
As a key member of the Risk Technology team, the Senior Data Engineer will be the team’s senior hands-on Power BI developer, responsible for designing complex reports and visuals, scalable semantic models, and governed business intelligence solutions. The successful candidate will be expected to apply a practical understanding of Fabric capacity, compute consumption, memory constraints, performance, and workload management.
The role also requires strong data engineering capability. The successful candidate will build and support reliable data pipelines that hydrate Power BI semantic models from enterprise data warehouses and will develop complex ETL and transformation solutions using Azure Databricks, Snowflake, Azure Data Factory, SQL, Python, and PySpark.
This position combines deep technical delivery with stakeholder partnership. The incumbent will collaborate with business users, business systems analysts, data engineers, platform teams, and external providers, and will contribute to a constructive, inclusive, and accountable team environment. The role follows the organization’s hybrid working model and requires regular in-office collaboration.
The incumbent will report to the Senior Manager, Data Technology.
As a Member of Our Team You Will be Responsible For:
Power BI development and reporting framework (Primary Area of Accountability)
Design, develop, test, deploy, and support sophisticated Power BI reports, dashboards, and interactive visual experiences for Investment Risk and related stakeholders.
Build and optimize enterprise-grade Power BI semantic models, including dimensional design, relationships, measures, calculation groups where appropriate, row-level security, object-level security, incremental refresh, and model performance tuning.
Write and optimize complex DAX and Power Query (M) logic, applying clear development standards and reusable design patterns.
Partner closely with business users to translate analytical requirements into intuitive visual designs, rapidly prototype solutions, validate usability, and incorporate feedback throughout delivery.
Understand and actively manage Fabric capacity considerations, including compute consumption, memory guardrails, concurrency, refresh demand, background versus interactive workloads, throttling risk, and workload optimization.
Use capacity and performance telemetry to identify bottlenecks, recommend remediation, and balance report responsiveness, refresh schedules, model size, and platform stability.
Design and support data pipelines that reliably hydrate Power BI semantic models from Snowflake, Databricks, enterprise data warehouses, lakehouses, and other approved data sources.
Implement governed Power BI access management, including workspaces, apps, audiences, Microsoft Entra security groups, role-based access, sharing, row-level security, deployment permissions, and periodic access reviews.
Design, build, test, and support Power Automate cloud flows that extend Power BI solutions through data-driven alerts, notifications, approvals, scheduled actions, and user-triggered workflows.
Apply appropriate Power Automate governance and support practices, including connection management, environment awareness, secure sharing, run monitoring, exception handling, and operational documentation.
Promote effective Power BI lifecycle management through source control, deployment pipelines, environment segregation, release controls, documentation, and CI/CD practices.
Data Engineering (Secondary Area of Accountability)
Develop complex, performant, and maintainable solutions in Azure Databricks and Snowflake using SQL, Python, and PySpark.
Develop and orchestrate data integration workflows using Azure Data Factory and other approved Azure data services.
Create and optimize database objects, data transformations, data quality controls, and reconciliation processes with a strong understanding of dimensional and analytical data modeling.
Build custom services and workflows when needed to complement platform capabilities, including file-format conversion, third-party API integration, and external web-service calls.
Automate manual processes and improve data delivery, observability, scalability, recoverability, and operational efficiency.
Contribute to solution architecture and technical design for the Databricks, Snowflake, Microsoft Fabric, and Azure data ecosystem.
Delivery, Operations and Collaboration
Work closely with business systems analysts, subject-matter experts, platform teams, and vendors to deliver solutions, investigate root causes, recommend changes, and maintain accurate technical and operational documentation.
Monitor production solutions, investigate incidents, perform performance tuning, and enhance service reliability through effective incident, problem, change, configuration, and release-management practices.
Prepare functional and technical specifications, data-flow documentation, support procedures, test evidence, deployment plans, and knowledge-transfer materials.
Facilitate testing and production implementation while acting as a trusted liaison between Technology, Investment Risk stakeholders, and external solution providers.
Share design, coding, troubleshooting, and analytical practices with colleagues through reviews, pairing, documentation, and knowledge sessions.
Demonstrate a constructive and collaborative working style, openness to feedback, accountability for outcomes, and willingness to support colleagues across disciplines.
Participate effectively in the organization’s hybrid working model, including regular in-office collaboration with the team and stakeholders.
What do you need to succeed?
Minimum 7 years of progressive experience in advanced Power BI development expertise, including complex report design, visual storytelling, semantic modeling, DAX, Power Query, model optimization, refresh design, and troubleshooting.
Experience of delivering data, analytics, data warehousing, or business intelligence solutions, with substantial recent hands-on Power BI development experience.
Demonstrated experience building governed, enterprise-scale Power BI solutions rather than solely creating ad hoc or departmental reports.
Hands-on Microsoft Fabric experience, or directly transferable experience with Power BI Premium capacity, including capacity monitoring, compute and memory constraints, workload management, performance tuning, and migration planning.
Experience designing and operating pipelines that load or transform data for Power BI semantic models from cloud data warehouses or Lakehouse platforms.
Practical experience administering Power BI access through workspaces, apps, audiences, security groups, permissions, and row-level security, with an understanding of least-privilege access and controlled content distribution.
Hands-on experience developing and supporting Power Automate cloud flows, ideally integrated with Power BI, Microsoft 365, approvals, alerts, or other enterprise services.
Minimum 3 years of Databricks experience with strong data engineering experience, including complex transformations and performance-aware development.
Advanced SQL skills, including complex queries, tables, views, stored procedures, query optimization, and performance tuning.
Proficiency in Python and PySpark for scalable data processing and automation.
Developed data warehouses with change data capture (CDC) and implemented dimensional data warehouses.
Understanding data quality, GitHub source control, CI/CD, and production support practices for enterprise BI and data solutions.
Strong communication, problem-solving, prioritization, and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively with technical and business stakeholders in a hybrid environment.
Experience in financial services, pension management, investment management, and capital markets is desirable.
Relevant Microsoft Power BI, Fabric, Azure data engineering, Databricks, Snowflake, or Power Platform certification is an asset.

At Ontario Health, we are committed to developing a strong organizational culture that connects and inspires all team members across the province. Our vision is that together, we will be a leader in health and wellness for all. Our mission is to connect the health system to drive improved and equitable health outcomes, experiences and value. How we work together is reflected through our five values: integrity, inspiration, tenacity, humility and care.
What Ontario Health offers:
At Ontario Health, your growth and well-being aren’t just supported—they’re celebrated every step of the way. Here, you have the opportunity to make a meaningful impact while shaping a fulfilling and sustainable career. Based on your role, you may receive:
Comprehensive health coverage from day one
, with fully paid medical, dental, and vision benefits to support you and your family’s health
Flexible health care or wellness spending accounts
, plus an inclusive program to support your overall well-being
A premium defined benefit pension plan
, ensuring long-term financial security

that encourages time to rest and recharge
Three personal days and two float days annually
, providing added flexibility to support work-life balance, in addition to vacation days
Ongoing learning and career development opportunities
designed to help you grow, advance, and thrive in your profession
A collaborative, values-driven workplace
where integrity, care, humility, inspiration, and tenacity shape everything we do
Opportunities to participate in Communities of Inclusion
, fostering belonging, equity, and the sharing of diverse perspectives across our team
Want to make a difference in your career?  Consider this opportunity.
Ontario Health Toronto’s Health System Strategy, Design and Engagement team advances regional strategies that bring provincial priorities to life in Toronto’s diverse local context. The team leads high-impact work in health equity, strategic partnerships, patient and caregiver engagement, and engagement with Francophone, First Nations, Inuit, Métis, Urban Indigenous, Black and other equity-deserving communities.
The Health Equity Lead, Indigenous Populations will play a key role in strengthening Ontario Health Toronto’s Indigenous engagement and health equity strategies, aligned with Ontario Health’s broader Equity, Inclusion, Diversity and Anti-Racism and Indigenous Health Equity portfolios.
Working with regional and provincial partners, Indigenous communities and organizations, this role will help advance culturally safe learning, working and care environments, improve access to services, and support system-level change that responds to the needs, values and preferences of Indigenous peoples.
As a trusted connector and subject matter lead, the successful candidate will support engagement with First Nations, Inuit, Métis and Urban Indigenous communities, patients, caregivers, partners and internal teams to shape strategies that improve Indigenous health outcomes and experiences across the Toronto Region.
Here is what you will be doing:
General
Build and sustain collaborative relationships with Indigenous communities, health system partners, service providers and internal teams to advance regional priorities and Ontario Health’s mission.
Represent Ontario Health Toronto on regional, provincial and local committees, working groups and project teams focused on integration, quality care and health equity.
Provide advice, reports and strategic input to senior leaders and program areas on Indigenous engagement, community issues, communications and change impacts.
Foster respectful, results-focused collaboration across partners to support shared accountability and meaningful outcomes.
Health Leadership
Lead engagement with First Nations, Inuit, Métis and Urban Indigenous communities, organizations, leaders and partners, supporting culturally appropriate protocols, events, workshops and communication.
Serve as a regional subject matter expert on Indigenous health equity, engagement, planning and facilitation, sharing promising practices and supporting alignment across the region.
Collaborate with internal and cross-regional colleagues to identify opportunities, address challenges and advance strategies that improve Indigenous health experiences and outcomes.
Lead or support ministry reporting, provincial initiatives and related deliverables connected to the Indigenous health equity portfolio.
Project & Change Management
Monitor health system trends, priorities and emerging issues related to Indigenous health equity, engagement and system change.
Plan, coordinate and manage projects that support regional priorities, including assigning resources, tracking progress, maintaining records and completing required reporting.
Develop value-added processes and practical solutions that support core regional work and continuous improvement.
Perform other duties as assigned.
Here is what you will need to be successful:
Education and Experience
Post-secondary degree in health administration, health planning, business administration, research or a relevant field, or an equivalent combination of education, training and experience.
Five years of management experience in complex, dynamic health care environments in the public and/or private sectors, including health care service delivery management.
Three years of experience working in Indigenous programs related to health education.
Good understanding of the City of Toronto FNIMUI population landscape, including urban communities, health service providers, First Nation communities, community engagement and cultural protocols.
Preference will be given to individuals with lived experience in a FNIMUI community and to candidates with an understanding of Ontario Health Toronto Region Indigenous languages.
Good working knowledge of FNIMUI health planning processes, including jurisdictional issues associated with the delivery of Indigenous health care services, and sensitivity to federal and provincial FNIMUI health planning processes.
Experience building and nurturing relationships with Indigenous communities, Leaders, Elders, Language-Speakers, Oral Historians and Knowledge Keepers.
Knowledge of the Ministry of Health, Ministry of Long-Term Care and the health care system, including the evolving role of Ontario Health, sector issues and priorities, and their impact on service delivery and patient/provider experience.
Demonstrated information-gathering techniques and resources.
Proven ability to be a productive team member and lead project teams.
Understanding of the Ontario health care system, its stakeholders, programs and issues.
Expert knowledge of planning models and approaches, recognizing broader trends in health care policy and system development.
Experience in process improvement methodology is an asset.
Experience in project management methodology, including use of project management software, is an asset.
Knowledge and Skills
Demonstrated passion for advancing health care within a system-wide strategy and responding to broader challenges in changing health care policies through a health equity lens.
Results-oriented leadership style that encourages empowerment, collaboration, accountability and sound decision-making.
Demonstrated mentorship and team-building skills, including the ability to inspire and motivate staff, achieve outcomes, demonstrate commitment to mission and values, and function effectively with tact and diplomacy while managing stressful issues.
Effective communication skills, including listening, presenting and conveying messages in an honest, open, transparent and straightforward style; strong writing skills, including experience writing business cases, briefing notes, funding proposals and evidence-based reports.
Strong facilitation skills, including comfort developing and delivering presentations and engaging with FNIMUI people.
Proven problem-solving, critical-thinking and conflict-management competencies.
Strong relationship management skills, including demonstrated experience working effectively in partnership with a broad range of individuals and organizations of diverse backgrounds.
Strategic planning skills, including the ability to develop short- and longer-term plans that reflect current trends, identify future priorities for relevance and leadership, and operationalize strategies to execute key priorities.
Strong change management skills, including the ability to focus priorities, drive positive change, and encourage accountability in self and others.
Risk management skills, including the ability to measure and evaluate outcomes and adjust direction as appropriate.

Promotes and leads a person-centred approach, and ensures the work is aligned with the Ontario Cancer Plan and other Ontario Health priorities

Oversees annual and multi-year portfolio planning and determines the human and financial resources required to deliver strategic and operational priorities.
Provides system-level leadership to identify emerging issues, opportunities and innovations and translate them into actionable provincial strategies.
Oversees the development, implementation and evaluation of evidence-informed clinical guidance, standards, recommendations, tools and other resources to support high-quality cancer care.
Provides full people leadership through a team of managers, including recruitment, performance management, coaching and development, succession planning and establishment of clear accountabilities and priorities.
Oversees the recruitment, onboarding, performance and ongoing engagement of Provincial Clinical Leads and other clinical experts.
Develops and advances business cases, funding proposals and recommendations to support provincial clinical and system priorities.
Collaborate with internal and external project teams, partners, government, working groups, committees, and colleagues to conceptualize, secure funding, plan and implement quality improvement initiatives
Works across Ontario Health portfolios to advance shared priorities, manage interdependencies and identify and mitigate organizational and system-level risks.

title: Lead, Capacity, Access & Flow
description:

À Santé Ontario, nous sommes résolus à bâtir une solide culture organisationnelle qui unifie et responsabilise tous les membres de notre équipe à travers la province. Une couverture santé complète dès le premier jour,

Voulez-vous faire la différence dans votre carrière?  Examinez l'opportunité qui s'offre à vous.
Relevant du directeur, Capacité, accès aux soins et flux des patients, le responsable fait progresser les stratégies régionales visant à améliorer la capacité du système de santé, l'accès, le flux des patients et les résultats liés aux autres niveaux de soins (ANS) à Toronto.
Dans le cadre de ses fonctions, le titulaire collabore avec des dirigeants cliniques et administratifs ainsi qu'avec des équipes transversales afin de renforcer la performance et les activités du système de santé dans l'ensemble de la région de Toronto.
Il s'agit d'un rôle régional axé sur l'évolution des besoins et des priorités de la région de Toronto.
Voici ce que vous aurez à faire :
Planification et amélioration du système de santé
Analyser les données régionales, les commentaires de la communauté et les pratiques exemplaires afin de cerner les lacunes du système, les priorités et les possibilités d'amélioration.
Diriger des initiatives régionales et des plans d'action éclairés par les données afin d'améliorer l'accès, le flux des patients et les résultats liés aux ANS.
Planification de la capacité du système
Surveiller la performance régionale en matière d'accès et de flux, cerner les tendances et les lacunes et soutenir les plans de capacité à court et à long terme qui favorisent le flux des patients.
Établissement et gestion des relations avec les intervenants
Établir des relations de confiance avec les fournisseurs de services de santé, les partenaires provinciaux et régionaux et les équipes internes afin d'harmoniser les priorités et de faire progresser les objectifs communs du système.
Fournir des conseils stratégiques et diriger des comités, des groupes de travail et des discussions avec les intervenants concernant l'accès, le flux et l'amélioration du système.
Gestion et réalisation de projets
Diriger des initiatives complexes et de grande envergure tout au long du cycle de vie des projets, en établissant des plans de travail, des jalons, les risques, la gouvernance et les outils de réalisation.
Coordonner les ressources internes et externes, harmoniser les processus de planification et communiquer les progrès aux partenaires et aux dirigeants principaux.
Gestion des enjeux et des intervenants
Anticiper et résoudre les enjeux complexes, élaborer des solutions pratiques et faciliter l'harmonisation entre les partenaires et les intervenants.
Cerner les possibilités de partenariat qui font progresser les priorités et les initiatives de Santé Ontario Toronto.
Ce dont vous aurez besoin pour réussir :
Formation et expérience
Diplôme universitaire en administration de la santé, en soins de santé, en administration des affaires ou dans un domaine connexe; une maîtrise est privilégiée. Une combinaison équivalente de formation et d'expérience sera prise en considération.
Au moins cinq années d'expérience dans un milieu de soins de santé.
Expérience en analyse de données, assortie d'un solide sens des finances.
Excellentes compétences informatiques, notamment dans l'utilisation de Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint et SharePoint.
Capacité démontrée à établir, à renforcer et à maintenir des relations stratégiques avec les cliniciens, les gouvernements locaux et provincial, les fournisseurs de services de santé et d'autres intervenants clés, ainsi qu'à travailler efficacement au sein d'équipes diversifiées.
Connaissances et compétences
Solide compréhension du système de soins de santé et du continuum de soins, notamment des processus cliniques, de l'accès et du flux à l'échelle régionale ainsi que de leurs interactions avec les intervenants du système.
Bonne connaissance des ressources communautaires, notamment des services et des programmes; des rôles des professionnels de la santé; des milieux et des politiques hospitaliers; ainsi que des priorités, des enjeux et de l'évolution actuelle du système de soins de santé de l'Ontario.

Health system planning and improvement

This is a unique opportunity to influence system-wide change by applying a provincial perspective to complex clinical quality challenges and helping remove barriers that enable meaningful improvements at the point of care.
This is an exciting opportunity to address complex healthcare challenges from a system-wide perspective, influence frontline change, and support the ongoing success of Ontario Health's Quality Improvement Plan (QIP) program.
Here is what you will be doing:
Supports Quality Improvement Programs
Working in partnership with internal and external stakeholders, develops, implements and evaluates strategies to facilitate the large scale spread of provincial programs designed to promote quality and to reduce clinical variation and inequities
Develops dissemination and implementation strategies to support the use of data (such as quality indicators, MyPractice reports, performance measures, etc.), the adoption and synthesis of evidence (such as Quality Standards and clinical guidelines), and the use of QI methodology to change clinical practice at the frontline

Ensures timely response to concerns arising from a large and diverse audience

Establishes trust and builds strong internal and external relationships with partners and key stakeholders to remain current on local priorities, emerging issues, and trends
Supports committees and working groups comprised of both internal and external stakeholders
Works collaboratively across Ontario Health portfolios, including the regions, and with system partners
Builds QI Capacity and Knowledge
Demonstrates subject matter expertise on priority issues such as: integrated care delivery models, public and patient engagement, improving patient and caregiver experience, coordinated care management, transitions in care, access to care, health care equity, and other clinical priority areas
Drives an understanding of relevant indicators needed for areas of focus with colleagues and stakeholders
Recommends relevant indicators in consultation within OH and external partners
In consultation with senior analyst, designs mixed methods analysis, incorporating into reports
Leads learning collaboratives and communities of practice to drive improvement in priority areas
Understands how to navigate multiple BI platforms and health system performance reporting products (e.g., Quality Standards eReports, Quality Based Procedures, Power BI dashboards)
Able to synthesize reporting outputs with evidence reviews to identify improvement opportunities and support the design, prioritization, and evaluation of QI initiatives
Shares resources and tools to support adoption of QI methodologies in the field

Excellent knowledge and understanding of Ontario’s health system and health policy issues, priorities and enablers and barriers to improving quality of care
Experience engaging clinicians, front line staff, patients and caregivers in design and delivery of clinical care
Skilled in use of textual and qualitative analysis
Skilled in use of common surveys for outreach and outputs such as Survey Monkey, Survey Gizmo

Excellent oral and written communication skills

Chief Communications and Corporate Affairs Officer
Ontario Health is implementing one of the most significant health system transformations in Canada. Created in 2019 to connect and coordinate care across the province, the agency unites world-class expertise in clinical care, digital health, quality, and system planning. Guided by its values of
Integrity, Inspiration, Tenacity, Humility, and Care
, Ontario Health works with partners across hospitals, community services, mental health, home care, and more to deliver better health outcomes and experiences for every Ontarian.
To confidentially explore this opportunity, please email your resume, quoting the appropriate position title, to Judy Mandelman or Heather Spiegel, at
resumes@promeus.ca.
The Position
Ontario Health is seeking an accomplished, astute, and highly strategic executive to serve as its next Chief Communications and Corporate Affairs Officer. Reporting to the President and CEO and serving as a member of the Senior Leadership Team, the Chief Communications and Corporate Affairs Officer will provide enterprise leadership for Ontario Health communications, corporate and public affairs, and stakeholder, patient, and family engagement.
This is a highly influential role at the intersection of government, health system transformation, and enterprise leadership. As a trusted advisor to the President and CEO, Board Chair, and senior leaders, the Chief Communications and Corporate Affairs Officer will help shape Ontario Health’s strategic positioning, reputation, and relationships with government and the health system.
A central priority will be maintaining strong relationships with Ministers’ offices, Ministry leadership, and other senior government decision makers. The Chief Communications and Corporate Affairs Officer will bring executive judgment, anticipate emerging issues and sensitivities, and ensure Ontario Health remains closely aligned with government priorities and expectations.
The Chief Communications and Corporate Affairs Officer will also position communications as a driver and enabler of the Ontario Health strategic agenda. Through proactive planning and a clear cadence of communications, they will help ensure Ontario Health has a compelling story to share about its priorities, progress, and impact, both within the organization and with external stakeholders. The Communications and Corporate Affairs portfolio includes internal and external communications, media and issues management, digital communications, brand and reputation, and stakeholder, patient, and family engagement.
This is not simply a communications leadership role. It is an enterprise role for an executive who can navigate complexity, influence at the highest levels, and help advance Ontario Health’s mandate across government and the health system.
The Person
The ideal candidate is an accomplished senior executive with significant leadership experience in communications, corporate affairs, or public affairs within government, the broader public sector, health care, or another complex and highly visible environment.
They bring deep experience working with elected officials and their teams, senior public servants, Boards, CEOs, and executive teams. They are recognized for sound judgment, discretion, and the ability to anticipate issues, navigate complex government environments, and build trust with senior decision makers.
An exceptional communicator and relationship builder, they can translate complex issues into compelling messages, build trust across diverse stakeholders, and operate effectively within a Crown agency environment. They combine strategic thinking with sound judgment and pragmatism and bring breadth and versatility to contribute beyond the traditional boundaries of a communications portfolio.

Directeur général des communications et des affaires internes
Santé Ontario met en œuvre l'une des transformations les plus importantes du système de santé au Canada. Créée en 2019 pour connecter et coordonner les soins dans toute la province, l'agence réunit une expertise de classe mondiale en soins cliniques, en santé numérique, en qualité et en planification du système. Guidée par ses valeurs que sont
l'intégrité, l'inspiration, la ténacité, l'humilité et la bienveillance
, Santé Ontario collabore avec des partenaires issus des hôpitaux, des services communautaires, de la santé mentale, des soins à domicile et d'autres secteurs afin d'améliorer les résultats et les expériences en matière de santé pour chaque Ontarien.
Afin d'explorer cette opportunité en toute confidentialité, veuillez envoyer votre CV par courriel, en indiquant le titre du poste approprié, à Judy Mandelman ou Heather Spiegel, à l'adresse
resumes@promeus.ca.
La position
Santé Ontario recherche un cadre expérimenté, avisé et doté d'un sens aigu de la stratégie pour occuper le poste de Directeur général des communications et des affaires internes. Rattaché(e) au Président-Directeur général et membre de l'équipe de direction, le Directeur général des communications et des affaires internes assurera la direction stratégique des activités de Santé Ontario en matière de communication, d'affaires internes et d'affaires publiques, ainsi que de l'engagement des intervenants, des patients et de leurs familles.
Il s'agit d'un poste très influent, à la croisée des domaines de l'action publique, de la transformation du système de santé et de la direction stratégique des activités. En tant que conseiller de confiance du Président-directeur général, du président du conseil d’administration et des hauts dirigeants, le Directeur général des communications et des affaires internes contribuera à définir le positionnement stratégique de Santé Ontario, sa réputation et ses relations avec le gouvernement et le système de santé.
L'une des principales priorités consistera à entretenir des relations solides avec les cabinets des ministres, les responsables des ministères et les autres hauts responsables gouvernementaux. Le Directeur général des communications et des affaires internes fera preuve d'un jugement de haut niveau, anticipera les enjeux émergents et les sujets sensibles, et veillera à ce que Santé Ontario reste en parfaite adéquation avec les priorités et les attentes du gouvernement.
Le Directeur général des communications et des affaires internes aura également pour mission de faire de la communication un moteur et un catalyseur du programme stratégique de Santé Ontario. Grâce à une planification proactive et à un rythme de communication bien défini, il contribuera à faire en sorte que Santé Ontario dispose d'un message convaincant à transmettre concernant ses priorités, ses progrès et son impact, tant au sein de l'organisation qu'auprès des intervenants externes. Le portefeuille du Directeur général des communications et des affaires internes comprend les communications internes et externes, les relations avec les médias et la gestion des enjeux, les communications numériques, la marque et la réputation, ainsi que l'engagement des intervenants, des patients et des familles.
Il ne s'agit pas simplement d'un poste de direction dans le domaine de la communication. Il s'agit d'un poste de direction destiné à un cadre supérieur capable de gérer la complexité, d'exercer une influence au plus haut niveau et de contribuer à faire progresser la mission de Santé Ontario au sein du gouvernement et du système de santé.
La personne
Le candidat idéal est un cadre supérieur chevronné, doté d'une solide expérience en matière de direction dans les domaines de la communication, des affaires internes ou des affaires publiques, acquise au sein du gouvernement, du secteur public au sens large, du secteur de la santé ou dans tout autre environnement complexe et très exposé aux regards du public.
Il possède une grande expérience de la collaboration avec les élus et leurs équipes, les hauts fonctionnaires, les conseils d'administration, les PDG et les équipes de direction. Il est reconnu pour son bon jugement, sa discrétion et sa capacité à anticiper les problèmes, à évoluer dans des environnements administratifs complexes et à instaurer un climat de confiance avec les hauts responsables.
Doté d'un talent exceptionnel pour la communication et la création de liens, il est capable de traduire des enjeux complexes en messages convaincants, d'instaurer un climat de confiance entre des intervenants divers et de travailler efficacement au sein d'un organisme public. Il allie réflexion stratégique, bon sens et pragmatisme, et apporte une vision large et une grande polyvalence qui lui permettent d'aller au-delà des limites traditionnelles d'un portefeuille de communication.
