Reporting to the Manager, Investigations, the Investigator leads fair, thorough and timely investigations into complaints involving Ontario health sector organizations. Managing both individual and systemic matters, the role develops investigation plans, gathers and analyzes evidence, conducts interviews and inspections, and prepares clear, objective reports with well-reasoned findings and recommendations.
Here is what you will be doing:
Investigations
Manage a varied caseload of sensitive, high-profile and time-critical individual and systemic investigations, balancing timeliness, fairness and attention to detail.
Assess complaints and case files, identify key issues and risks, and develop proportionate investigation plans, methodologies and lines of inquiry.
Gather, review and analyze relevant records and evidence; plan and conduct interviews, site visits and inspections with complainants, witnesses and health sector organization staff.
Identify barriers to effective investigations, recommend practical solutions, and consult with the Manager and colleagues on strategy, resolution and escalation.
Share investigative expertise through file reviews, quality-improvement activities and support to Early Resolution Specialists.
Analysis and Report Writing
Evaluate evidence and relevant legal or regulatory considerations to develop impartial findings, recommendations and next steps.
Maintain complete, accurate and objective investigation records in the case management system.
Prepare clear, persuasive and accessible reports and correspondence that present the facts, analysis and evidence-based conclusions.
Communication
Use active listening, sound judgment and advanced interviewing skills to obtain relevant information and navigate sensitive or emotionally charged situations.
Communicate clearly, respectfully and professionally with complainants, health sector organizations, witnesses and other stakeholders across written, virtual, telephone and in-person channels.
Collaborate with the Patient Ombudsman team, provide timely case updates, flag emerging challenges and seek guidance as needed.
Compliance
Conduct work in accordance with applicable legislation, including the
Excellent Care for All Act
,
Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act
,
Ontario Human Rights Code
,
Health Care Consent Act
and
Occupational Health and Safety Act
, as well as Patient Ombudsman policies and procedures.
Other Activities
Protect personal and personal health information and maintain strict confidentiality.

Ontario Health is implementing one of the most significant health system transformations in Canada. Created in 2019 to connect and coordinate care across the province, the agency unites world-class expertise in clinical care, digital health, quality, and system planning. Guided by its values of
Integrity, Inspiration, Tenacity, Humility, and Care
, Ontario Health works with partners across hospitals, community services, mental health, home care, and more to deliver better health outcomes and experiences for every Ontarian.
To confidentially explore this opportunity, please email your resume, quoting the appropriate position title, to Judy Mandelman or Heather Spiegel, at
resumes@promeus.ca.
The Position
Reporting to the President and Chief Executive Officer, the Chief Regional Officer (CRO) for the Toronto and East Regions leads one of Ontario Health’s most complex and diverse portfolios. This region spans major urban academic centres and regional hospitals to small rural providers, as well as a diverse network of community-based services. The CRO is a visible and trusted system leader, accountable for translating provincial priorities into action, advancing regional integration, and ensuring consistent, high-quality, and measurable results across a challenging and dynamic environment.
Internally, the CRO will work closely with Ontario Health’s senior leadership team to align people, resources, and strategy, building team cohesion, strengthening operational capacity, and fostering a culture of collaboration and high performance. Externally, the CRO will represent Ontario Health with health service providers, Ministry officials, community leaders, and political stakeholders, cultivating trust-based relationships and navigating complex issues with clarity and integrity.
The CRO will provide credible, solution-focused leadership to help providers navigate workforce shortages, financial pressures, and infrastructure challenges while maintaining alignment with provincial standards. They will strengthen integration and planning across sectors, using data, relationships, and funding levers to improve access, continuity, and efficiency of care. Accountable for delivering on provincial performance targets that directly affect patient care and system sustainability, the CRO will monitor progress, act on emerging issues, and ensure measurable results. In a politically complex environment, they will build strong, respectful relationships with a wide range of stakeholders, addressing sensitive matters with diplomacy and transparency. At the same time, they will lead long-term system transformation, ensuring that immediate operational successes lay the foundation for a forward-looking vision of regional health system improvement.
This is an exceptional opportunity to shape system performance and integration in a region that reflects the full diversity of Ontario’s health landscape. The incoming CRO will guide the regions through ongoing operational pressures, while keeping a clear focus on long-term transformation and equity.
The Person
The ideal candidate is an accomplished health system leader with senior-level experience in health care service delivery, operational and financial administration, performance management, and/or data analytics. Adept at navigating complex, multi-stakeholder environments, they bring strong political acumen and a proven ability to work effectively with government, service providers, boards, and community stakeholders. They possess deep knowledge of Ontario’s health sector, including funding models, policy directions, and transformation priorities, and are skilled at turning strategic vision into measurable results. A collaborative and values-driven leader, they build trust, foster alignment, and inspire teams toward shared goals. Resilient and grounded, they demonstrate sound judgment, thrive in complexity, and remain focused on improving care and equity for the people and communities of Ontario.
To confidentially explore this opportunity, please email your resume, quoting the appropriate position title, to Judy Mandelman or Heather Spiegel, at
resumes@promeus.ca.

Directeur général régional de Toronto et de l'Est
Santé Ontario met en œuvre l'une des transformations les plus importantes du système de santé au Canada. Créée en 2019 pour connecter et coordonner les soins dans toute la province, l'agence réunit une expertise de classe mondiale en soins cliniques, en santé numérique, en qualité et en planification du système. Guidée par ses valeurs que sont
l'intégrité, l'inspiration, la ténacité, l'humilité et la bienveillance
, Santé Ontario collabore avec des partenaires issus des hôpitaux, des services communautaires, de la santé mentale, des soins à domicile et d'autres secteurs afin d'améliorer les résultats et les expériences en matière de santé pour chaque Ontarien.
Afin d'explorer cette opportunité en toute confidentialité, veuillez envoyer votre CV par courriel, en indiquant le titre du poste approprié, à Judy Mandelman ou Heather Spiegel, à l'adresse
resumes@promeus.ca.
La position
Relevant du président-directeur général, le directeur général régional (DGR) des régions de Toronto et de l'Est dirige l'un des portefeuilles les plus complexes et diversifiés de Santé Ontario. Cette région englobe aussi bien de grands centres universitaires urbains et des hôpitaux régionaux que de petits fournisseurs en milieu rural, ainsi qu'un réseau diversifié de services communautaires. Le DGR est un responsable reconnu et de confiance du système, chargé de traduire les priorités provinciales en actions, de faire progresser l'intégration régionale et de garantir des résultats cohérents, de haute qualité et mesurables dans un environnement difficile et dynamique.
En interne, le DGR travaillera en étroite collaboration avec l'équipe de haute direction de Santé Ontario afin d'harmoniser les personnes, les ressources et la stratégie, de renforcer la cohésion de l'équipe et la capacité opérationnelle et de favoriser une culture de collaboration et de haute performance. En externe, le DGR représente Santé Ontario auprès des fournisseurs de services de santé, des représentants du ministère, des dirigeants communautaires et des intervenants politiques, en cultivant des relations fondées sur la confiance et en abordant des questions complexes avec clarté et intégrité.
Le DGR assure une direction crédible et axée sur les solutions afin d'aider les fournisseurs à faire face aux pénuries de main-d'œuvre, aux pressions financières et aux défis liés aux infrastructures, tout en maintenant la conformité aux normes provinciales. Il renforcera l'intégration et la planification entre les secteurs, en utilisant les données, les relations et les leviers de financement afin d'améliorer l'accès, la continuité et l'efficacité des soins. Responsable de la réalisation des objectifs de performance provinciaux qui influent directement sur les soins aux patients et la viabilité du système, le DGR suit les progrès accomplis, prend des mesures pour régler les problèmes émergents et veille à l'obtention de résultats mesurables. Dans un environnement politiquement complexe, il établit des relations solides et respectueuses avec un large éventail d'intervenants, tout en abordant les questions sensibles avec diplomatie et transparence. Parallèlement, il coordonne la transformation à long terme du système, en veillant à ce que les succès opérationnels immédiats jettent les bases d'une vision prospective de l'amélioration du système de santé régional.
Il s'agit d'une occasion exceptionnelle de façonner la performance et l'intégration du système dans une région qui reflète toute la diversité du paysage de la santé en Ontario. Le nouveau DGR guidera les régions face aux pressions opérationnelles continues, tout en maintenant clairement le cap sur la transformation à long terme et l'équité.
La personne
Le candidat idéal est un responsable accompli du système de santé possédant une expérience de haut niveau dans la fourniture de services de soins de santé, l'administration opérationnelle et financière, la gestion du rendement et/ou l'analyse des données. Apte à évoluer dans des environnements complexes impliquant de multiples intervenants, il fait preuve d'un sens politique aigu et d'une capacité avérée à travailler efficacement avec les pouvoirs publics, les fournisseurs de services, les conseils d'administration et les intervenants communautaires. Il possède une connaissance approfondie du secteur de la santé de l'Ontario, notamment des modèles de financement, des orientations politiques et des priorités de transformation. Il est également capable de transformer la vision stratégique en résultats mesurables. En tant que responsable collaboratif et axé sur les valeurs, il instaure la confiance, favorise la coordination et motive les équipes à atteindre des objectifs communs. Résilient et pragmatique, il fait preuve d'un bon jugement, s'épanouit dans les situations complexes et reste concentré sur l'amélioration des soins et de l'équité pour la population et les communautés de l'Ontario.

Participate in making thorough recommendations as to appropriate proceedings, considering potential defenses, and prepare evidence briefs that support the recommendation.
Work collaboratively with the litigator on the preparation for court or hearings (disclosures, witnesses, hearing briefs and settlement discussions) and testify as a fact witness.

We are looking for someone who is committed to working to protect investors and foster confidence in our capital markets, and who is naturally curious.  Experience with data analytics, open source intelligence gathering, and law enforcement or intelligence agency investigation techniques are assets as is experience and knowledge of our capital markets.  More particularly, we would prefer to see a candidate with:
Completion of an undergraduate degree in Business, Finance, Accounting, Criminology, Computer Science, or other STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering or Math) degree.
Minimum of 5 years of investigative experience specializing in financial investigations, fraud investigations, money laundering, proceeds of crime, and/or computer evidence analysis.
Law enforcement experience specializing in financial investigations, fraud investigations, money laundering, proceeds of crime, and/or computer evidence analysis.
Previous experience in an intelligence gathering role and/or formal training on intelligence extraction.
Strong understanding and knowledge of the capital markets industry, trading products, and role of participants as well as administrative and criminal justice systems, and securities legislation.
Strong understanding of emerging crypto currencies, crypto assets, crypto platforms, and current social media.
Strong project management and problem-solving skills with the ability to demonstrate professional skepticism, resourcefulness, and good business judgment.
Excellent communication skills with the ability to actively listen, probe, and interpret information, including in examining witnesses, and to present information orally and in writing coherently and concisely.
Excellent interpersonal skills and a demonstrated collaborative and results-oriented style in working effectively both within a team structure and independently, while delivering on expectations in a dynamic environment.
Superior team-based skills necessary to collaborate, inspire and demonstrate a service excellence mindset within the team and other OSC staff.
Completion of the Canadian Securities Course and/or other related industry courses is an asset.
Strong understanding of emerging crypto currencies, crypto assets, crypto platforms, and social media is an asset.

is passionate about making a difference and having a meaningful impact on investors and participants in Ontario’s capital markets,
desires the opportunity to investigate challenging issues and work on high profile and complex cases and,

title: Senior Law Clerk
description:
Business Unit
Regular, Full time
Closing Date: October 9, 2026
The Ontario Securities Commission (OSC) is the statutory body responsible for regulating Ontario’s capital markets in accordance with the mandate established in the provincial Securities Act and the Commodity Futures Act. The mandate of the OSC is to provide protection to investors from unfair, improper or fraudulent practices, to foster fair, efficient and competitive capital markets and confidence in the capital markets, to foster capital formation, and to contribute to the stability of the financial system and the reduction of systemic risk. This mandate is performed through policy, operational, and enforcement activities. The OSC also contributes to national and global securities regulation development.
We offer a diverse, fair, and flexible work environment and take pride in our challenging and rewarding work.
The
Enforcement Division
of the Ontario Securities Commission delivers fair, vigorous, and timely enforcement responses to capital markets misconduct. The Enforcement Division investigates and prosecutes breaches of securities laws in Ontario.  Team members work closely with other securities regulators, self-regulatory organizations and law-enforcement agencies to enhance initiatives to fight misconduct.  A strong visible enforcement presence assists in protecting investors from unfair, improper or fraudulent practices, fosters fair, efficient and competitive capital markets, fosters capital formation, and contributes to the stability of the financial system and the reduction of systemic risk.
The
Criminal Investigations and Prosecutions
team is recruiting for a
Senior Law Clerk.
What’s in it for you?
Be an integral part of a leading-edge team leveraging an innovative mix of traditional investigative techniques, data analytics, and open-source intelligence analysis to investigate and assist in the prosecution of complex cases of Securities Act and Criminal Code offences.
Work in a collaborative, progressive, and professionally diverse team.
Make a difference and have a meaningful impact on investors and participants in Ontario’s capital markets.
What will you do?
The Senior Law Clerk provides senior-level law clerk support to investigators, litigation counsel and prosecutors on complex investigations and proceedings. The Senior Law Clerk also takes on leadership responsibilities within the law clerk group, identifies and establishes best practices, coaches and trains colleagues, and assists with onboarding.
·                Provide law clerk support throughout complex investigations and proceedings involving alleged breaches of Ontario securities law and related criminal offences.
·                Research, locate, retrieve, review and organize civil and criminal files, records, evidence and other materials, identifying key documents and potential privilege or confidentiality issues for review by investigators and counsel.
·                Assemble documentary evidence from multiple sources, including interview transcripts, and prepare control indexes, evidence summaries, chronologies, schedules and draft or revised documents.
·                Assist with the preparation of search warrants, Informations to Obtain, production orders, affidavits, orders and directions, and maintain files and track summonses, orders and responses.
·                Work with investigation teams to prepare, review and submit requests for assistance to other securities regulators in Canada and internationally.
·                Prepare and manage documentary briefs for disclosure and use in evidence, including organizing electronic disclosure, preparing indexes, arranging affidavits of service, eliminating duplicates and completing required redactions.
·                Support litigation counsel and prosecutors with motions, hearings, trials, sentencing proceedings, appeals and post-hearing or post-trial work, including preparing, serving and filing court and tribunal materials.
·                Review transcripts and witness summaries, identify discrepancies, update charts and schedules, prepare hearing and trial materials, and ensure evidence and exhibits are assembled, available and maintained.
·                Attend hearings and trials to manage exhibits, hearing databases and proceeding logs, and testify when required.
·                Liaise with witnesses, opposing counsel, court and tribunal staff, court reporters, regulators and law enforcement partners, and support scheduling and information exchange.
·                Manage file-closing activities to ensure files are indexed, organized and stored in accordance with Enforcement Division requirements.
·                Lead and support the law clerk group by identifying opportunities to improve practices, convening meetings, sharing developments, coaching and mentoring colleagues, and assisting with the onboarding and training of litigation counsel, prosecutors, law clerks and articling students.
What do you need to be successful in this role?
·                Completion of a two-year Law Clerk program at a community college.
·                Membership in good standing with the Institute of Law Clerks of Ontario, or eligibility for ordinary membership.
·                At least 10 years of experience with a law office, government agency or other organization performing administrative or managerial law clerk functions under the guidance of a lawyer, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
·                Experience supporting complex investigations, regulatory proceedings, criminal or provincial offences prosecutions, appeals, judicial review applications or other court proceedings.
·                Knowledge of standard eDiscovery software and experience organizing electronic evidence, disclosure and hearing or trial materials.
·                Knowledge of the Securities Act (Ontario), the Commodity Futures Act (Ontario), the Criminal Code and related legislation, together with knowledge of the securities regulatory environment preferred.
·                General knowledge of the Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms, access-to-information and privacy legislation, the Provincial Offences Act, federal and Ontario business corporations legislation, bankruptcy and insolvency legislation, evidence legislation, and the Statutory Powers Procedure Act preferred.
·                Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, sound judgment, and a high level of accuracy and attention to detail.
·                Excellent organizational, tracking, prioritization and workload-management skills, with the ability to meet strict deadlines while managing multiple files and responsibilities.
·                Well-developed proofreading, legal drafting, writing and administrative skills.
·                A proactive and self-motivated approach to workload management and professional development.
·                Demonstrated ability to lead, coach and guide less-experienced staff by providing regular, clear direction and constructive feedback.
·                Excellent interpersonal and team-based skills, with the ability to collaborate, coach, mentor and demonstrate a service-excellence mindset within a professionally diverse team.
If you are the type of person who:
·                Is passionate about making a difference and having a meaningful impact on investors and participants in Ontario’s capital markets;
·                Desires the opportunity to support challenging investigations and work on high-profile and complex cases; and
·                Enjoys being part of a dynamic and flexible work environment with a collaborative, progressive, and professionally diverse team.

title: Practicum Student
employer: Public Health Ontario (Ontario Agency for Health Protection and Promotion)
description:
Practicum Student
Location: Toronto-661 University
Department: IPAC Physicians, Third Party Grants
This posting is to fill a current vacancy.
The Role:
Audit and feedback (A&F) interventions are widely used to improve antibiotic prescribing in primary care and are a key strategy in antimicrobial stewardship. Randomized trials and systematic reviews have shown that A&F can reduce inappropriate prescribing; however, the magnitude of effect varies substantially across studies.
This variability likely reflects differences in how A&F interventions are designed and delivered. A set of predefined components for A&F has been proposed based on prior evidence and expert consensus, covering aspects such as feedback content, delivery, and targeting (1). Despite this, there is limited empirical evidence on which specific components are most strongly associated with intervention effectiveness.
Understanding the contribution of individual components is essential for optimizing A&F design and improving impact. A meta-epidemiological approach allows examination of whether the presence of specific components across trials is associated with variation in effect sizes.
This study aims to systematically synthesize evidence from trials of A&F interventions for antibiotic prescribing and to assess the association between predefined intervention components and observed outcomes. The student will join a team and take the lead for this study using systematic review methodology using an AI tool.
Please note:
•	this position is only open to students who are currently enrolled in an academic program where the completion of a practicum placement is required.
•	this position is only open to students currently residing in Ontario and attending a Canadian academic institution. Preference will be given to students enrolled in Ontario-based academic institutions.
•	this is a paid placement.
Suggested placement start & end date: January to April 2027
Educational objectives
:
1.     Gain knowledge about AMR and interventions to improve antibiotic prescribing.
2.     Gain knowledge in systematic review methodology including screening and extraction of study data.
3.     Gain experience using an AI tool supporting systematic review work.
4.     Gain experience performing data analysis and manuscript writing.
Proposed deliverables at the end of the placement:
·         Participate in screening and extracting data.
·         Support the analysis of data.
·         Assist in drafting of a manuscript.
·         Presentation of findings.
Required education and experience:
·         Currently enrolled in an MPH program.
·         Experience with systematic reviews and data analysis in R is an asset.

Infrastructure Ontario’s AME-CI team delivers essential public‑sector infrastructure across the province, including new construction, major rehabilitation, demolition, and other asset‑related initiatives. Our made‑in‑Ontario approach to modern project delivery has positioned the province as a global leader by consistently delivering projects on time and on budget while upholding high standards for design excellence, quality, and health and safety.
The Project Manager plays a central role in advancing capital projects through planning, procurement, and implementation. This includes leading scope, schedule and budget management, stakeholder engagement, risk mitigation and coordinated delivery across a diverse program of work.

:
Lead complex infrastructure projects through all phases of development and delivery, including planning, RFQ/RFP processes, design, construction, commissioning, and transition to operations.
Manage the planning, design, and construction of large and complex projects delivered through traditional direct‑delivery models (e.g., stipulated sum, construction management) and/or in an oversight capacity for projects delivered through Project Management Services Providers (PMSPs).
Lead and manage the project administration processes for external consultant(s), contractors, and PMSPs and specialty vendors. This includes financial management of contracts, negotiations, dispute resolution, and/or interpretation and terms of agreement(s) on behalf of the organization.

Build and maintain strong relationships with internal and external stakeholders to identify and mitigate project risks, resolve issues, and ensure alignment with project objectives.

Experience and education in a discipline related to infrastructure planning, design, or construction (e.g., Construction Management, Architecture, Engineering, Landscape Architecture or related fields).

Lead and be accountable for Cost Control activities and deliverables across assigned capital projects, performing the work directly on some projects and overseeing Specialists and consultants supporting delivery on others.

Facilitate the change control process throughout the project lifecycle, including the identification, assessment, tracking and reporting of approved and potential changes and their impact on project forecasts and contingency.

Collaborate with Finance, Budgeting and other stakeholders to align project Cost Control information and reporting with financial, budgeting and organizational requirements.

Job Purpose
The Manager, Building Maintenance & Operations (“Manager”) is responsible for the first‑line management of the building, and provides coordination and planning throughout the Law Society. This includes the planning, implementation and monitoring of safe and efficient services related to mechanical and electrical maintenance and operations and overseeing various service contracts.
The Manager is also accountable for the effective management of employees to facilitate responsive support services to employees across the organization. This includes managing the day-to-day work order management, janitorial services, move management, and ergonomic requests.
Qualifications
The minimum level of education required is a post-secondary university and/or college diploma or equivalent, with courses in general mechanical and electrical services, health and safety, fire and building codes.
Professional Engineer, LEED AP, and/or IFMA designations with facilities management experience implementing / managing BOMA certification program(s) is desirable.
As the Manager is expected to provide hands‑on management, the incumbent is required to have a minimum of 7 years of broad experience with a strong mechanical aptitude and experience, with at least 2 years of supervisory experience in a customer service-oriented environment.
Function Related Skills, Knowledge and Abilities
Thorough knowledge of mechanical systems and its associated distribution including, but not limited to, low pressure steam (ENWAVE) and circulating hot water heating systems and forced air heating and cooling systems, their maintenance and operation.
Thorough knowledge of electrical systems and its associated distribution including high voltage sub stations, electrical rooms with associated equipment, etc.
Thorough knowledge of plumbing systems and its associated distribution including sewage sump pits, boilers, tanks, etc.
Thorough knowledge of fire alarm systems and its associated distribution including F/A panels, sprinkler systems, heat/smoke detectors, etc.
Proven mechanical ability in assessing and scheduling repairs and service calls for various equipment.
Ability to read floor plans and technical drawings (i.e., riser diagrams, schematics, details, etc.) along with excellent reading and writing skills.
Thorough knowledge of construction/building materials and their usages.
Working knowledge of industry standards and safety guidelines, WHMIS, OHS Act, AODA, Building Codes, Fire Codes, Electrical Codes.
Good computer skills, experience in the use of Microsoft Word, Excel, and G Suite (Gmail, Calendar, etc.).
Sustainability: Identify and implement initiatives, cost savings, energy reduction and efficiencies with current and new equipment, systems, operations, etc.
Working knowledge of a Computer Maintenance Management System (Asset Essentials)
Working knowledge of Building Automation Systems (Automated Logic).
Speaks and writes in a clear, articulate manner for individual and/or group situations.
Valid driver’s license is desirable.
Technical Skills and Knowledge
Familiarity with various software applications, including word processing, spreadsheets and computer assistance drawing programs, e‑mail and the Intranet/Internet.
Key Accountabilities
Client / Customer Service Planning
Plans and coordinates the service delivery of the Building Maintenance and Operations team to ensure the safe, clean, and efficient operation of mechanical, electrical, plumbing, pneumatic and electronic systems.
Collects, monitors, and evaluates utility and waste consumption data to help implement opportunities for operational cost savings, reduce utility consumption, and improve operational efficiencies of building engineering systems.
Implements and manages a nationally recognized facility operations certification program to help continuously track and assess building operational efficiency, improve sustainability practices, reduce overall environmental footprint, and lower carbon generation.
Evaluates the required maintenance or operational work to be completed within the building and based on the impacted variables (building operations, department operations, costs/budget, time/scheduling, and physical site constraints/logistics), strategically develops a plan which minimizes negative impacts to LSO operations, while considering costs.
Evaluates the health and safety risks (dust, odours, noise, fire, flood, etc.) associated with proposed maintenance work, and details the appropriate health and safety measures to ensure both regulatory compliance while addressing any work specific concerns.
Oversees various service contracts, including but not limited to, groundskeeping, waste management, office cleaning, office shredding, graffiti removal, elevator maintenance, building automation system maintenance, emergency power testing and maintenance, grease trap removal, backflow prevention inspections, fire safety systems, washroom and hygiene products.
In collaboration with the Director, Facilities and Planning and department representatives, assesses the impact of programs related to mechanical and electrical systems, staffing, maintenance projects, budgets, supplies, and legal issues, recommending courses of action.
Plans for potential utility outages and troubleshoots to determine faults, and initiate repairs of infrastructure systems.
Coordinates and supervises preventative and proactive maintenance and repairs of systems.
Receives requests for services from staff throughout the building, assessing feasibility and prioritizing maintenance requests, liaising with clients to ensure that needed support is provided in a timely and efficient manner.
Completes work requests, either directing employees, and/or coordinating with external contractors.
Prepares Requests for Proposals, interviews, and decides on successful contractors, seeking input and approval from the Director for major contracts.
Client / Customer Service Delivery
Actively contributes to the secure and safe maintenance, repair and replacement of mechanical and electrical systems.
Responds to employee, member and builder users’ related issues and concerns.
Monitors contracts and service contractors for compliance with scope, timeline, budget and quality control, and effectiveness of service delivery.
Establishes relationships with service providers to maintain service level agreements beneficial to the Law Society.
Identifies and implements initiatives for cost savings, energy reduction and improved efficiencies with current and new equipment, systems, and operations, with a commitment to sustainability.
Performs daily monitoring and checks, anticipating deadlines and seasonal requirements.
Monitors and maintains inventories of supplies, including required purchasing.
Keeps accurate and timely logs and schedules.
Ensures all services meet relevant codes and standards, including health and safety, WHMIS, and regular inspections, such as fire monitoring and sprinkler systems.
Maintains current knowledge and expertise in the area of mechanical services, ensuring a proactive approach to service delivery.
Resolves escalated issues related to consultant, supplier, and/or service contracts.
People Leadership
Hires, develops, and assesses performance of team members in accordance with the policies of the organization and best human resources practices.
Fosters a team environment by clarifying team goals, valuing team input, building team member commitment, strengthening the team’s collective skills and encouraging creativity and problem solving.
Provides input into departmental issues resolution, vision, and communication strategy.
Ensures career development of direct reports by coaching, training and/or mentoring; conducts performance reviews for direct reports within the department.
Supervises day-to-day activities of team performing technical work and ensures quality standards and procedures are followed and met.
Provides direction and checks the quality of contractors’ and service providers’ work, negotiating contracts and ensuring cost‑effectiveness and conformance with legal requirements.
Financial Responsibility
Oversees the preparation of contract services, quotations from external vendors, and manages team through the execution of each contract.
Tracks and reports on utility and contract services expenditures, negotiates contracts with clients and vendors, to ensure cost effective utilization of resources.
Responsible for annual expenditure, revenues, and contract negotiations related to external building maintenance service providers.
Analyzes budget needs and contributes to the development of the Maintenance and Operations budget process, including forecasts for materials purchases and replacements, services and staffing.
Monitors the appropriate budget, taking corrective action on variances.
Receives requests for supplies and equipment, conducting purchases within approved budget and guidelines, meeting cost‑effectiveness requirements, and ensuring adequate stock of inventories.
Provides support to the Director and assists in budgeting and budget monitoring.
Team Membership
In conjunction with the Director and other team members, contributes to the proactive planning of immediate and longer term departmental, opportunities and initiatives, and works with the team to implement cost-effective, user-friendly solutions.
Coordinates and communicates with the immediate team, employees, internal and external clients, consultant, vendors, and contractors throughout planning and execution of maintenance work.

title: Director, Enterprise Planning and Performance (Permanent)
location: 130 Queen St W, Toronto, ON M5H 2N5, Canada
description:
Overview
At Law Society of Ontario we believe in the importance of a collaborative and supportive work environment that provides high quality and professional service to the public, lawyers and paralegals, and other stakeholders.
We are always on the lookout for exceptional individuals who are ready to make a meaningful impact, innovate and grow with us.  Our offering:
We value each member of our team and invest in your professional learning and development.
We provide access to the resources needed to support professional growth, mental health and well-being is a priority.
Our competitive compensation package includes a defined contribution pension plan, health and dental benefits plan and a robust Employee and Family Assistance Plan (EFAP).
Our progressive employment policies, high levels of employee engagement and the impressive architecture and beautiful grounds of the historic Osgoode Hall, there are many reasons to work at the Law Society.
We hope you will consider joining the Law Society!
Job Purpose
The Director, Enterprise Planning & Performance will build and manage a small professional team and is charged with strengthening enterprise-wide planning, performance measurement, and transparent reporting on delivery of the Law Society’s Strategic Plan. Reporting to the Executive Director, Strategy, the Director supports the CEO, Executive Committee and Convocation by establishing practical planning rhythms, enterprise-level key performance indicators (KPIs), and disciplined reporting that demonstrates progress against approved strategic objectives in a manner that is clear, transparent and measurable.
The Director works in partnership with operational areas across the organization as well as Business Innovation and Operations Management (BIOM), Information Technology (IT) and Finance as an enterprise integrator, helping to connect priorities, surface interdependencies, and support coordinated execution of the Strategic Plan. Working through influence, the Director helps ensure that planning and reporting processes are coherent, proportionate and supportive of effective delivery.
Key Accountabilities:
1. Enterprise Planning & Performance Framework (Planning)
Under the guidance of the Executive Director, Strategy, the Director provides leadership and expertise to the CEO, Executive Committee, and Convocation to achieve the Law Society’s objectives with respect to enterprise planning, execution discipline, and performance accountability. Establishes and maintains enterprise planning cycles, templates and routines that translate approved strategic priorities into clear initiatives, milestones and measurable outcomes. Supports enterprise prioritization, sequencing and trade-off decisions across initiatives and resources.
2. Enterprise Planning & Accountability Reporting (Delivery)
Coordinates the development, implementation, monitoring and reporting of enterprise-level performance measures and progress against the Strategic Plan, supporting the CEO’s and Executive Committee’s accountability to the Board through clear and measurable reporting. Defines reporting standards to ensure that Strategic Plan accountability is evidence-based, reliable, and consistent over time.
Works in partnership with leaders and teams across the organization as an enterprise integrator to coordinate cross-functional inputs into KPI dashboards, progress updates, and briefing materials that reflect organizational outcomes achieved, delivery risks, mitigation actions, dependencies, and overall confidence in execution of the Strategic Plan. This includes but is not limited to coordination with Policy, Professional Development & Competence, Professional Regulation, Finance, Business Innovation & Operations Management, Information Technology, Communications and others.
3. People Leadership
This senior position supports the Executive Director in ensuring that deliverables will be appropriately operationalized, and that day-to-day mentoring and direction are provided.
Hires, trains, develops and evaluates employees accountable to the Director in accordance with organizational policies and best human resources practices. Fosters a team environment by role modeling leadership behaviour, empowering employees accountable to the Director and building team capability.
4. Financial Responsibility
Assists the Executive Director with developing and monitoring the team’s budget and project-related expenditures, adjusting plans as required to meet fiscal resource constraints.
5. Team Membership
Able to work collaboratively in supporting the CEO, the Executive Committee, and senior leaders, ensuring consistency in enterprise planning and performance reporting across the organization. Works with various internal stakeholders and cross-functional teams, providing leadership and expertise to team members, ensuring broad information and idea exchange.
The Director demonstrates personal excellence, bringing knowledge and functional expertise to the team. Contributes to group decision-making and processes, generating ideas that are strategically sound, integrated with the Law Society’s broader mandate, and achievable in a timely, balanced and fiscally sound manner.
6. Relationship and Alliance Building
Builds credibility and develops effective working relationships with key groups both internally and externally. Partners with operational leaders to support coordination without undermining operational authority. Works closely with Professional Development & Competence and Professional Regulation divisions to understand the core functions of the organization. Where appropriate, supports strategic relationships and shared learning with other regulatory bodies or sector partners on planning, performance measurement and modernization approaches.
Qualifications
Education
The minimum level of education required to fulfill the core requirements of this position includes a university degree in Business Administration, Public Administration, Public Policy, Law or a related field. An equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered.
Experience
The position requires a minimum of 10 years’ progressive related experience gained in a complex, multi-stakeholder environment such as a government, regulatory or complex not-for-profit environment, at least 5 of which are in a managerial / leadership capacity.
Function Related Skills, Knowledge and Abilities
Comprehensive understanding of enterprise planning, performance measurement and reporting in a complex organization, including governance and accountability expectations.
Demonstrated ability to translate strategic priorities into measurable outcomes, performance indicators, and practical reporting products.
Proven ability to synthesize complex information quickly and communicate it clearly in concise, well-written reports and briefings.
Strong facilitation and relationship management skills; ability to influence without authority and coordinate across functions.
Experience working in highly political situations, managing a variety of viewpoints and sensitivities.
Political astuteness and sound judgment to calibrate intervention—staying light-touch where work is on track and increasing support where delivery is at risk.
Capability to lead, develop and manage a team of professionals, including the conducting of annual team member performance reviews.
Demonstrated ability to assess organizational capability and adjust plans as required to successfully carry out organizational strategies.
Demonstrated ability to manage multiple agendas, meet changing deadlines, and deliver on a large number of concurrent commitments.
Superior analytical and communication skills coupled with excellent interpersonal and negotiation skills.
Technical Skills and Knowledge
Computer literacy, including familiarity with email, word processing, spreadsheets, databases and dashboards.
Ability to partner effectively with BIOM/IT on data definitions, reporting automation and CRM-enabled insights.

Make a difference
The Contract Administrator is responsible for managing the full post-award lifecycle of procurement contracts, from contract setup through amendments, renewals, extensions, and close-out. The role ensures contracts are accurately established, maintained, and administered within the Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM) system, in compliance with organizational policies, approvals, and governance requirements.
Working closely with Legal, Finance, SPU colleagues, Divisions, Vendors, Vendor Relationship Management (VRM), and the Data, Analytics & Technology team, the Contract Administrator ensures contract records are complete, compliant, and support effective vendor performance oversight and reporting.

Contract Execution & Administration (60%)
Review award documentation to confirm contract type, scope, value, and contractual dates prior to initiating contract setup and storage in the CLM system.
Select the correct contract workflow (new contract, amendment, renewal, or extension) and validate that all required approvals are in place before processing.

Close out contracts by confirming completion of deliverables with Divisions, attaching final documentation, and archiving contract records in accordance with internal procedures.

Work closely with Legal to review proposed contract changes, confirm contractual clauses, and resolve non-standard terms as required.
Communicate with Divisions to verify deliverables, service timelines, performance expectations, and updates throughout the contract lifecycle.
Follow up with Vendors to obtain missing compliance documentation or to clarify discrepancies in submitted materials.
Collaborate with Vendor Relationship Management (VRM) to share contract compliance results for integration into vendor performance reporting and scorecards.
Partner with Sourcing Specialists to take over awarded contracts following negotiations and confirm final contract details for setup.
Oversight, Risk & Continuous Improvement (15%)
Apply established naming conventions, version control standards, and contract checklists to ensure consistency, auditability, and compliance across all contract records.
Use contract reporting provided by the Data, Analytics & Technology team (e.g., upcoming expirations, incomplete records, amendment volumes) to identify required follow-ups and confirm next steps with stakeholders.
Monitor system alerts related to key contract milestones and proactively notify responsible teams to support timely action.
Escalate recurring delays, compliance gaps, or system-related issues to the Supervisor and contribute recommendations for workflow, process, or template enhancements to improve efficiency and controls.

The Supervisor, Contract Management oversees the day to day execution of post award contract activities, including contract setup, amendments, renewals, extensions, and closeout. This position serves as the escalation point for complex post award contract issues and works closely with Legal, Finance, Strategic Procurement (SPU), Vendor Relationship Management, Centre of Excellence, and Divisions to resolve documentation gaps, conflicting terms, terminations, and other contract risks. The role supports reporting, compliance, and continuous improvement of contract administration processes and controls.

Identify and address escalated issues such as missing or conflicting contract terms, incomplete documentation, termination or early‑exit requirements, and other post‑award risks, coordinating resolution with Legal and relevant stakeholders prior to workflow progression.
Supervise and validate that CLM contract records, including key milestones, vendor deliverables, renewal triggers, and contract metadata, are accurate, complete, and maintained in compliance with policy.
Team Leadership & Workflow Coordination (30%):
Assign and monitor daily workload of Contract Administrators to ensure adherence to timelines, workflow requirements, and documentation quality standards.
Review complex or high‑risk contract files to confirm accuracy and completeness prior to record activation or advancement within the CLM system.
Provide day to day guidance to team members on standard processes, escalating  non‑standard or high risk scenarios, or ambiguous contract inputs to Supervisor / Sr Mgr Contract Management as appropriate.
Stakeholder & Cross‑Functional Collaboration (20%):

Collaborate with Vendor Relationship Management to validate vendor compliance inputs during renewals, extensions, performance issues, or other escalations requiring compliance confirmation.
Support   alignment between CLM processes, legal templates, and standard contract terms, including updates to documentation requirements and workflow routing.
Participate in cross‑functional discussions, including with the Centre of Excellence, to improve integration between sourcing decisions, contract administration, tools, workflows, and reporting.

Monitor recurring contract issues, service and quality trends, and reporting dashboards to identify process gaps and control improvement opportunities.
Validate the quality and completeness of CLM contract records and supporting documentation submitted by the team.
Support testing, implementation, and rollout of CLM enhancements or upgrades in collaboration with the Data, Analytics & Technology team and other stakeholders.
Recommend improvements to contract workflows, approval checkpoints, and controls based on lessons learned and trend analysis.

5–7 years of progressive experience in contract management, procurement, or a related field
Experience overseeing post‑award contract administration activities, including contract setup, amendments, renewals, extensions, and closeout.
Experience supervising staff and coordinating workflows with defined quality and documentation standards.
Experience working with a Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM) system, including maintaining contract metadata, milestones, and deliverable tracking.

Reporting to the Senior Director, Community Safety Unit, the Manager, CSWB Implementation and Project Management provides disciplined implementation, project-management and coordination leadership for Toronto Community Housing’s Community Safety and Well-Being (CSWB) Strategy. The position translates the Board-approved Strategy into sequenced workplans, coordinates place-based pilots and Community Safety and Well-Being Plans, supports integrated service tables, and ensures that commitments, risks, dependencies and implementation learning are tracked and acted upon.
The position works across CSU, Regional Operations and other TCHC divisions, as well as with tenants and external partners. It provides implementation governance and project discipline but does not exercise daily operational command, direct front-line deployment, independent quality assurance or corporate analytical ownership.
What you’ll do
CSWB Strategy Implementation and Portfolio Management
Translates the Board-approved CSWB Strategy and annual priorities into a multi-year implementation roadmap and detailed annual workplans.
Maintains the master implementation plan across the five CSWB outcome areas, including deliverables, milestones, accountable owners, dependencies and timelines.
Establishes and maintains a portfolio view of major CSU and cross-divisional projects to support prioritization, sequencing and management oversight.
Develops project charters, governance structures, work breakdowns, schedules, decision logs, risk and issue registers, and project-closure documentation.
Monitors implementation progress, tests the reliability of status updates and identifies delays, scope changes, unresolved decisions and capacity constraints.
Escalates material barriers and recommends practical corrective action, re-sequencing, resource adjustments or governance decisions.
Promotes consistent project-management methods while tailoring the level of documentation and control to the size, risk and complexity of each initiative.
Ensures implementation reflects TCHC’s strategic priorities, tenant-centred service commitments, equity obligations and approved CSWB principles.
Place-Based Pilots and Community Safety Planning
Leads the project management of East, Central and West CSWB pilots and any approved expansion to additional communities.
Coordinates development, implementation and periodic review of place-based Community Safety and Well-Being Plans.
Integrates operational information, tenant experience, community conditions, environmental findings, partner capacity and available analytical evidence into practical action plans.
Ensures each pilot or plan includes clearly defined outcomes, actions, owners, timelines, resources, measures and review points.
Maintains pilot-specific action, risk, issue and decision logs and ensures overdue or unresolved matters are addressed through the appropriate escalation route.
Documents implementation learning, identifies transferable practices and recommends adjustments to the operating model before broader expansion.
Develops and applies readiness, need, sustainability and capacity criteria when recommending whether and how CSWB planning should expand.
Integrated Service Coordination, Partnerships and Tenant Input
Establishes and supports integrated working tables for complex community safety and well-being priorities requiring coordinated action.
Coordinates participation from CSU, Regional Operations, Facilities, Tenancy Management, Programs and Partnerships, Communications and other relevant TCHC functions.
Supports structured involvement of external partners, including community organizations, health and social services, violence-prevention partners, emergency services and other public institutions.
Ensures meetings result in documented decisions, assigned actions, clear deadlines and appropriate follow-through rather than information-sharing alone.
Coordinates with corporate and regional engagement leads so that tenant priorities and lived experience inform local plans and implementation decisions.
Tracks commitments arising from tenant and partner engagement and supports timely communication back to tenants on progress and constraints.
Maintains role clarity between project coordination and the operational delivery responsibilities of Special Constables, Community Safety Advisors, investigators and other service teams.
Implementation Frameworks, Governance and Reporting
Designs and maintains implementation frameworks for cross-functional priorities, including the CSU call follow-up model and other approved service improvements.
Defines governance requirements, accountabilities, service expectations, escalation paths and closure criteria in consultation with functional owners.
Prepares concise implementation dashboards, status reports, briefing notes, presentations and decision materials for the Senior Director and senior management.
Supports preparation of ELT, Committee and Board reports by providing validated implementation status, risks, milestones, lessons and next steps.
Works with Research, Analytics and Performance to align implementation milestones with appropriate performance measures, baselines and evaluation plans.
Works with Records and Quality Assurance to ensure implementation controls, records and compliance requirements are incorporated into project design.
Maintains complete, accurate and accessible project records in accordance with TCHC records-management, privacy and information-security requirements.
Functional Leadership, Resource Stewardship and Continuous Improvement
Provides functional leadership and direction to employees, consultants, working groups and project teams assigned to CSWB implementation initiatives.

Make a difference
The Workplace Investigator is responsible for investigating allegations of employee misconduct, workplace harassment, discrimination, reprisal, violence, policy breaches, and other workplace concerns in accordance with TCHC policies, applicable collective agreements, legislation, and workplace investigation best practices. As part of the Employee and Labour Relations Team within People & Culture, the position conducts threshold assessments, develops investigation plans and terms of reference, identifies the scope and mandate of investigations, conducts fair and respectful interviews, gathers and assesses relevant evidence, analyzes applicable policy, collective agreement and legislative requirements, makes findings of fact on an objective and evidence-based basis, and prepares clear, thorough, neutral and well-supported investigation reports. The role carries out investigations in a timely, impartial, procedurally fair, confidential, trauma-informed and culturally responsive manner, applying an equity, anti-Black racism and human rights lens while maintaining neutrality and avoiding assumptions, bias or prejudgment.
What you’ll do
Investigation Intake, Planning and Execution
Supports and conducts assigned components of the workplace investigation process from complaint intake to conclusion, including triage, threshold assessment, scoping, investigation planning, interviews, evidence gathering, analysis, credibility assessment, findings and reporting for complex workplace issues, including harassment, discrimination, reprisal, inappropriate conduct, workplace violence and other alleged misconduct or breaches of TCHC policies, collective agreements or legislation. Applies a demonstrated understanding of anti-Black racism throughout the process, recognizing that it may be explicit or subtle and may arise through individual conduct, racial stereotypes, organizational culture, institutional practices, differential application of policies, or patterns of cumulative disadvantage.
Conducts research into assigned areas ensuring that such research takes into account developments within the field, corporate policies and practices, legislation and initiatives by other levels of government.
Investigates complex allegations of workplace misconduct or wrongdoing for unionized and non-unionized staff across the organization, including fraud, conflict of interest, theft, maladministration, harassment, discrimination, reprisal, nepotism, cronyism, substance-related concerns, unethical behaviour, workplace violence, breaches of workplace standards and other conduct concerns. Ensures allegations are reviewed and analyzed through a fair, neutral, timely, evidence-based and policy-grounded process, with attention to fact-finding, procedural fairness and detail.
Equity, Human Rights and Culturally Responsive Practice
Applies distinctions-based and culturally safe investigation approaches that respect First Nations, Métis and Inuit peoples by avoiding pan-Indigenous assumptions and supporting participant-led cultural or community supports where requested and appropriate.
Applies procedural fairness equitably rather than mechanically, recognizing that impartiality does not always require identical treatment of every participant. Identifies and appropriately addresses relevant barriers, accessibility requirements, cultural considerations, racialized power imbalances and participation needs while maintaining a neutral, confidential and evidence-based investigative mandate.
Exercises essential investigative skills, including critical thinking, active listening, trauma-informed interviewing, credibility assessment, data and document analysis, rigorous research methods, and effective time management to ensure investigations are thorough, impartial, unbiased, timely, well documented and capable of withstanding internal, arbitral, tribunal or court scrutiny.
Conducts credibility and reliability assessments without relying on racialized assumptions or stereotypes concerning demeanor, communication style, emotional expression, accent, tone, confidence, perceived professionalism, authority, cooperation or trustworthiness. Assesses testimony within the full factual, cultural, organizational and power context, while relying on relevant and probative evidence.
Applies trauma-informed, anti-racist, anti-oppressive, culturally responsive and human rights-informed approaches throughout workplace investigations, recognizing that participants may have different lived experiences, communication needs, accessibility needs, trauma histories or emotional responses, while maintaining investigator neutrality, procedural fairness and an evidence-based mandate.
Uses effective communication, accommodation-aware practices, psychological safety tools and respectful interview techniques to engage with persons of diverse identities, abilities, backgrounds and experiences, including individuals who may be distressed, distrustful, guarded, or have heightened emotional responses because of the alleged incident, disability, trauma, prior experience of discrimination, institutional distrust or systemic barriers.
Evidence Assessment, Reporting and Records
Conducts on-site and or virtual interviews and gathers evidence at various work locations.

Ensures records are consistently labelled, securely maintained, readily retrievable, and managed in accordance with TCHC record-keeping practices, confidentiality requirements, privacy obligations and litigation or adjudicative needs.
Assesses the evidence, applies credibility analysis where required, and makes findings of fact based on the balance of probabilities, the applicable factual record, and relevant policies, procedures, collective agreement provisions or legislation. Prepares detailed reports, confidential communications and briefings that clearly distinguish facts, evidence, analysis, findings and any applicable policy conclusions.
Develops investigation plans, terms of reference, interview plans, evidence lists, findings reports and related communications with input from the Manager, Employee and Labour Relations, as appropriate, to ensure the investigation process is consistent, fair, well scoped, legally defensible, confidential and aligned with TCHC standards.
Stakeholder Communication and Proceedings
Works collaboratively with internal partners, management, union representatives where applicable, law enforcement agencies and legal counsel to exchange information on a need-to-know basis, preserve confidentiality, support procedural fairness, and ensure investigation-related communications are accurate, respectful and appropriately documented.

Develops and delivers education, guidance and training on workplace investigation policies, procedures and best practices, including procedural fairness, confidentiality, trauma-informed interviewing, anti-racist and anti-oppressive practice, documentation standards, evidence handling, neutrality and the role of participants in the investigation process.
Models and contributes to an environment that supports equity, inclusion, dignity, respect, psychological safety and organizational change. Provides subject matter expertise and consultation to management and employees on rights, responsibilities, roles and expectations within the investigation process, while reinforcing procedural fairness, neutrality and confidentiality.
Maintains and applies advanced working knowledge of human rights, anti-racism and equity principles relevant to workplace investigations, including individual, interpersonal, systemic and institutional dimensions of anti-Black racism; racial stereotyping and coded language; intersectional discrimination; racial harassment; reprisal; accommodation; accessibility; anti-Indigenous racism; gender identity and expression; disability-related considerations; cultural responsiveness; and the effects of power imbalances, racial trauma and lived experience on participation and evidence.

Lead by the Director of the Retail Payments Supervision portfolio, you will join a dynamic and highly skilled team working together to design, develop, and support our regulatory IT platform built on the Power Platform.
Further, you will have the full support of your leader and teammates to enhance your skills, experiment, and further your career through our customizable Learning & Development programs across various domains (IT, Programming, Architecture, Analytics, etc.) and relevant certifications.
What you will do
As a Developer, you will be responsible for developing new features and maintaining existing components for the Bank’s RPS regulatory IT platform using the Microsoft technology stack, comprised of Power Pages (Portal), Model Driven Apps, Custom PCF controls, SharePoint, Power Automate Flows, Azure services (Function Apps, APIM) and multiple system integrations.
More specifically, you will:
Contribute to the development of the Power Platform application and peripheral technologies
Analyze, design and implement enhancements to meet business requirements
Maintain collaborative relationships with internal clients and external counterparts
Perform technical and root-cause analysis on issues and make recommendations for correction
Create working procedures and documentation on solutions and populate knowledge databases, testing plans and results
Apply a continuous improvement mindset, by identifying innovative ways of doing or providing services to our clients; changing or reconfiguring approaches to improve efficiency and capacity

Experience developing within Dynamics 365 and Power Platform or other CRM systems
Experience building custom APIs and Plug-ins
Proven experience with C# programming language and .NET Framework
Proven experience with web portal development in a Microsoft or equivalent environment
Experience developing and maintaining HTML5, CSS, JavaScript web portal applications
Experience working with business analysts or user experience (UX) designers to creatively translate business requirements and designs into interactive web portal functionality

Experience in writing programming scripts using PowerShell

Join the Securitization Operations team, in the Specialist, Analytics and Reporting role. Compute and report on securities guaranteed/guarantees in force, mortgage arrears and other securitization performance measures for quarterly and annual financial statements.

Comprehensive and advanced knowledge of conceptual and transactional elements of securitization funding models.
Broad-ranging knowledge of capital markets instruments, securitization markets, regulatory issues, accounting and disclosure standards, and trends in funding and risk management practices.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills and ability to model and assess financial risks.
Oral and written communication skills including presentation skills.
Techniques for the measurement and understanding of financial and operational risk as well as performance.
An ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships.
A demonstrated ability working in a sophisticated technological environment, using such tools as spreadsheets, PowerBI, Bloomberg, etc.

A post-graduate degree(s) in business, finance, economics or related fields and/or professional designations attesting specialty in the areas of finance and risk management (for example, CFA, FRM).
A Knowledge of R or Python.

À propos du rôle
Joignez-vous l'équipe des opérations de titrisation, au poste de Spécialiste, analytique et rapports. Vous serez chargé de concevoir et d’analyser les mesures de rendement pour les programmes de titrisation de la SCHL et d’en faire rapport. Vous devrez de plus appuyer les activités de titrisation de la SCHL en surveillant le Programme des Obligations hypothécaires du Canada (OHC), pour aider la SCHL à remplir son rôle de conseiller en services financiers (CSF) auprès de la Fiducie du Canada pour l’habitation (FCH). Vous vous occuperez de l’établissement du prix des titres hypothécaires émis en vertu de la Loi nationale sur l’habitation (TH LNH) ainsi que de la vérification des prix et participe à diverses activités liées à chaque émission d’OHC.
Ce que vous ferez:
calculer les titres cautionnés, les cautionnements en vigueur, les prêts hypothécaires en souffrance et d’autres mesures de rendement des activités de titrisation et en faire rapport pour les états financiers trimestriels et annuels;
examiner les demandes d’attribution de TH LNH présentées par les émetteurs et procéder, s’il y a lieu, à des attributions ou réattributions trimestrielles de TH LNH;
établir et tenir à jour des modèles et une infrastructure pour appuyer la tarification et les évaluations, les analyses et les rapports liés aux activités commerciales, le Plan d’entreprise, la tarification des titres et l’indemnité d’écart de taux;
préparer les rapports mensuels et trimestriels sur les activités de titrisation de la SCHL qui sont présentés à la haute direction, la publication des rapports de la Société (notamment le supplément d’information sur les activités de titrisation) et divers rapports à l’intention des organismes de réglementation (ministère des Finances, Banque du Canada et Bureau du surintendant des institutions financières);
contribuer à l’exécution des opérations pour le Programme des OHC en s’assurant du respect des délais, de l’exactitude et de l’exhaustivité;
préparer et présenter une courbe d’évaluation quotidienne des prix des TH LNH vendus à la FCH;
surveiller la conformité des activités de titrisation aux exigences du Programme des OHC, aux contrôles et aux niveaux de tolérance au risque de la SCHL.
Les compétences que vous devriez posséder:
un diplôme universitaire (1er Cycle) dans un domaine connexe, par exemple en administration des affaires, en finance ou en économie et un minimum de cinq années d’expérience pertinente en sécurisation;
une connaissance vaste et approfondie des éléments conceptuels et opérationnels des modèles de financement de la titrisation;
une vaste connaissance des instruments des marchés financiers, des marchés de titrisation, des enjeux réglementaires, des normes comptables et de présentation de l’information ainsi que des tendances des pratiques en matière de financement et de gestion des risques;
d’excellentes aptitudes d’analyse et de résolution de problèmes et capacité de modéliser et d’évaluer les risques financiers;
des aptitudes pour la communication orale et écrite et pour la présentation d’exposés;
une connaissance des techniques permettant de mesurer et de comprendre les risques financiers et opérationnels ainsi que les résultats;
une capacité d’établir et d’entretenir des relations de travail efficaces;
une capacité confirmée de travail dans un environnement technologique de pointe, en utilisant des outils comme les tableurs, PowerBI et Bloomberg.
Ce serait formidable que vous possédiez aussi ces compétences:
un diplôme universitaire de deuxième ou troisième cycle en administration des affaires, en finance, en économie ou dans un domaine connexe ou titre professionnel témoignant d’une spécialisation en finance et en gestion des risques (par exemple, CFA, FRM);

Ce que vous ferez :
répondre aux demandes des prêteurs relatives aux produits, politiques, processus et outils d’assurance prêt hypothécaire pour immeubles collectifs, en assurant un service professionnel, exact et opportun, tout en favorisant l’établissement de relations durables avec la clientèle;

analyser les tendances relatives aux demandes de renseignements, la qualité des dossiers soumis et les commentaires des clients afin de cerner les problèmes récurrents et de recommander des améliorations aux processus ou des initiatives de formation;
appuyer l’élaboration et la diffusion d’initiatives de formation, ce qui comprend l’animation de présentations et de webinaires dynamiques et la production de matériel d’information à l’intention de la clientèle;
collaborer avec l’équipe Développement des affaires (DA) – Immeubles collectifs, pour assurer l’harmonisation, le partage des connaissances et le soutien coordonné axé sur les relations avec les clients;

Les compétences que vous devriez posséder :
un diplôme de premier cycle dans un domaine pertinent comme l’administration des affaires, les finances, l’économie ou le commerce, ou une combinaison équivalente d’études et d’expérience;
au moins cinq années d’expérience dans le secteur des services financiers, de préférence dans des postes de première ligne ou de développement des affaires;
de bonne connaissance des pratiques de prêt hypothécaire ainsi que des produits d’assurance prêt hypothécaire de la SCHL, notamment ceux applicables aux immeubles collectifs résidentiels;
un fort sens du service à la clientèle et de la gestion des relations d’affaires, avec une aptitude démontrée à gérer les demandes de renseignements de façon efficace, professionnelle et judicieuse;
d'excellentes aptitudes pour la communication orale et écrite dans les deux langues officielles (anglais et français);
des excellentes aptitudes organisationnelles, avec la capacité de gérer simultanément plusieurs priorités et délais dans un environnement dynamique et en constante évolution;
un expérience démontrée en résolution de problèmes, sens de l’initiative et capacité à analyser l’information afin de générer des renseignements exploitables;
une capacité démontrée à collaborer efficacement avec des intervenants internes et externes.
Ce serait formidable que vous possédiez aussi ces compétences :
de l'expérience en assurance prêt hypothécaire (APH) pour immeubles collectifs, notamment en ce qui concerne les produits, les outils et les exigences relatives aux demandes;
l'expérience du soutien ou de la prestation d’initiatives de formation, y compris des présentations et du matériel d’information à l’intention de la clientèle;

About the role
Join our Securitization team, in the Manager, Securitization Operations position. In this role, you will lead the operational execution and governance of key activities supporting the NHA MBS (National Housing Act Mortgage-Backed Securities) Program, including pool creation, readiness for validation, guarantee processes and ongoing operational management.  You will ensure effective risk and compliance governance at the operational level, including monitoring, reporting and resolution of loan errors as well as operational incidents, while supporting the Senior Manager on complex risk assessments and escalations.  In this role, you will prioritize system enhancements and operational improvements while maintaining effective governance documentation and processes. You will also lead a team of professionals, aligning resources and activities to achieve business objectives, drive continuous improvement, and support a high-performing, engaged workforce.
What you'll do:
Lead and coordinate day-to-day securitization operational activities, ensuring effective execution of pooling and validation readiness processes.
Monitor operational performance, identify opportunities for improvement, and ensure compliance with established processes, service standards, and regulatory requirements.
Resolve critical pooling errors and operational issues, escalating complex matters as required.
Identify, assess, and address risks related to MBS pooling process, including risks related to non-compliant pools, loans, and documentation.
Maintain and support risk governance activities, including incident management, reporting, audits, regulatory reviews, and adherence to policies and risk frameworks.
Act as an MBS (Mortgage-Backed security) business lead in Securitization POD, prioritizing system maintenance, incident resolution, and business-driven enhancements.
Support the delivery of system improvements and operational initiatives while maintaining governance documentation, procedures, controls, and continuity protocols.
Lead, develop, and engage a high-performing team by setting objectives, managing resources, fostering accountability, and building organizational capability.
Support operational excellence through strong team performance, employee engagement, effective stewardship of resources, and the promotion of an inclusive and bilingual workplace.
What you should have:
An undergraduate degree in business, finance, economics or a related field.
A minimum seven years of relevant experience, including some supervisory or team leadership experience.  An equivalent combination or education and experience will be considered.
An excellent knowledge of financial systems, mortgage securitization and NHA MBS program (National Housing Act Mortgage-Backed Securities Program).
A solid understanding of regulatory requirements (e.g., OSFI).
A strong knowledge of operational processes, risk management, compliance, and governance practices.
An experience supporting process improvements, operational excellence, and business systems initiatives.
Proven analytical, reporting, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to identify issues and drive effective solutions.
Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and deliver results in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment.
It would be great if you also had:
Experience working within an AGILE / POD delivery model.
Certifications (e.g., CFA, FRM, project management).
