title: Director, Legal Services
description:
CreateTO
is shaping Toronto’s future through impactful real estate solutions. A City of Toronto agency, CreateTO works collaboratively with internal stakeholders, external partners and community members to create more livable, sustainable and inclusive communities. CreateTO is here to increase the social, cultural and economic value of our city’s $27-billion real estate portfolio, ensuring positive impacts for residents and a bright future for Toronto.
We are looking for a lawyer who understands the business and strategic objectives behind a transaction, can identify and manage risk while minimizing project delays, and can provide clear, practical advice to senior leaders and project teams. If you’re passionate about contributing to the best use of one of North America’s largest and most valuable real estate portfolios, we’d love to have you on the team.
THE OPPORTUNITY
The Director, Legal Services supports the Associate General Counsels and Chief Legal Counsel in resolving legal issues, ensuring legal compliance and mitigating risks. The role includes:
Supporting the legal aspects of the assigned portfolio of projects and corporate functions.
Providing advice on legal implications related to CreateTO’s projects.
Maintaining an awareness of legal and regulatory matters relevant to achieve CreateTO’s broad business and policy objectives.
Advising project leads on all legal matters affecting CreateTO’s projects and business arrangements to support operational decision-making.
PRINCIPAL FUNCTIONAL RESPONSIBILITIES
Maintaining a deep understanding of CreateTO’s business and industry and providing leadership in operational business decisions from a legal perspective.
Leading the drafting and negotiating of complex real estate and leasing transactions, including acquisitions, dispositions, leases, licences, easements, rights-of-way, development agreements, reciprocal rights and operating agreements, and other property-related arrangements.
Providing strategic legal advice on lease structuring, property/asset management, development rights, environmental matters, litigation and other landlord and tenant issues.
Advising on transaction structures involving public and private-sector partners, joint ventures, development partners and other stakeholders.
Providing legal advice throughout the development lifecycle, from early feasibility and structuring through approvals, financing, construction, project delivery and long-term operations.
Providing legal advice on construction and capital projects, including construction agreements (e.g. CCDC and OAA), consultant agreements, low carbon and sustainability initiatives, procurement, project delivery, insurance, contractor/consultant performance, change orders, claims, disputes, litigation and other construction related matters.
Conducting due diligence on real estate and commercial leasing transactions, including title searches and corporate searches.
Navigating legal and regulatory challenges to achieve CreateTO’s broad business and policy objectives.
Providing direction and supervision to external counsel, including with respect to litigation, arbitrations, mediations and expropriations.
CANDIDATE ATTRIBUTES
An experienced lawyer with 7+ years of broad real estate, commercial leasing, development and construction experience that meets the above requirements, and the ability to lead cross-divisional teams to resolve legal issues.
Ideally will have had exposure to public and private sector real estate interests and land use planning, as well as gained corporate governance experience and board experience.
Aptitude for detail, with a high level of accuracy and superior legal drafting skills.
Exceptional organizational skills are necessary to coordinate a variety of responsibilities, in an often-changing environment, to achieve stated goals and objectives.
Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to exercise good judgment, tact and discretion.
Ability to work with highly confidential information with both maturity and professionalism.
A high degree of competence in verbal and written communication.
Ability to solve problems and take the initiative.
TOTAL COMPENSATION
The salary range for this position is $128,270 to $192,910 annually, with the expected range for this role to start between $150,000 to $160,000 commensurate with qualifications and experience.
In addition to base salary, CreateTO offers a comprehensive total compensation package including participation in the OMERS defined benefit pension plan, competitive vacation entitlement, extended health and dental benefits, life and disability insurance, and access to employee wellness support including an Employee and Family Assistance Program (EFAP).
With a highly engaged team, CreateTO scores well above benchmarked organizations in terms of its employees’ passion, commitment, diversity and pride. As part of the organization’s Strategic Plan 2023-2027, “Inspire internal success” was named as one of five priority objectives.
CreateTO wants its team to reflect the city we represent, and we strive to provide an inclusive workplace that promotes and values diversity in age, gender identity, race, sexual orientation, physical or mental ability, ethnicity, and perspective, all of which are proven to build better companies. Our goal is to create an environment where everyone, from any background, can do their best work and be themselves.
We provide equitable treatment and accommodation to ensure barrier-free employment in accordance with the Ontario Human Rights Code and Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act. Candidates can request accommodation related to the protected grounds at any stage of the hiring process.

Legal Counsel
description:
WHY WORK AT HCRA:
We foster a professional home building industry that Ontarians can trust.
The Home Construction Regulatory Authority (HCRA) is a not-for-profit corporation that is designated by the provincial government of Ontario to administer and enforce the New Home Construction Licensing Act, 2017 and associated regulations. HCRA holds licensed builders to professional standards, protects the public interest, and enhances consumer confidence in the homebuilding industry in Ontario. In addition, HCRA strives to educate consumers to ensure that they can make informed decisions and understand the benefits of a regulated homebuilding sector. As one of Ontario’s newest regulators, HCRA is dedicated to providing the highest level of service to everyone they serve.
HCRA provides a flexible, hybrid and collaborative work environment, with an array of benefits as well as considerable time off allowances. Additionally, as a mid-sized organization, team members have direct exposure to senior management on a regular basis, and they get the opportunity to work on a range of assignments with significant responsibilities. By joining the HCRA, you'll be a part of the establishment of a growing regulator that is passionate, engaged, forward-thinking and innovative.
WHAT THE POSITION IS:
We are seeking a permanent, full-time Legal Counsel as a backfill. As Legal Counsel, you'll provide legal advice and representation with a primary focus on litigation and regulatory enforcement. You'll support HCRA’s enforcement program by assessing inspections and investigations and providing opinions on the viability of prosecutions or other regulatory enforcement actions. Day to day, you'll draft pleadings and motion materials and represent HCRA at the Licence Appeal Tribunal and other legal proceedings. You'll independently manage assigned litigation and enforcement matters while working closely with the Assistant General Counsel and other members of the legal team on complex, high-risk or precedent-setting issues. You'll brief the Assistant General Counsel, the General Counsel, and senior leadership on the status of assigned matters and provide recommendations on hearing strategy and settlement options, escalating significant or unprecedented legal issues as appropriate. Beyond litigation, you'll conduct legal research, advise on legislative and regulatory developments, and provide legal support on a range of operational, governance, licensing, compliance and policy matters across the organization. You'll also contribute legal advice to project teams and support special initiatives involving legislative, regulatory or policy change.
WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE:
Success in this role requires strong litigation experience, whether in civil, criminal, regulatory or professional discipline matters. Your experience should include conducting trials or administrative hearings, drafting related materials, and working with internal stakeholders, opposing counsel and external parties. You'll bring strong research, analytical and problem-solving skills, along with the ability to manage multiple matters and competing priorities effectively. You should be able to identify emerging legal issues, assess their potential impact, and exercise sound judgement in determining when matters require escalation or additional support. You'll thrive in an evolving environment, adapt quickly to changing priorities, and bring strong tact, judgement and diplomacy to your work. Just as important are strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to deliver clear, practical advice to diverse audiences.
Candidates must be called to the Bar of Ontario and be members in good standing with the Law Society of Ontario. We are looking for at least three years of post-call experience, including meaningful experience in civil, criminal, regulatory or professional discipline litigation. Experience conducting trials, administrative hearings, motions, mediations or other contested proceedings is strongly preferred.
Experience with professional regulatory enforcement matters and familiarity with complaints and investigations processes would be an asset.
Experience with administrative authorities and the new home construction sector would be an asset.
Annual Salary Range:
The salary range for this position is between $105,000.00 CAD and $150,000.00 CAD (Depending on qualifications, skills, and experience).

September 6, 2026
.

hr@hcraontario.ca
. For more information about HCRA or to view other career opportunities, please visit
www.hcraontario.ca
.

We are an equal opportunity employer and do not discriminate against employees or qualified applicants on the basis of race, religion, ethnicity, national origin, ancestry, marital or family status, age, gender identity or expression, gender, sexual orientation, disability, or any other characteristic protected by law.

What will I be doing?

What Skills and Qualifications Do I Need?
Completion of
a degree or diploma in construction management, project management, engineering, quantity surveying or a related discipline – or a combination of education, training and experience deemed equivalent.
Demonstrated experience of at least 2 (two) years in
major project commercial and/or claims management; progressive experience in the administration of major construction/infrastructure contracts.
Active membership in PEO, AACE, PMI, CIQS, RICS or similar association
is an asset.
Knowledge and understanding of capital construction methods, practices, contractors’ methods of tendering and contract/subcontract administration, schedule/delay analysis, cost / damage analysis, prolongation costs, acceleration costs and disruption/loss of productivity analysis.
Knowledge of AACE recommended techniques for estimating claims for extension of time/prolongation and loss of productivity. Knowledge of contractor’s estimation practices and construction pricing.
Experience and knowledge of detailed assessment of Contractor’s variations for entitlement and costs impacts in coordinating with the members of the Project Teams including SMEs, for resolving pending and potential variations and claims.
Knowledge of contract administration and project delivery using AFP, P3, or design/build methodology. Good understanding and knowledge of the practical application of contract administration and document management software, CM14, Aconex, ProjectWise, and SharePoint. Excellent written, verbal and presentation communication skills. Proficiency in MS Office (e.g., Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint etc.). Well-developed problem solving and analytical skills, including being highly responsive with the ability to act quickly under changing circumstances and anticipate multiple claim paths and investigate client impacts, to keep ahead of the claimant.

description:

Our Deputy Chief Financial Officer’s (DCFO) Office is looking for multiple Co-op Students to provide support within the various Finance teams. You will work with internal and external stakeholders to support financial analysis, reporting, presentations, systems maintenance, and process improvement initiatives while gaining exposure to a variety of finance functions within a large public sector organization.
We have DCFO Office, Finance co-op roles available in the following areas:
Accounting:
1 vacancy, 8-month term
Embedded Finance:
5 vacancies, 4- or 8-month terms

1 vacancy, 8-month term
Descriptions of each area are provided below:
Accounting:
The Accounting team leads the month end close processes which facilitates the preparation of the quarterly balance sheet and annual financial statements for Senior Management, Board of Directors and our stakeholders such as the Ministry of Transportation and the Province of Ontario. The team activities include supporting the assurance work with external auditors, Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, Diesel Fuel Hedging, General Ledger accounting and analysis, statutory financial reporting ensuring compliance with corporate policies and generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) and tax compliance.
Embedded Finance - Corporate Finance, Payments Finance, and Operations Finance GO/UP:
The Embedded Finance Team works alongside the departments as a trusted business partner and is crucial in advancing the financial strategies, goals and decisions of the departments. Through active involvement, it provides well-informed financial guidance and support to enable the departments to achieve its financial goals and savings initiatives. The teams support operating and capital financial portfolios and financial asset management functions. This includes capital budgeting/forecasting, financial reporting and insights to drive effective business decisions, asset classes on memo development, and capital funding strategy development.
Embedded Finance - Operations GO/UP Capital:
The Capital team plays a key role in supporting the delivery of Operations’ capital infrastructure program. The team provides financial oversight throughout the entire project lifecycle, from project planning and funding approval to budgeting, forecasting, capitalization, and project closeout. As part of the team, you will gain exposure to capital planning, financial analysis, performance reporting, and governance processes that support major transit and infrastructure investments across the organization.
Financial Planning & Analysis:
The FP&A team plays a pivotal role in ensuring that Metrolinx is meeting its financial objectives to deliver its growing programs, while adhering to government policy and legislative requirements. The team provides analytical support to senior management and the Embedded Finance teams to enable effective data-driven decisions. This includes development of Metrolinx’s operating budget, monthly Business Performance Review report, quarterly forecasts, Metrolinx’s public-facing Business Plan as well as the Management Discussion and Analysis section of the Annual Report. The team also manages the Oracle Hyperion application.
What will I be doing?
Support business case financial modeling for various business intake projects and initiatives with a view to monitor and manage costs and inform performance management activities.
Assist with ad hoc deliverables and projects that may involve developing worksheet templates for analyses, updating process documentation/manuals, preparing PowerPoint slides, and working with various cross-functional teams on initiatives.
Help produce daily, weekly, and monthly operational documentation and reports, as assigned.
Support to staff in a variety of areas, including gathering, inputting, organizing, and interpreting data for reports/presentations/meetings/projects, and supporting year-end inventory counts.
Prepare agendas, coordinate, attend, and take minutes for daily technical/operational meetings.
Support gathering audit evidence in the external auditor’s portal.
Maintain and update electronic and hardcopy filing systems and provide records management support.
Recommend improvements to existing processes and procedures to achieve greater efficiency.
Assist with the maintenance, development, monitoring and reporting of tools and systems for data analysis.
Develop spreadsheets, forms, and databases to input, track, store and retrieve data.
Present key findings to team members and management as required.
What will I gain?
Hands-on experience supporting finance, accounting, budgeting, forecasting, and business planning activities.
Exposure to a variety of finance functions, including Accounting, Embedded Finance, Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A), and Capital Finance.
Opportunities to develop financial analysis, data management, problem-solving, and stakeholder engagement skills.
Experience working with financial systems, reporting tools, and large datasets.
Exposure to budgeting, forecasting, financial reporting, audit support, and business performance reporting processes.
Mentorship and guidance from experienced finance professionals.
The opportunity to contribute to projects that support major transit operations and infrastructure investments across the region.

Required
Currently enrolled full-time in a recognized post-secondary co-op program and eligible to complete a co-op work term as part of your academic requirements, with plans to return to school following the work term.
Must be enrolled in Finance, Economics, Accounting, Business, or a related program at a post-secondary institution.
Strong written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel, Word, and PowerPoint.
Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a team environment.
Willingness to learn and gain exposure to various areas of Finance.

Interest in Finance, Accounting, Financial Planning & Analysis, or business partnering.
Progress toward, or interest in pursuing, a CPA or CFA designation.
Experience with Power BI or other reporting and data visualization tools.

French language skills.

title: Senior Contract Administrator
description:

Our Enterprise Commercial Management Office is seeking a Senior Contract Administrator to provide contract planning, management and administration services for large scale, high profile and complex operations, maintenance, and construction projects.
What will I be doing?
Prepares, reviews and administers high profile, large scale and complex contracts (e.g. construction, commercial/supplier, operations, consulting contracts) during various stages of the contract management process, including: working with internal project teams to define scope of project work and project specifications, identifying potential project risks and mitigation strategies to ensure risk mitigation and management, value management and cost control, participating in the preparation of scope for potential procurement/RFP documentation, monitoring contracts to ensure contracts are aligned with procurement /contract management strategies and are complying with the terms and conditions set out in the contractual agreements, and working with the Finance Group to obtain payment approval for invoices.
Reviews, validates and analyses the Division’s requirements, tenders and contract documents and determines/administers sourcing or category strategies to ensure that the overall contracting strategy and individual clauses/terms are applied appropriately and consistently to reduce risk and protect the interests of Metrolinx.
Reviews contract management documentation to ensure required clauses are included and recommends changes/revisions where omissions/inconsistencies occur.
Identifies and advises on the resolution of a range of critical contract issues including contractor performance, and monitors contractor adherence to the terms of contractual agreements.
Enforces contractual obligations and conditions by engaging internal legal representation as well as helping in negotiations and resolution of matters, or enforcement of penalty clauses, Liquidated Damages.
Identify when a risk may become a claim to ensure the compliance of contracts and change orders to minimize corporate liability throughout the lifecycle of the projects.
Contributes expertise and advice to the design, planning, development and implementation of contract management systems, standards and operational procedures, including recommendations to improve/adjust contract management processes.
Liaises with various internal stakeholders (e.g. internal project teams, Procurement, Legal, Finance etc.) with respect to all aspects of contract administration and risks including claims and dispute resolution.
Assists in standardizing and updating wording for terms of reference and supplemental conditions by recommending revised/updated language to ensure consistency in application and interpretation.
Systematically manages contract-related correspondence and documentation and ensures tracking of contract deliverables is proactively managed.

Completion of a degree in Business Administration, Engineering, Contract/Construction Law, or a related discipline or a combination of education, training and experience deemed equivalent.

Knowledge of construction/commercial/operational contract administration and claims management techniques and practices in a large multi project complex construction/commercial and infrastructure environment.
Knowledge of design and construction/commercial programs, standards and processes to provide contract administration/management expertise/advice for large scale, high profile, complex construction/commercial/operational/consulting projects.
Experience with various procurement methods, both traditional and non-traditional (including AFP – Alternate Financing Procurement).
Skilled in the development and communication of internal contract administration policies, procedures and best practices.
Experience in the interpretation of contract law, and Ontario legislation (e.g. Construction Act, Professional Engineers Act, Canadian Construction Documents Committee documents, bespoke contract documents, specifications and drawings, and legal statutes and proceedings) would be an asset.
Excellent oral/written/presentation skills to assist in standardizing and updating wording for terms of reference and supplemental conditions.
Experience in using contract administration systems, such as Primavera Contract Manager and Oracle Unifier.

Role Summary
Our award-winning Legal Services team is seeking a labour, employment, and human rights lawyer to join our busy and collegial legal team, headquartered in downtown Toronto. Ideal candidates will have a strong interest in problem solving, contributing to setting key strategic direction, and partaking in the leadership and strategic development of a busy labour and employment legal team.
Reporting to a Director, Legal Services, the successful candidate will provide proactive, timely and strategic advice to senior business leaders and their teams, including labour and employment issues arising from operating a busy bus and train transit network; complex infrastructure construction projects; issues that may impact upon Metrolinx customers and the general public; and a wide range of human resources-related files arising from long-range planning as well as day-to-day operations.
Metrolinx has both unionized and non-union employees, and the workforce is both office-based and front-line. Our bus and rail operations operate within a highly regulated environment. Our capital programs entail delivery of complex transit infrastructure, sometimes involving consideration of contractor and/or construction-related labour issues. As a safety-critical and safety-centric organization, experience working within or advising within some or all of these contexts (or analogous) would be an asset.
What will I be doing?
Works independently with a wide variety of business units and stakeholders
Provides labour, employment law and human rights legal advice to internal clients, including on litigation or potential litigation
Undertakes and provides advice regarding litigation on behalf of Metrolinx by representing Metrolinx in legal proceedings, including attendance at the Grievance Settlement Board (grievances), Human Rights Tribunal of Ontario (regarding applications brought by both employees and/or customers), in Court (in particular, wrongful dismissals), before the Ontario Labour Relations Board, and/or before other adjudicative or investigatory bodies, including preparing pleadings, written submissions and any other materials needed to undertake litigation files on Metrolinx’s behalf
Provides legal and/or strategic advice regarding negotiations and/or represents Metrolinx in negotiations with individual or commercial claimants, including related to collective bargaining, including preparing correspondence, memoranda and/or other documentation related to negotiations and binding settlements
Directs and manages external counsel on litigation, solicitor-type work, transaction matters and other work, making recommendations, as necessary, to the Labour & Employment lead (Director), Legal Management Team (Directors, VPs, EVPs), Chief Legal Officer and others, including client groups
Provides high-quality and timely legal advice, strategic advice, research, opinions, guidance and service on matters pertaining to labour law, employment law, human rights law and/or other related legal matters
Directs external counsel on litigation, solicitor work and/or transaction matters, and makes recommendations to client groups, portfolio leads and Chief Legal Officer
Drafts and reviews complex contracts, memoranda of understanding and other legal documentation
Works effectively with various agencies, departments and levels of management within and external to the organization, including program managers, business and financial analysts, consultants and executives
Advises and leads presentations to all levels of management, including briefings of Senior Management and Division Heads
Understands how to prioritize tasks, push files forward, handle a busy file load with disparate client groups and issues, and escalates issues appropriately
Provides proactive and strategic legal advice to organization outside of specific legal assignments
Assists with developing training and mentorship programs for junior lawyers and students
Provides feedback and direction to legal clerk and administrative staff
What Skills and Qualifications Do I Need?
Completion of a degree in law (JD or LLB)
Demonstrated senior experience as a lawyer, gained at a reputable law firm and/or in-house legal group, within the areas of Labour Law, Employment Law, Human Rights Law and/or related areas
Membership in the Law Society of Ontario as a Lawyer in good standing is required
Fluency and experience with the Employment Standards Act, Labour Relations Act and/or Crown Employees Collective Bargaining Act, the Ontario Human Rights Code, and the Occupational Health and Safety Act, is required
Strong understanding of key Ontario labour, employment and human rights jurisprudence and concepts required
Experience litigating labour and employment matters
Experience advising with a unionized context (i.e. labour law experience, in addition to employment law experience)
Ability to identify and resolve legal issues
Ability to work well as a full and valuable member of an integrated business-legal team
Able to think strategically, and comfortable working independently, as well as, a good understanding and judgment of situations which require escalation, including to portfolio leads and/or Chief Legal Officer
Contributor to and reviewer of corporate policies, standards, and procedures to minimize corporate legal risk and protect position, personnel, customers and assets
Ability to provide sound legal advice and suggest business-oriented solutions to complex legal issues in commercial and political contexts
Excellent interpersonal, negotiation, oral/written/presentation, and drafting skills, and able to provide legal opinions and interpretations, and direct and manage external legal counsel effectively
Ability to function well under pressure and demonstrate teamwork in a legal department and across client departments
Ability to translate complicated legal concepts into readily understandable advice
Experience appearing before, or directing cases before the Human Rights Tribunal, in Ontario Courts, and/or before grievance arbitrators will be an asset.
Experience managing labour and employment issues arising from complex commercial contracts would be an asset, as would experience conducting or advising on: workplace investigations and collective bargaining.
Experience in any of the following areas would be an asset: Privacy Law, FIPPA, Charter Law.

Drive SRE & Operations Leadership:
Lead, coach, and direct engineering teams responsible for day-to-day infrastructure operations, platform reliability, data center management, and disaster recovery.

description:

We are also building new and improved rapid transit, including GO Expansion, Light Rail Transit routes, and major expansions to Toronto’s subway system, to get people where they need to go, better, faster and easier. Metrolinx is an agency of the Government of Ontario.
At Metrolinx, equity, diversity and inclusion are essential to living our values of serving with passion, thinking forward and playing as a team.
This role is an in‑office position based at our 20 Bay St location. Our team is highly collaborative, and much of our work benefits from in‑person co‑creation, relationship‑building, and hands‑on partnership with leaders across the organization.
The Senior Manager, Internal Audit provides technical leadership and expertise in the development of audit approaches for Metrolinx’s complex I&IT and Operations programs.  The position applies deep subject matter expertise in information and payments technology, data governance and project management.  This experience will serve our multi-year audit strategies and approaches to address operational risk in alignment with international industry and audit best practices.  This role will provide leadership to the audit team on the application of International Auditing Standards and Risk Management frameworks.
The Senior Manager, Internal Audit is the senior level management position responsible for managing and overseeing complex and critical engagements within Internal Audit, in coordination with the IT and Operational Audit Director.
What will I be doing?
Advises Senior Management and the ARCC executive team on the development of multi-year audit strategies to provide assurance over Metrolinx’s complex I&IT and Operations process models, with consideration of international best practice approaches.
Leverages subject matter expertise in all aspects of the SDLC project lifecycle, and operations program management, and contracting to develop audit approaches tailored to Metrolinx’s evolving business model.
Determines the adequacy of Metrolinx’s network of risk management, controls, and governance processes, including maintaining current information on the various sources of assurance across the organization (e.g., reviews, audits, evaluations and assessments performed by the business areas or elsewhere in the organization).
Oversees execution of various audit projects and coordinates priorities with other audit manager(s) and across audit teams.
Provides strategic advice to Senior Management and the ARCC Executive on audit, risk, and compliance activities related to the Ministry of Transportation (MTO), the Office of the Auditor General of Ontario, and other external audit functions, and assesses compliance with other regulatory bodies.
Key support to Internal Audit Director to develop reports for executive management and the Audit Committee of the Board (e.g. results of audit projects, lessons learned and their applicability across the organization, Internal Audit operations, etc.); assists the Internal Audit Director to develop reports for Metrolinx Management Committees.
Manages IA projects and/or staff for conformance with professional (IIA) and divisional standards and industry best practice, including procuring and appropriately managing co-sourced audit service providers and utilizing the IIA competency framework.
Develops and maintains strong relationships with senior management to strengthen confidence and trust on IA Services; works collaboratively with senior management to ensure management action items and recommendations from audit findings are addressed and completed in a timely fashion.

Support the hiring and development of Managers and Auditor staff and management level personnel to have and maintain a talented team of professionals that work together well with a high level of self-initiative.

Bachelor’s degree/University degree or equivalent experience (e.g., Engineering, Business Administration, Information Technology, Accounting, or a related discipline).
Demonstrated progressive experience conducting internal audits, including experience directly managing audit staff, or a comparable combination of progressive experience in internal and external audit while obtaining relevant professional designation(s).
Demonstrated experience in a similar audit function and compliance environment is required. Similar experience in a related field, preferably in the public sector, is an asset.
Deep and recent experience leading IT audits, including audits of IT projects, systems, technology controls, and related operational processes, is required.
Certified Internal Auditor (CIA) is required.
Certified Information Systems Auditor (CISA), Certification in Risk Management Assurance (CRMA) certification is an asset.
Must become a member of the Institute of Internal Auditors.
Continuing Education in auditing, project management, technology and / or construction is required.
Relevant designations are expected with priority given to auditing designations.
Application of deep knowledge and expertise in operational and IT infrastructure auditing to provide tailored advice and recommendations to Senior Management and the ARCC Executive, including experience auditing complex operations and IT service and delivery models used within Canada and Internationally.
Knowledge of internal auditing standards and guidance in the International Professional Practice Framework and Code of Ethics issued by the IIA; knowledge of audit practice standards from the Chartered Professional Accountants of Canada (CPA Canada) to: maintain a comprehensive Internal Audit strategy for the organization; support the development of an annual and long-term risk-based internal audit plan; manage the development and execution of  audit plans, and the sophisticated data analysis, prevention and detection of fraud.
Knowledge of Quality Assurance (QA) methodology to manage quality assurance audits for projects led by professional staff, and to be well prepared for the team’s working papers to meet QA methodology standards on any independent QA review.
Experience and skill with preparing analyses, summaries, memos, and reports using computer applications including MS Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Access, Visio); experience with audit-related software applications (e.g., SQL and TeamMate); experience with TeamMate setup and maintenance is highly desired.

This role requires demonstrated experience with emerging technologies, including the ability to understand technical requirements, assess evolving privacy risks and ensure compliance with FIPPA and other applicable directives while enabling responsible innovation. The successful candidate will provide practical, risk-informed guidance to support privacy by design and uphold public trust in the delivery of digital services.
The successful candidate is a self-starter and will support initiatives in an agile capacity as a Privacy Subject Matter Expert across several business areas such as Transit Safety, PRESTO, Customer Experience, Information Technology, AI initiatives, and Marketing.
What will I be doing?
Promote interpretation, and compliance with legislative requirements of the Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act (FIPPA), and guidance from Ontario's Information and Privacy Commissioner.
Promote the development of privacy best practices above and beyond FIPPA and related legislative requirements, including requirements of the private-sector Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents Act (PIPEDA), guidance from the Federal Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada, guidance from the Ontario Public Service and related directives, and industry best practices.
Maintain current knowledge of the application of privacy legislation and regulations and industry changes and anticipate the impact on privacy issues to organizational/corporate practices.
As privacy subject matter expert, provide support to Metrolinx departments and project team members to ensure compliance with Metrolinx privacy policies, legislative and contractual obligations, and support standards and methodologies and implementation of best practices on an on-going basis.
Model Metrolinx’ s values and core competences, especially in dealings with external partners, and in the handling of personal and confidential information.
Support the privacy program governance framework under the leadership of the Director, Privacy Program.
Implement strategic privacy projects, including policies, best practices, and risk mitigation strategies across our departments.
Work effectively with other data governance partners such as Legal, AI Governance, Security, Records Management, and others to ensure a fulsome review and assessment of projects assigned.
Monitor and conduct privacy research activities to identify and assess jurisdictional/private sector and industry best practices, risks and impacts related to program delivery, to inform and enhance the effectiveness of Metrolinx's privacy policy, legal commitments, and program delivery.
Identify contentious issues, monitor changes to best practices and legal requirements, brief staff and senior management, and implement revisions/mitigation strategies.
Identify and assess privacy risks and provide advisory and consultative support to risk owners to develop appropriate mitigation plans. Conduct post-implementation analysis and reviews to ensure recommendations have been implemented.
Investigate privacy incidents to identify privacy breaches and support response plans through all phases of the incident response process, including privacy analysis, root cause analysis, development of mitigation strategies, and reviewing associated communications and reporting.
Lead investigations and respond to privacy inquiries, privacy complaints and breach incidents, and act as the primary contact for Ontario's Information and Privacy Commissioner; log follow-up activities and resolutions and provide advice to staff and senior management.
Review, propose, and coordinate appropriate action plans to address findings of privacy audits and monitoring, in collaboration with Internal Audit and departments.
Ensure assigned risks are added to the Enterprise Risk Register and monitor to ensure compliance with risk mitigation plans and associated timelines.
What Skills and Qualifications Do I Need?
Completion of a degree in Public Policy, Business Administration, Computer Science, Information Management, Information Technology, or related field – or a combination of education, training and experience deemed equivalent.
Demonstrated experience/training in providing technical advice in connection with emerging technologies, including an ability to understand technical requirements, assess evolving privacy risks and ensure legislative compliance while enabling responsible innovation.
Knowledge of and ability to interpret and apply legislation and government regulations guiding privacy protection and access to information (e.g. Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act (FIPPA), the Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents Act (PIPEDA), Canada's Anti-Spam Legislation (CASL).
Experience assessing privacy compliance for new programs, information systems, or services, ideally in a public sector environment.
Experience preparing a range of written materials, documentation, reports, briefing notes, training materials; brief senior management and staff on a range of privacy issues/matters; provide information/documentation to the IPC.
Strong interpersonal skills, with a sense of political acuity and the ability to present complex facts, information and explanations to different audiences including, matters brought before Ontario's Information and Privacy Commissioner and senior management.
Collaboration and relationship management skills to demonstrate aptitude for building trusted relationships and a reputation for sound judgement and pragmatism with internal clients and partners. Ability to work effectively and in partnership with colleagues, diverse teams (including legal counsel and information technology, internal audit, and risk professionals) and partners to build consensus and influence decisions; foster a culture of information privacy awareness.
Knowledge of data digitization, data mining, information flow and security concepts, to review and advise on the agreement of our technology/information management/security projects/plans to privacy practices and legislative compliance requirements.
Any relevant designations from IAPP such as CIPT/C, CIPP/C, AIGP, are an asset.

$29.30 per hour

Represents Metrolinx and the Metrolinx brand, and always works in accordance to our customer and safety charters to provide excellent customer service.

ABOUT THE MTCC
Located in the heart of downtown Toronto, the Metro Toronto Convention Centre (MTCC) is Canada’s most successful convention and trade show facility. The MTCC welcomes approximately 1 million visitors each year, hosting a variety of events from meetings and conventions to public shows and galas. The Centre is an economic driver, a proud supporter of our community, and a meeting place where meaningful connections are made. Beyond helping planners create successful events, we believe that “Our People are the Centre.” Our talented team is our greatest strength, and we offer a corporate culture that values work-life balance, great benefits, professional development, wellness, and fun.
Want to take a look behind the scenes? Visit our employee Instagram page:
@lifeatmtcc
JOB DESCRIPTION
We are currently recruiting for a Cleaning Services Supervisor in our Cleaning Services Department. Reporting to the Cleaning Services Manager, the successful candidate will ensure that the building is maintained to highest standard of cleaning that the MTCC has been recognized for throughout its history. If you have a passion for customer service and enjoy working in a high energy and creative work environment then this position is for you. The successful candidate will have strong work ethic and demonstrated ability to foster an engaging team environment.
Cleaning Services Supervisor plays an integral part to the success of the cleaning services team. Encouraging, coaching and teaching staff to complete the assigned tasks up to the MTCC’s high standard is of the upmost importance to this role’s success.
JOB RESPONSIBILTIES
Ensure that the building is maintained to highest standard of cleaning
Ensure that the building is completely clean after each shift including booth and equipment cleaning, bulk trash and tape removal
Administer and ensure that company policies and procedures are adhered to, including all health and safety and WHMIS legislation
Administrative duties which including scheduling, timesheets and accident reports
Supervise to guide and instruct for the purpose of performance and use of equipment and supplies.
Inspect buildings daily to ensure cleaning is maintained to high standard
Assisting with department weekly schedule to ensure alignment with the Collective Bargaining Agreement and  operational demands
Training and overlooking job responsibilities of new and existing staff
Train staff on Health & Safety procedures
Check Sign In/Out sheets for equipment and ensure accuracy
Track and complete staff shift sign in sheets and ensure accuracy
Inspect and record bulk trash amounts for each event for the purpose of billing
Track supply inventory levels and request additional supplies when needed
Distribute reminders on show floor to increase sales and promote booth cleaning to clients
Provide and complete client order forms on the show floor
In absence of Manager, represent the department
Please note that this position includes rotated shifts, nights, weekends and holidays. On occasion you would be required to fill in for the Cleaning Services Manager.
JOB SKILLS & QUALIFICATIONS
Strong working knowledge of power sweepers and scrubbers, plus high-speed floor machines
3-5 years of supervisory experience in a cleaning industry
Previous housekeeping experience preferably within a large facility is required
Work shifts on a rotational basis
Solid computer skills are required
Knowledge of Microsoft Word and Excel
Fluency in English is essential, French is an asset
Excellent customer service skills
Good communication skills

October 9, 2026

title: Director, Sector & Regional Development
description:
Position Summary:
The Director, Sector and Regional Development is responsible for executing on OVIN’s external engagement strategy to drive sector growth, strategic partnerships, and commercialization opportunities across Ontario’s automotive and mobility ecosystem. This role is focused on building and activating relationships with industry, global partners, government, and the broader innovation ecosystem to reinforce OVIN as a key connector and catalyst.
About the Ontario Centre of Innovation:
The Ontario Centre of Innovation (OCI) is a not-for-profit organization committed to accelerating economic growth in Ontario through the commercialization of advanced technologies and research. OCI acts as a bridge among academia, industry, and government, investing in collaborative R&D, fostering innovation ecosystems, and helping promising ventures bring new technologies to market. In 2024, OCI invested $117 million across the province, including $61 million in industry contributions. These efforts helped drive the creation and retention of over 5,500 jobs and catalyzed more than $700 million in private-sector follow-on investments. OCI’s role is central to Ontario’s vision of innovation-led prosperity: by reducing the risk of commercialization, facilitating partnerships, and strategically deploying capital into high-impact technologies, OCI contributes to the province’s competitiveness, talent retention, and long-term economic resilience.
Key Responsibilities:
As the Director, you will be expected assume the following responsibilities:
Strategic Partnerships & External Engagement
Support the development and deliver on the execution of OVIN’s external engagement strategy across Ontario and priority global markets.
Build, maintain, and expand relationships with industry leaders, SMEs, post-secondary institutions, government, and ecosystem partners.
Identify and secure high-value partnerships that drive commercialization, sector growth, and new opportunities.
Represent OVIN at industry forums, events, and engagements.
Sector Strategy & Market Intelligence
Maintain a deep understanding of sector trends across automotive, mobility, advanced manufacturing, and defence and dual-use technologies.
Identify emerging opportunities and align engagement strategies to advance OVIN’s strategic priorities.
Provide market insights and strategic advice to inform organizational direction and portfolio growth.
Regional & Ecosystem Development
Strengthen relationships across Ontario’s regional innovation ecosystems.
Lead initiatives that promote regional development, supply chain growth, and cross-sector collaboration.
Facilitate connections between Ontario companies and global markets, customers, and partners.
Work closely with internal teams to align external opportunities with program priorities and pipeline development.
Support and contribute to corporate initiatives, advisory committees, and cross-functional activities.
Other duties as assigned
Skills and Competencies:
10+ years of progressive experience in business development, strategic partnerships, or ecosystem development within automotive, mobility, advanced manufacturing, or related sectors
Demonstrated success in originating, structuring, and closing complex, multi-party partnerships and collaborations.
Strong, established network across industry, government, academia, and/or global markets.
Deep understanding of the Ontario innovation ecosystem, including funding programs, commercialization pathways, and key stakeholders.
Proven ability to identify and translate market and technology trends into actionable strategic opportunities.
Experience engaging with global partners and navigating international markets and partnerships
Strong commercial acumen, with the ability to assess business cases, partnership models, and investment opportunities.
Experience working with or alongside large industry players (OEMs, Tier 1s), SMEs, and scaling companies.
Demonstrated ability to influence senior stakeholders and operate effectively in ambiguous, fast-evolving environments.
Strong communication and executive presence, with experience representing organizations in high-profile forums.
Experience contributing to or shaping strategy, policy, or sector-level initiatives.
Highly developed analytical and critical thinking skills, with the ability to synthesize complex information into clear insights.
Ability to operate at both strategic and tactical levels, connecting ecosystem opportunities to programmatic outcomes.
High degree of professionalism, integrity, and sound judgment.
Internal Contacts/External Contacts
OCI staff at all levels
Industry (from the CEO to the shop floor)
Academic researchers, students, university research administrative staff
University/college/hospital/government administration
Government (at all levels, federal, provincial, and municipal)
Working Conditions
Frequent travel (30 – 70%) across Ontario.
Participation required in non-office hour events such as networking meetings and workshops
This role is being recruited for a current vacancy.
OCI is committed to creating a diverse and equitable environment and is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. OCI welcomes and encourages applications from people with disabilities. Accommodations are available on request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the selection process.

title: Director, Strategic Partnerships
description:
Position Summary
The Director, Strategic Partnerships is responsible for initiating, developing, and executing strategies and processes to promote OCI’s growth and sustainability.This role is a critical position at OCI and the successful candidate will act in coordination with the Executive Team to define short- and long-term strategies and work with internal and external stakeholders to execute on the strategies essential for the development of OCI. This role reports directly to the, Assistant Vice President, Corporate Development, Partnerships and International.
Who We Are
The Ontario Centre of Innovation (OCI) is the province’s leading innovation engine, bringing together industry, academia, government, and investors to accelerate commercialization and scale Ontario-made technologies.
From AI and quantum to life sciences, cleantech, and advanced manufacturing, OCI powers the programs and partnerships helping Ontario companies grow, compete globally, and build the future, right here.
Key Responsibilities:
Leadership
Lead staff, direct and indirect, by providing guidance and coaching, providing a clear sense of purpose and direction, and creating through his/her leadership a positive and stimulating work environment.
Actively participating in relevant business associations, technical committees, and professional organizations to promote and grow OCI’s network.
Leading key activities (e.g., committees of volunteer groups, advisory or review committees) or serving on corporate committees (e.g., Research, Commercialization, and /or Talent Committees), making proposal presentations, conducting project specific and business-case reviews, etc.).
Tracking developments and keeping up to date on the latest technological and business developments within the province; including current knowledge of sector specific industry news, regulations, and contacts.
Providing advice and support to other OCI support groups, e.g., Marketing / Communication and Finance groups on key initiatives.
Strategy and Delivery
Strengthen and manage OCI’s strategic relationships with but not limited to domestic and international organizations, academic institutions, Regional Innovation Centres (RICs), Angel and VC investment communities and economic development entities.
Direct the development of viable opportunities in partnership with key networks, negotiate partnerships and agreements and generate outcomes aligned with the Ontario Centre of Innovation (OCI) strategic and operating plans.
In conjunction with the Executive Team, the Director is accountable for developing new opportunities, agreements, and partnerships and other new project initiatives to increase OCI’s reach and create additional opportunities.
Accountable for identifying, contacting, and forging relationships with strategic partners as well as creating unique solutions-oriented strategies. Engage strategically with the public and private sectors and secure traditional as well as non-traditional industry-based partnerships to improve the impact, integration, and effectiveness of OCI’s investments.
Act as the primary point-of-contact to active partners to ensure value is being created and to continue evolve the partnership through its lifecycle.
Report KPIs to executives and conduct quarterly review with partners.
Develop strategy, conduct negotiations, and drive activities to closure.
Responsible for all aspects of the transaction through the coordination and facilitation of internal cross functional teams to identify and develop the strategic opportunities and partnerships.
Engage with developing networks to facilitate the formation of effective partnerships between industry, research, the investment community, and government.
Measure the performance of each partnered project and programs to quantify outcomes.
Actively participate in relevant business associations, committees, and professional organizations to promote and grow OCI’s network.
Required Skills and Competencies
Relevant post-secondary education, ideally in Engineering, Applied Science, Business, or equivalent
Significant work experience in building partnerships at the government, corporate, and non-profit stakeholders is highly desired, however, some experience may be drawn from advisory positions in investment, legal or consulting firms.
Experience in dealing with public sector funding along with federal and provincial contacts and network.
Strong strategic thinking to develop creative and effective strategies to achieve the organization’s strategic partnership objectives.
Ability to present effectively to stakeholders at all levels and lead discussions as a representative of OCI.
Strong skills in strategic and quantitative analysis, project management, leadership, negotiation, and oral and written communication are essential.
Demonstrated ability to work cross-functionally, managing internal and external teams.
A proven collaborator and relationship builder with ability to understand different perspectives, seek mutually beneficial solutions and broker deals.
Able to assume the role of both team player and team leader.
Familiar with the “language” and terminology of industry, finance, government, and the academic community.
Significant knowledge of Government agencies, Incubators, Accelerators, and their programs within Ontario Communities.
Understanding of the Ontario innovation ecosystem and key stakeholders.
Working Conditions
Standard office environment
Standard office hours
Onsite work with stakeholder partners
Required to attend at events outside of normal business hours
Travel 20 – 40% of the time within Ontario.
This role is being recruited to fill a current vacancy.
OCI
is committed to creating a diverse and equitable environment and is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. OCI welcomes and encourages applications from people with disabilities. Accommodations are available on request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the selection process.

title: Director, Strategic Programs
description:
Job Summary
Reporting to the Assistant Vice President, Strategic Programs, the Director, Strategic Programs will develop and execute strategies and tactical plans to achieve program and initiative targets and drive portfolio growth for a range of OCI programs. This role will primarily be responsible for managing the strategic growth of the portfolio, whilst also managing and supporting the successful delivery of a range of strategic initiatives, projects and partnerships. The Director, Strategic Programs will lead and or build the team(s) associated with the specific program(s) providing tactical guidance and coaching to staff and creating through their leadership a positive and stimulating work environment. The Director, Strategic Programs demonstrates strong leadership, strategic thinking and effective program management skills to ensure seamless execution of programs under the strategic programs portfolio. They will also support work to promote, market and build profile around Ontario’s leadership, nationally and globally.
Duties and Responsibilities
Analyze market trends and develop new proposals and approaches to create value for OCI’s strategic programs portfolio.
Support partnership opportunities with the various ministries and stakeholders to co-develop and negotiate new and existing programs and initiatives.
Drive thought leadership and outreach to a broad range of stakeholders across Canada’s priority areas.
Lead key program development and delivery activities, including but not limited to establishing program focus, objectives, structure, delivery model, processes, criteria and evaluation tool.
Develop and execute the strategic program(s) strategic planning process and report on program performance using quantitative and qualitative metrics, making data driven decisions and adjustments as necessary.
Build and maintain the OCI network, including the identification and development of strategic partnerships and initiatives to advance the stakeholder goals of this and other initiatives.
Leverage and grow existing networks of investors, alumni, mentors, and other community assets to support public sector led ventures.
Provide operational leadership to manage and deliver programs under the strategic programs portfolio.
Work collaboratively across the organization to deliver on program targets and deliverables, organizational objectives and the evolving needs of stakeholders.
Manage the allocation of resources, including budget and personnel to support the successful implementation of programs and initiatives.
Lead staff who are allocated to the assigned programming, including providing guidance and coaching, providing a clear sense of purpose and direction, and creating through his/her leadership a positive and stimulating work environment.

title: Investment Associate
description:
Investment Associate
Position Summary
The Investment Associate supports OCI’s investment activities by providing investment analysis, market intelligence, transaction support, and portfolio insights across a range of investment initiatives. Working with both investment funds and innovative growth-stage companies, the Associate contributes to investment decision-making and helps advance OCI’s strategic objectives within Ontario’s innovation ecosystem.
The role requires strong analytical capabilities, sound business judgment, and the ability to synthesize complex information into actionable recommendations. The successful candidate will work closely with internal stakeholders and engage with investors, entrepreneurs, researchers, and industry leaders to support OCI’s investment and commercialization mandate.
About the Ontario Centre of Innovation
The Ontario Centre of Innovation (OCI) is a not-for-profit organization committed to accelerating economic growth in Ontario through the commercialization of advanced technologies and research. OCI acts as a bridge among academia, industry, and government, investing in collaborative R&D, fostering innovation ecosystems, and helping promising ventures bring new technologies to market.
In 2024, OCI invested $117 million across the province, including $61 million in industry contributions. These efforts helped drive the creation and retention of over 5,500 jobs and catalyzed more than $700 million in private-sector follow-on investments.
OCI’s role is central to Ontario’s vision of innovation-led prosperity: by reducing the risk of commercialization, facilitating partnerships, and strategically deploying capital into high-impact technologies, OCI contributes to the province’s competitiveness, talent retention, and long-term economic resilience.
Key Responsibilities
Investment Research and Decision Support
Evaluate investment opportunities through financial analysis, market research, business assessment, and industry evaluation.
Develop investment recommendations and supporting analyses for internal stakeholders and decision-makers.
Conduct research on emerging technologies, sector trends, investment activity, and market developments.
Prepare briefing materials, investment memoranda, presentations, and other decision-support documents.
Analyze opportunities across a variety of sectors, including technology, life sciences, cleantech, advanced manufacturing, and other innovation-driven industries.
Transaction Management and Investment Operations
Support investment activities throughout the transaction lifecycle, including opportunity assessment, diligence coordination, and closing activities.
Manage information requests and coordinate with internal and external stakeholders during investment reviews.
Assist with investment documentation, approvals, and administrative processes.
Support ongoing investment program initiatives and special projects as required.
Portfolio Insights and Performance Analysis
Monitor portfolio performance through the collection and analysis of financial, operational, and strategic information.
Identify trends, risks, and opportunities across portfolio investments and prepare recommendations where appropriate.
Contribute to portfolio reviews, performance reporting, and governance materials.
Maintain investment records and support portfolio data management and analysis.
Ecosystem Development and Stakeholder Engagement
Build and maintain relationships with founders, investors, fund managers, research institutions, accelerators, and ecosystem partners.
Support OCI’s visibility and engagement within Ontario’s innovation and investment community.
Participate, as needed, in industry events, conferences, and stakeholder meetings to strengthen market awareness and identify emerging opportunities.
Contribute insights on ecosystem developments, investment trends, and market activity to support strategic planning and investment priorities.
Qualifications
Education and Experience
Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, Economics, Science, Engineering, or a related field.
Minimum five years of experience in venture capital, private equity, investment banking, corporate development, management consulting, strategic finance, capital markets, commercialization, or a related analytical role.
Demonstrated experience conducting financial analysis, evaluating business opportunities, and preparing professional recommendations for senior stakeholders.
Skills and Competencies
Strong analytical, quantitative, and problem-solving skills.
Advanced financial modeling, valuation, and research capabilities.
Ability to assess investment opportunities and synthesize complex information into clear recommendations.
Excellent written, verbal, and presentation communication skills.
Strong organizational skills and ability to manage multiple priorities effectively.
Professional judgment, integrity, and attention to detail.
Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively across teams.

Experience with venture investing, fund investing, startup ecosystems, technology commercialization, or innovation-focused organizations.
Knowledge of Ontario’s innovation, research, and investment landscape.
Experience evaluating companies across sectors such as software, artificial intelligence, life sciences, cleantech, or advanced manufacturing.
MBA, CFA, CBV, or other relevant professional designation is considered an asset.

OCI leadership and employees across investment, commercialization, strategy, and corporate functions.

Founders, investors, fund managers, industry leaders, academic institutions, researchers, innovation organizations, and government stakeholders.

title: Lead, OVIN Incubators
description:
Who We Are:
Ontario Centre of Innovation (OCI) was established in 1987 and is a leading not-for-profit organization that works with industry, academia, and government. OCI focuses on ensuring that the people of Ontario reap the personal and economic benefits of leading-edge research underway at our publicly funded universities, colleges, and research hospitals - research that can be transformed into technologies and services that enhance quality of life and help build a globally competitive, job-creating economy in Ontario.
Specifically, OCI supports the commercialization of academic intellectual property (IP), industry-academic collaborations, and the development and adoption of emerging technologies. This includes overseeing the execution of advanced technology platforms that will equip Ontario companies to compete in a competitive global digital economy.
We also support and invest in early-stage projects where the probability of commercial success and investment return on innovation are substantial. OCI’s strong expertise in de-risking innovation helps attract private investors and other funders to new ventures, bolstering their success. We also contribute to the development and retention of talent to ensure that industry has access to personnel with the most advanced skills and knowledge and that highly trained personnel find opportunities to apply their expertise in Ontario.
OCI leads the Ontario Vehicle Innovation Network (OVIN) initiative on behalf of the Government of Ontario. OVIN builds upon Ontario’s position as a world-leading automotive manufacturing and supply jurisdiction in addition to the large cluster of information and communication technology companies operating in the province. Ontario’s high-quality post-secondary institutions, first class talent, innovative small and medium sized enterprises, and infrastructure to support entrepreneurship ensure that the province is uniquely positioned to capture the economic opportunity of the automotive technology and smart mobility innovation space and lead the global mobility transformation.
Through resources such as research and development (R&D) funding, talent development, technology acceleration, business and technical supports, and demonstration grounds, OVIN provides a competitive advantage to Ontario-based automotive and mobility companies – allowing Ontario to reinforce its position as a North American leader in transformative automotive technologies, as well as transportation and infrastructure systems.
The Opportunity:
OVIN, in collaboration with industry partners, post-secondary institutions, municipalities and regional stakeholders is launching automotive and mobility incubators, designed to:
Foster a collaborative ecosystem where researchers, entrepreneurs, startups and scale-ups can systematically engage with industry
Support research and the commercialization of IP through interdisciplinary projects
Support the translation of IP and new technologies into the creation of new ventures across the province
Provide resources and programming to support the success and viability of new ventures and regional incubation and acceleration space in the province
Reporting to the Manager, Incubators, the Lead, OVIN Incubators will be the regional representative for all incubator activities, manage the day-to-operations, and play a coordinating role between all key stakeholders.
Key Responsibilities
The Lead is expected to assume operational responsibilities, including, but not limited to:
Support the Manager on the strategic planning and design of OVIN Incubators, ensuring alignment with organizational goals and objectives.
Apply knowledge of research commercialization and start-up incubation/acceleration to make recommendations on program development, execution and improvements, in collaboration with internal and external stakeholders.
Develop and maintain a database of enterprises active in the sector.
Develop and maintain a database of academic researchers active in the sector.
Pursue extensive outreach to enterprises in the sector.
Develop and manage the incubator intake and review processes, timelines, program budgets and the day-to-day delivery of the program.
Work collaboratively and liaise with incubator partners, including members of industry and post-secondary institutions, to ensure that key requirements are defined, and program delivery executed within the appropriate framework.
Execute on the promotion of incubator programming, working in tandem with the key stakeholders and departments within OCI.
Support steering committee and other stakeholder meetings.
Support OCI/ OVIN Incubator presence at external events and functions, including delivering content at meetings, workshops, and events in support of incubator programming.
Work cross-functionally across departments and collaboratively with other OCI staff (Business Development Operations, Programs, and MARCOM etc.).
Manage program stewardship, including program monitoring and metrics, outcomes, and impacts for internal strategy and external reporting.
Support Manager to identify and manage program outcomes, and work with marketing and communications teams to develop success stories.
May be required to perform other related duties as assigned.
Qualifications
:
Bachelor's degree in a relevant field (e.g., Business, Technology, Project Management).
3-5 years experience in program management, incubators, start-up/SME support or technology/IP development particularly in: automotive and mobility, research projects or technology integration.
Strong project management skills, including budgeting, scheduling, and resource allocation.
Excellent communication and presentation abilities.
Problem-solving abilities and adaptability in a dynamic environment.
Highly developed, interpretive and analytical skills in MS Word, PowerPoint, and Excel.
Innovation, technology commercialization, or entrepreneurship program management experience; experience with automotive and mobility programs would be a strong asset.
Occasional requirement to attend events outside of normal business hours.
Occasional travel within Ontario.
Competencies:
Team player with highly developed interpersonal skills and the ability to work effectively and collaborate with people at all levels within the organization and externally.
Demonstrated high degree of initiative, efficient, organized and able to produce high quality work under pressure in a fast-paced environment, with the ability to manage numerous conflicting and changing priorities simultaneously.
Ability to work with minimal supervision and take accountability to address obstacles and overcome barriers by identifying possible resolution options and alternatives.
Intellectually curious about developments and trends in a sector.
Able to demonstrate integrity and ethics in decision making and in relationships with colleagues and clients.
Able to reflect and promote OCI’s values through work with colleagues, clients and stakeholders.

description:
Ontario Centre of Innovation (OCI) drives the development of Ontario’s economy by helping create new jobs, products, services, technologies, and businesses. In partnership with industry, OCI co-invests to commercialize innovation originating in the province’s publicly funded colleges, universities, and research hospitals. We also support and invest in early-stage projects, where the probability of commercial success and potential total return on innovation are substantial. Another expanding focus for OCI is the development of the next generation of innovators through our entrepreneurship fellowships and programs for students and youth across Ontario. OCI’s efforts are focused on sectors of the economy with the greatest potential to drive Ontario’s future prosperity and global competitiveness: energy and environment (including water); advanced manufacturing; advanced health technologies; and information, communications technologies, and digital media. A trusted partner of government in program delivery, we are committed to advancing a whole-of-government approach as a means of streamlining funding application processes for companies and entrepreneurs.
OVIN (Ontario Vehicle Innovation Network), led by OCI, is the Government of Ontario’s flagship initiative to support the future of the automotive and mobility sector. The Director, Education Design & Intelligence will shape how TVO responds. Learning Design, Pathways & Assessment
Lead the human-centred design and continuous improvement of learning experiences across TVO’s education portfolio, ensuring they are inclusive, accessible, pedagogically grounded, and responsive to changing learner needs.
Establish and maintain shared learning design principles, standards, and frameworks that guide how educational experiences are conceived, developed, evaluated, and improved across programs and platforms.
Work in close partnership with the Director, Curriculum & Course Production, Director, Content Engagement, and Director, Academic Services to strengthen learner journeys, pathways, engagement, and educational outcomes.
Lead the continuous review and modernization of assessment and evaluation practices across TVO Education, responding to developments in AI, academic integrity, learner evidence, and emerging approaches to teaching and learning.
Establish processes for regularly evaluating learning design standards, assessment approaches, and learner journeys, using research, learner feedback, outcomes data, prototyping, and testing to guide continuous improvement.
Examine how AI and emerging technologies are reshaping curriculum, instruction, assessment, learner supports, credentialing, and progression, and translate those developments into practical opportunities for TVO.
Embed collaborative design practices that centre diverse perspectives, lived experiences, accessibility, and learner needs.
AI Strategy, Emerging Technology & Professional Learning

Establish responsible, ethical, equitable, accessible, and learner-centred approaches to integrating AI into educational experiences, services, and internal workflows.

Identify, evaluate, and recommend emerging technologies, tools, platforms, and practices that can advance TVO’s educational mission and improve learning experiences.

Develop and implement a professional learning strategy that builds AI literacy, digital fluency, instructional capability, and confidence across the Education division.
Create learning experiences, communities of practice, guidance, and resources that help employees use emerging technologies effectively, critically, creatively, and responsibly.
Foster a culture of curiosity, experimentation, knowledge sharing, and continuous learning that enables teams to navigate educational and technological change.
Contribute expertise to the development of AI literacy and fluency initiatives for educators, learners, and families in collaboration with the Directors responsible for programming, content, and academic services.

Lead, coach, and develop team members, creating clarity, encouraging collaboration, and building the capabilities needed for future-focused educational design and production.
Manage budgets, contracts, technology investments, and resources associated with Learning Experience Design and Production, and oversee allocated resources for professional learning and innovation initiatives in AI and emerging educational technology.

Work in close partnership with Directors across Education to ensure that learning design, AI, production, technology, and learner experience decisions support shared educational priorities.
Build strong working relationships across TVO so that educational design and AI initiatives are aligned with broader organizational, technology, research, communications, and operational directions.

Education
A postsecondary degree in Education, Educational Leadership, Learning Design, Educational Technology, Instructional Design, Digital Learning, Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, or a related field is required. description:
