title: Sr. Financial Analyst - Finance
description:
Req ID: 28641
Vacancy Type: Permanent
Number of Positions: 1
Closing Date: 10/07/2026
Job Summary
Supports the preparation and presentation of budgets and business plan submissions while ensuring the accuracy and timeliness of financial statements and forecasts. The role involves monitoring budget variances, managing complex operating and capital portfolios, and developing financial models to support decision making. This role follows a hybrid work model, requiring employees to be onsite in the office 3 days per week and allowing remote work for the remaining days. Specific in-office days may be set by the team or department to support collaboration and business needs. Our offices are located at Mississauga City Hall, 300 City Centre Drive in Mississauga.
Duties and Responsibilities
Prepare monthly journal entries and perform detailed balance sheet reconciliations to ensure the accurate and timely presentation of financial statements.
Develop quarterly financial statements and forecasts, providing clear variance commentary and insights for senior leadership and members of council.
Lead financial review meetings with Managers and Directors, delivering analysis and data driven forecast recommendations that reflect current business conditions.
Lead the Business Planning budget process, evaluating departmental initiatives for compliance, accuracy, reasonableness, and financial data integrity.
Oversee the operating and capital budget processes, including consolidation, review, validation, and coordination with departments and corporate partners.
Conduct financial analysis of operating and capital expenditures, identifying trends and recommending appropriate budget adjustments.
Develop financial models, labour costing analyses, and scenario evaluations to support departmental planning and strategic initiatives.
Collaborate with departments, Corporate Finance, HR, and other internal partners to support business planning, labour analysis, and financial submissions.
Provide well supported financial advice and recommendations to internal stakeholders to guide planning, resourcing, and decision making.
Identify, recommend, and implement enhancements to financial processes, reporting quality, and operational efficiency.
Skills and Qualifications
Graduation from a recognized post-secondary institution, preferably in Business, Accounting, Economics, or related field.
Strong understanding of finance, accounting, and accounting terminology are required.
Professional accounting designation (CPA, CA, CGA, CMA) preferred.
Minimum five (5) years of related experience in a municipal or other public sector environment.
Proficiency in financial analysis/modelling.
Microsoft Office applications skills required.
Knowledge of SAP and Questica systems an asset.
Excellent analytical and organizational skills with an ability to manage multiple projects and priorities, under pressing deadlines, are essential.
Excellent research and written skills, including reading and interpreting legislation, regulations, and policies/standards required.
Strong interpersonal skills required.
Ability to work as part of a team with a demonstrated ability to collaborate and work in consultation with internal staff as well as external groups, agencies, corporations, and Members of Council.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills. Must have strong organizational, problem solving and decision making skills.
The role requires business and political acumen when collaborating with internal staff and external groups.
Staying informed of all regulations and legal requirements that may influence financial policy, projects, and initiatives.

Job Summary
Responsible for enforcement of City by-laws by interpreting the by-laws and communicating these to the general public.
Duties and Responsibilities
The Specialized Housing Enforcement (SHE) Unit administers and enforces a range of municipal by-laws, licensing requirements, and regulatory standards governing City-regulated housing accommodations. The team conducts inspections, investigations, public education, and enforcement activities related to apartment buildings, short-term rentals, additional residential units, lodging houses, and other regulated housing uses to ensure compliance and support safe housing conditions for residents. Bylaws enforced include, but are not limited to the Rental Apartment Buildings By-law, the Property Standards By-law, and the Short-Term Rental Accommodation Licensing By-law.
To be considered, candidates must meet and maintain the following requirements:
Interpret and apply municipal by-laws, legislation, policies, standards, and regulatory requirements.
Investigate complaints, collect evidence, and perform follow-up inspections and investigations to achieve and maintain compliance.
Conduct inspections and investigations to determine compliance and identify contraventions.
Resolve compliance issues through education, voluntary compliance, and enforcement. Where necessary, take legal action in order to bring violators into conformity/compliance, providing professional testimony and evidence for court and tribunal hearings
Prepare and maintain accurate inspection records, correspondence, reports, notices, orders, and prosecution briefs.
Initiate legal proceedings where necessary and present evidence before courts and tribunals.
Participate in joint enforcement operations with police and other enforcement agencies.
Provide information and education to residents, businesses, City staff, elected officials, and industry stakeholders.
Review by-laws, operational policies and procedures, and recommend amendments, changes, etc.
Adhere to a strict code of confidentiality, incidental to all investigations.
SHE is one of 3 by-law enforcement Units, the others being Property Standards, Investigations, and Enforcement (PSIE), and By-law, Compliance, and Enforcement (BCE), who deal primarily with private property investigations and licensing/nuisance bylaws, respectively.
Perform other duties as assigned.
NOTE
: This position will require the successful candidates to work various shifts, which include days, evenings, overnight, weekends and statutory holidays and, at times, will require overtime. This position may involve operating a City fleet vehicle and wearing of a City-issued uniform. A Vulnerable Sector Check (Level 3) will be required of all successful candidates, at their own expense, to verify the absence of a criminal record for which a pardon has not been granted. There may be a written test conducted as part of the interview process. Successful candidates for this Municipal By-law Enforcement Officer (MBEO) competition may be considered for other MBEO positions, including PSIE and BCE, based on operational needs.

Municipal Law Enforcement Officer certification (may be obtained upon hiring)

Graduate of a recognized community college in discipline of law enforcement, security administration, criminal justice studies or a by-law related course/major.
3-5 years working experience in related disciplines
Excellent communication, interpersonal and conflict-resolution skills
Strong organization and time management skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and meet deadlines.
Experience with Microsoft Office programs and appropriate City software.
Site visits where there is considerable debris to manoeuvre around. May require some lifting of objects. Detailed visual inspections.
Ability to work primarily in the field operating a vehicle to conduct inspections and general patrols, along with general office duty

Reporting to the Senior Manager, Revenue, responsible for the management and direction of all collection activities for defaulted Provincial Offence Act (POA) fines, non-parking Administrative Monetary Penalty (AMPS), tax accounts in arrears, and miscellaneous receivables owed to the City.  In addition, this position is responsible for all administrative aspects of the Tax Collection, POA, and General Receivables sections. This individual provides leadership, strategic direction, and overall staff development within the Corporate Collections area.  The individual will be required to either personally represent the Corporation or co-ordinate representation in dealings with external agencies, various clients, legal proceedings and appeal hearings.  Provides direction, guidance and skills development to non-union and union staff.
Manage all operational and administrative aspects of the tax arrears, defaulted POA fines, Non-parking AMPS and general accounts receivable billing and collection processes including supervision, hiring, guidance and direction of staff; •    Review and initiate staff development activities; •    Monitor/ coach area supervisory staff to ensure that proper priorities and service levels are established and maintained; •    Recommend, plan, develop and implement new or innovative procedures to improve efficiency and the overall success of collection activities; •    Recommend and implement changes to Corporate Policies and Standard Operating Procedures as required; •    Provide leadership to ensure high productivity to realize corporate priorities; •    Manage debt collection activities undertaken by both internal staff and on behalf of the City by external service providers, such as collection agencies and bailiffs; •    Ensure accuracy of commissions paid to external collectors; •    Ensure that all collection activities are compliant with applicable legislation, Municipal Act,  City policies and By-laws, and Memorandum of Understanding with the Ministry of the Attorney General for POA fine activities; •    Manage the Tax Sale process in strict compliance with the requirements of the Municipal Act, Ontario Regulations, and court precedent; •    Represent the Department/City in meetings with internal and external customers, suppliers, tribunals, legal proceedings, professional associations, and municipal and provincial governments; •    Responsible for the accuracy and balance of the Accounts Receivable system ; •    Ensure a proper system of internal controls are in place for entries to TXM 2000 tax system, CAMS, the Integrated Court Offences Network (ICON), the Accounts Receivable system and related General Ledger entries; •    Review and authorize cheque requisitions and reconciliations for the distribution of the POA fines collected on behalf of other municipalities and government agencies; •    Responsible for the approval and posting to the general ledger of journal entries for POA revenue and general accounts receivable. •    Review doubtful accounts and make annual financial provision for doubtful allowance in the general ledger. •    Responsible for identification of uncollectable accounts (POA, property tax and general accounts receivable) and preparation of Council reports for write-off of accounts. •    Prepare reports as required for Council information and approval •    Prepare and monitor the annual budget for all accounts under Corporate Collections responsibility. •    Prepare related schedules of annual Financial Information Return (FIR) as needed; •    Establish and maintain a high level of professional customer service in balance with  effective collection processes; •    Responsible for managing the procurement process (Request for Proposal, Request for Quote) and administer contracts with external vendors related to the operation of the Collections unit. •    Collaborates with systems administrators and vendors in preparation of business requirements, testing and deployments of any new software for the Collections unit. •    Establish and maintain a high level of professional customer service in balance with effective collection methods; •    Provide assistance/backup to Supervisor of Tax Collection and Collections Group Leader as required; •    Ensure that records retention is in compliance with legislative and by-law requirements.

EDUCATION:
Post secondary degree in Business Administration or other relevant discipline.
EXPERIENCE:
5 years senior supervisory experience in a unionized environment •    Collection experience is required

Completion of a CPA designation (CA, CMA, CGA) is considered an asset •    Sound knowledge of The Municipal Act with exceptional understanding of Taxation and Tax Collection requirements •    Knowledge of public sector operations and PeopleSoft financials modules are an asset •    Excellent organizational skills with acute attention to detail •    Exceptional communication skills along with superior report writing, performance and work record.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
:
Reporting to the Manager, Internal Audit, (or to the Director, Internal Audit on solo projects) this position plans, performs internal audit assurance and advisory engagements of moderate complexity for the City of Brampton in accordance with the Internal Audit Charter and recognized Internal Audit Professional Practices and codes of professional conduct. This includes initiating, leading and conducting, risk based audits, operational effectiveness reviews, audits of compliance with applicable legislation, regulations, by-laws, City policies and procedures and working with management to develop effective and efficient risk mitigation strategies. Ability to work independently and objectively when conducting audit engagements of moderate complexity, preparing audit reports and evaluating management action plans. Supports the Director in planning, coordinating and management of audit resources, including third party consultants. Participating in the development of the audit function’s strategic plan and multi-year and annual internal audit work plan.  The role is an ambassador for risk management and continuous improvement of the control environment, and brings innovative ideas and methods to increase awareness and buy-in from management.
Conducts operational audits in accordance with professional audit standards in the role of lead auditor, team member or working independently on some projects, with responsibility to supervise more junior project staff
Performs assigned projects of moderate complexity (or work with a Manager, Internal Audit on complex audit engagements) and deal with high dollar values and confidential and sensitive information affecting the City operations, assets and resources
Develops a solid understanding of the audit entity or subject matter by conducting background research accomplished through use of the internet, discussion with the auditee, site visits, the review of relevant documents such as multi-year business plans, consultant reports, statues, regulations or standards, committee and council minutes, previous year’s audited financial statements and management letters, contact with other professional and municipal organizations
Develops (independently or in collaboration with the Manager, Internal Audit) the project plan including determining audit objectives, scope and methodology; assessing risk and internal controls; establishing budget and reporting timelines
Prepares (independently or in collaboration with the Manager, Internal Audit) the audit program and /or evidence collection plan which includes defining of audit criteria by performing extensive research of sources such as recognized bodies of experts, applicable laws, regulations and other authorities, other bodies or jurisdictions delivering similar programs and services, internal policies and procedures and applicable criteria successfully applied in other audits or reviews done internally and externally; developing audit procedures and tests; and determining what evidence is needed, how the evidence can be collected, will be analyzed, interpreted
Complete assigned audit procedures (interviews, analysis, examination of documentation, site visits, and other testing) in accordance with the project plan and adapts /expands audit procedures, as necessary, based on issues identified as the audit progresses
Conducts thorough assessment and analysis and obtains sufficient and appropriate evidence
Identifies significant audit issues and improvement opportunities, quantifying cost savings / revenue opportunities, and illustrating non-financial impacts
Develops practical and meaningful audit recommendations that will help improve City services or operations
Prepares and / or reviews audit working papers (audit project files) that contains evidence supporting the findings, conclusions, and recommendations and ensures that they adhere to professional auditing standards and Internal Audit’s office guidelines and audit manuals.
Evaluate audit results and prepares a written summary of major audit issues (audit observations, conclusions, and recommendations) independently or in consultation with the Manager, Internal Audit or the Director of Internal Audit
Demonstrate critical thinking skills in all aspects of work (audit planning, fieldwork, audit finding evaluation, and reporting)
Prepares draft audit reports or parts thereof, for review by the senior management of Internal Audit prior to submission to auditee, Audit Committee and /or other standing committees
Makes presentations to auditee personnel to communicate audit recommendations, as required.
Evaluates action plans in response to recommendations
Keeps Director/Manager, Internal Audit informed of audit progress, any emerging issues and /or significant areas, and recommends appropriate action and /strategies to meet planned project objectives and audit reporting deadlines
Attends Audit Committee meetings and makes presentations on audit project(s) as required
Performs special audits and investigations including fraud reviews and forensic audits, as required
Maintains good auditee relationships and acts at all times in a professional manner
Liaises with and keeps current of the operations of assigned departments with particular reference to audit concerns and issues
Contribute to effective teamwork and communication, high standards of work quality and organizational performance and continuous learning
Participates in development and implementation of Internal Audit’s corporate initiatives, including coordinating training, IT system applications, continuous process improvement projects etc)
Contributes to the Internal Audit’s strategic planning process, such as the City-wide risk assessment, and annual and long-term work plan
SELECTION CRITERIA
Education:
University Degree, with a professional Accounting Designation (such as CPA, CA; CPA, CGA; or CPA, CMA); or designation as an auditing professional (CIA, CGAP, CRMA, CISA).
An equivalent combination of education, skills and considerable experience in the field of performance auditing, operational and control auditing, and other audit projects will be considered.
Fraud certifications Audit certifications (such as CFE) are an asset.
Experience:
A minimum of 5 years of practical experience planning, performing, and reporting on value-for-money/performance audits, operational/control audits, and other audit projects, with at least 2 years of leading experience with audit professionals. Public sector internal audit experience is desirable.
Comprehensive in-depth knowledge of all aspects of audit principles, practices, techniques and standards (including the IIA Standards and the Generally Accepted Government Auditing Standards.)
Other Skills and Assets:
Sound organizational, interpersonal, oral and written communications skills.
Sound project management, analytical, excellent initiative, and problem solving skills.
Ability to deal courteously and effectively with all levels of staff, management and members of council, and build consensus.
Ability to work independently and with minimum supervision.
Ability to work in a multi-disciplinary setting and team environment.
Computer proficiency in MS Office Suite and audit applications such as TeamMate or Pentana.
Experience with data analytics applications (such as ACL, TeamMate Analytics) and performing data analytics as part of audits or other special projects which assist in the collection and analysis of electronic data would be asset.
Experience with Pentana, TeamMate or other audit software is strongly preferred.
Mandatory Requirements:
University Degree in relevant fields (business, accounting, management), coupled with an accounting designation (CPA, CA or CPA, CMA or CPA, CGA); or and auditing designation such as CIA, CISA.
A minimum of 5 or more years practical experience planning, performing, and reporting on value-for-money (performance) audits, operational/control audits,  and other audit projects, with at least 2 years of leading experience with audit professionals.

AREA OF RESPONSIBILITY:
Reporting directly to the Treasurer, this role provides strategic direction and expert advice to the Finance Division on financial planning, budget review, and ensuring fiscal efficiency. The role involves preparing detailed assessments, aligning departmental proposals with the City’s Strategic Plan, and ensuring financial and legislative compliance. This position also plays a critical role in City-wide strategic planning, fostering a collaborative environment that values trust, diversity, and inclusivity.
Stakeholder Relationships
Collaborate with stakeholders to identify improvement areas, facilitate solutions, and promote a culture of fiscal responsibility and innovation. •    Build effective working relationships at all levels, particularly with senior leaders in client departments across the City, ensuring the highest possible level of client satisfaction and being established as a trusted advisor. •    Build and foster strong working relationships and collaborative arrangements with internal and external customers, stakeholders, business and community leaders, sponsors, public and the media.
Operation Strategy
Lead initiatives that enhance operational excellence, setting goals and implementing policies to support Council priorities. •    Identify and manage complex, interdependent projects, ensuring alignment with relevant strategic goals. •    Provide the Treasurer with recommendations on managing critical issues and risks. •    Ensure a high standard of financial planning, budget, management reporting, and analytical support is delivered consistently to their department portfolio. •    Establish clear goals and create policies that support the Council’s priorities and the City’s strategic vision. •    Regularly review and report on the status of strategic initiatives to ensure continuous alignment with strategic goals.
Financial Analysis & Strategic Planning
Provide financial analysis, support the annual budget process, and prepare short to long-term capital funding analysis. •    Advise on financial impacts of budget proposals and submit recommendations to the leadership team and Council. •    Participate in strategic planning at both the sectional level as well as the provision of expertise to the broader City-wide strategy. •    Prepare detailed financial reports that include analysis, projections, and recommendations. •    Assist with the annual budget planning process, ensuring it meets the City’s financial requirements and strategic objectives.
Policy & Legislative Support
Interpret legislation, monitor trends, and use research and data analytics to inform policy and strategy decisions. •    Maintain knowledge of all laws, regulatory, judicial mandates, ordinances, legislative various acts, codes and by-laws set out by Federal, Provincial or Municipal levels of government. •    Continuously update policies and procedures to reflect legislative changes and best practices.
Financial Modelling & Advice
Develop financial models and provide insights to support decision-making, collective bargaining, and resource management. •    Offer guidance to finance staff across City departments. •    Provide financial analysis, support the annual budget process, and prepare short to long-term capital funding analysis. •    Provide expert advice on the financial implications of various budget proposals to the leadership team and Council.
Communication and Reporting
Prepare and present complex financial reports and recommendations, keeping leadership informed of key activities and initiatives. •    Develop comprehensive financial reports that accurately reflect the City’s financial status and projections. •    Regularly update the leadership team on key financial activities and initiatives. •    Maintain a high level of transparency in all financial communications to build trust and credibility.
SELECTION CRITERIA:
Education:
Post-secondary degree in Economics, Business, Public Administration or other relevant discipline. •    CPA designation (CA, CMA, CGA) or CFA or MBA is preferred.
Experience:
Minimum 5 years of progressive experience in finance or public administration, preferably within a municipal or similarly complex organization, with significant responsibility for strategic and financial analysis, multi-year operating and capital budgets, funding strategies, and business case development. •    Proven experience advising senior leadership, leading and facilitating complex cross-departmental initiatives, and applying legislative and policy analysis to support financial, strategic, and organizational decision-making.
Other Skills and Assets:
Strong analytical, communication, and problem-solving abilities, with proficiency in Microsoft tools. •    Ability to handle sensitive situations with discretion and maintain strong internal and external relationships. •    Strong knowledge of financial planning, budget management, and capital funding analysis. •    Excellent written and verbal communication skills for preparing and presenting complex financial reports and recommendations. •    Expert knowledge of Municipal, Regional, Provincial and Federal Governments, applicable Legislations and awareness of current social, economic and political priorities •    Ability to prioritize highly complex tasks with critical deadlines •    Experience developing policies and procedures and ensuring compliance

Area of Responsiblities:
Reporting to the Manager, Enterprise Corporate Systems, this position will participate in a major City-wide project to implement an application that will deliver automation and transform business processes and practices in the area of WFM Workforce Management solutions supporting Employee Time Capture, Absence Management (Time and Attendance) and Workforce Scheduling. This position is responsible for assessing, researching, analysing and documenting business and systems requirements while working with both internal, external and City-wide department resources. In addition, the incumbent will be heavily involved in the design of business processes, testing, training and the preparation of operational documentation.
This role partners with HR, Finance and Operating Departments in supporting, troubleshooting, coordinating, implementing and recommending solutions that meet client needs. This role can be involved in the RFP process as well as development of business requirements to ensure that projects align with strategies.
Once this application is live and in production, this position will be responsible for the support and on-going maintenance of the application as well as recommend solutions to leverage the functional capabilities to meet future business needs. This position will also offer guidance, support, advice, and direction to various City departments in post-implementation operations of this system and related integrations/interfaces to enhance the use of these systems, thus leveraging functionality to gain efficiencies in business processes and/or greater insight into information. This position provides excellent customer service while protecting the integrity of the data, automating business processes, participating in major system implementations, upgrades, troubleshooting incidents and maintaining optimal configuration.
Business Analysis
- Liaise with clients to gather business requirements, to conduct current and future process mapping to determine the fit/gap in the planning and development of new system functionality and/or related business processes. Consult with Stakeholders and evaluate business needs to develop understanding of true requirements and translate into functional specifications while working with technical teams, to recommend solutions. Interpret Union collective agreements and collaborate when necessary to understand the rules, knowing how they intersect with business processes, system functionality and related system configuration. Present, explain, and validate analysis with client to ensure proposed solution meets their business needs. Lead the implementation of necessary business and systems changes. Serve as a functional source of expertise in supporting the maintenance and/or development of process improvements and changes. Perform benchmarking to help determine the future/strategic direction of the systems.
System Technical Analysis
- Responsible for defining interface parameters between systems, identifying system data dependencies, and approving all technical specifications and changes. Responsible for the daily operation and troubleshooting of user problems.  Lead and contribute to project teams to assist in the research, selection, evaluation and implementation of new software applications and services.
Confidentiality
- Access to system wide confidential data for analysis and operations. Participate in development and implementation of confidential initiatives.
Testing and Quality Assurance
-
Prepare, review and collaborate on development of test strategy, test plans and test metrics. Create user stories, use cases and subsequently create and execute detailed test scripts including documenting of defects, defect reporting and collaborative issues resolution. Prepare testing time and effort estimates and schedule testing activities with various resources. Report on testing status and progress against project plans. Manage the design, specification and execution of tests, including ensuring that test design accounts for risk and selecting the appropriate test types. Review and improve on test cases developed by other testers. Interacts with developers, project team resources and vendors during issue resolution and re-testing. Utilize appropriate tools for test scripting, test execution, defect reporting and overall status reporting.
System Lead and Trainer
- Act as Project Lead or Project Support for different initiatives. Act as the System Lead in developing and providing direction to a team of employees in the maintenance, implementation or upgrades of all systems with a view of other areas impacting or being impacted by change. Ensure that application standards are followed, and that development, set-up/configuration, testing and data validation are completed successfully and on time. Develop and maintain training materials and conduct user training sessions to support system business demands including both functional, system and related business processes and procedures.
Project
Lead and Support
– Support Team Lead and the Project Manager in
d
eveloping and maintaining applicable project documentation that clearly defines what processes, functionality, timelines and results will be expected for each new functionality implementation or upgrade of the systems. Develop project plans and lead assigned operational projects.
Data Integrity and Report Development
- Develop and maintain data integrity standards using system audits and business process reviews.  Audit and review the system framework that supports business processes.  Prepare functional specifications in creating new reports and system enhancements. Capture, interpret and develop a detailed understanding of data reporting requirements to create and test standard and ad hoc queries and mass data extracts for data requests for often time sensitive and confidential data requests.
Compliance
- Maintain system documentation as it pertains to configuration, issue resolution, test plans, project decisions, standard operating procedures, data standards, processes, training and support.
Security
– Ensure security requests are actioned and analysed to ensure compliance with security strategy, related policies and audit assessments to safeguard the system and confidential business data. Evaluate all requested changes to ensure segregation of duties in business processes are not compromised. Includes processing daily access requests, regular system audits and escalations.
System Support
– Develop / configure / set-up / maintain functional application configuration and rules to ensure required functionality and reporting capability meets the needs of the Corporation and end users. Troubleshoot User and system issues, perform root cause analysis and document resolutions. Provide guidance, clarification and resolution to system issues.
System Administration
- Develop, maintain and audit system defined standards and processes. This includes ensuring batch job processing schedules, interfaces and integrations are processed in a timely manner to support time sensitive business processes. This also includes the setup and maintenance of system-wide installation, configuration settings, controls and security/privacy design. Ensure application data integrity, system access and data distribution managed appropriately. Investigate, analyze, design, test and recommend optimal system enhancements.

Education:
Degree/diploma in Business, Computers Science, Human Resource Management or equivalent
Experience
:
3 to 5 years experience in implementing and/or maintaining and supporting an enterprise scale WFM (including Time and Attendance / Time, Absence Management, Scheduling) and integrations with other internal and external applications such as Payroll, employee data whare houses, etc.
Minimum 3 to 5 years experience in translating enterprise business requirements into WFM (HR/Time and Attendance/Scheduling/Absence Management) application functionality, business processes and policy impacts
Strong knowledge of Human Resources, Payroll, Information Technology policies and practices with an ability to assess the impacts of policies and practices on related technologies supporting business processes
Other Skills and Assets:
Knowledge of Duty Rostering, Scheduling and Time Attendance Practices and Processes.
Strong project planning and project management skills with the ability to manage multiple concurrent projects that include cross-functional teams in different business units
Must be able to ensure Corporate standards are adhered to while maintaining confidentiality of HR / Payroll / Absence / Scheduling data
Experience in testing / quality assurance processes, test cycles, defect management, testing tools and test automation is an asset
Experience with Oracle-PeopleSoft Enterprise HRMS / HCM and/or Payroll, WorkforceSoftware (cloud solution) would be an asset
Municipal experience would be an asset
Experience working in a unionized environment ensuring application compliance with Collective Bargaining Agreements would be an asset
Demonstrated knowledge, experience and analytical skills as it pertains interpreting and analysing employee related business policy, practices and processes
Experience in business process mapping and redesign, relational database concepts, SQL query tools, data integrations, dashboarding tools and project management techniques
Exceptional written and verbal communication skills including the ability to deliver effective training and translate functional requirements for technical people and technical details to functional people, i.e. within own team, HR, Payroll, Functional Departments, Vendors and other Technical Teams
Proficient in the use of Microsoft Windows and Microsoft Office products including Excel, Word, PowerPoint Project and Visio

Responds to Occurrence Reports generated by the public, bylaw enforcement, police or fire prevention to Investigate fire damage and building impact/failure accidents to determine requirement for a building permit or unsafe condition.
Provide comments and input in the development of technical policies and procedures.
Make recommendations of acceptance or refusal on Alternative Solutions proposal by design professional, related to the Objective and Functional statements in the Building Code.
Requests information and/or additional documentation from manufacturers and testing agencies for verification and ruling, to resolve uncertainty with new products or systems as it relates to intended performance, Building Code requirements and suitable site condition application.

Maintains written documentation and records as required.

POSITION DUTIES:
Reporting to the Director, Cultural Services, this position provides senior-level strategic and operational leadership to advance the City of Brampton’s readiness for the future transfer of the Peel Art Gallery, Museum and Archives (PAMA), effective January 1, 2028, through the design and integration of a new Museums & Collections line of business.
The role operates within a multi-party governance structure where the PAMA Transition Board provides strategic direction and oversight, the Region of Peel maintains operational responsibility during the transition period, and external advisors (including KPMG) support operating model development.
Within this context, the position is accountable for leading the City’s internal planning, integration, and operational readiness work, translating Transition Board direction and consulting outputs into City-ready service models, implementation plans, and decision frameworks. The role ensures that the City is prepared to assume operations with a cohesive, financially sustainable, and operationally viable Museums & Collections service
Museums & Collections Strategy and Service Model Development
Lead the development of an integrated Museums & Collections service framework, including mandate, scope, and service delivery model
Define how PAMA, gallery and exhibition functions, heritage sites (including Bovaird House and Alderlea), and programming operate as a coordinated municipal service
Establish clear roles, relationships, and workflows between collections stewardship, curatorial practice, exhibitions, and public programming
Align the Museums & Collections service with existing Cultural Services lines of business while defining a distinct and sustainable service identity
Ensure alignment between external operating model work (including KPMG) and the City’s broader Cultural Services framework
Identify service delivery options, including governance considerations, programming approaches, and partnership opportunities
Develop long-term vision and positioning for municipal museum and gallery services in Brampton
Prepare briefing materials, business cases, and strategic recommendations for senior leadership and Council
Align work with broader corporate initiatives and transition-related studies
PAMA Transition Planning and Readiness
Lead Cultural Services’ role in transition planning to support the future transfer of PAMA
Translate Transition Board direction into actionable City requirements, including service delivery expectations and operational implications
Develop and maintain a City-focused transition roadmap, including key milestones leading to January 1, 2028
Identify and document readiness requirements, dependencies, and constraints across systems, staffing, and operations
Establish and monitor readiness frameworks and validation criteria to ensure preparedness for transfer
Identify, assess, and escalate risks to the City’s future assumption of operations, including financial, operational, and reputational risks
Coordinate cross-functional planning across Finance, HR, Legal, IT, Planning, Communications, and Facilities
Support development of implementation plans, timelines, and resource requirements
Provide ongoing updates, analysis, and advisory support to senior leadership
Bovaird House Collections and Strategic Positioning
Lead a comprehensive review of collections, assets, and current operations at Historic Bovaird House
Develop and oversee implementation of a collections management and rationalization strategy, including retention, deaccessioning, and transfer

Reporting to the Senior Project Advisor, Engineering, Construction and Transportation Management (ECTM), the Project Manager I is responsible for planning, coordination, and delivery of numerous capital municipal infrastructure projects. The role manages projects through the full lifecycle, including preliminary and detailed design, approvals, procurement, construction, commissioning, warranty and closeout. Projects may include water and wastewater linear infrastructure, transportation improvements, wastewater pump stations, waste management infrastructure, water booster stations and reservoirs.
Duties & Responsibilities
Plans and manages the delivery of capital projects, primarily state of good repair work, from initiation to preliminary and detailed design, permitting, property and utility coordination, procurement, construction, warranty and ultimately closeout.
Leads procurement of consulting engineering services through Request for Quotations (RFQ) and Request for Proposals (RFP) and contracting services through Request for Prequalification (RFPQ) and Request for Tender (RFT) processes. Participates in evaluation, contract award, negotiation, and contract administration activities.
Co-ordinates, manages and leads consultants, contractors, and various other vendors to successfully deliver capital projects. This includes regular reporting, formal and informal meetings, vendor performance reviews, and utilization of various project management tools as required.
Manages all aspects of assigned projects including, but not limited to, scope, budget, schedule, contract administration, change management, risk, and quality. Utilizes project management plans, risk registrars, schedules, project charters, change management documentation, and tracking logs to support project delivery.
Builds and maintains working relationships with internal stakeholders, external agencies, utility providers, property owners, consultants, contractors, and regulatory authorities to facilitate successful project delivery.
Conducts quality assurance of project deliverables through including, but not limited to, design review workshops, budgeting, risk management and constructability reviews.
Ensures all necessary regulatory approvals and permits are in place prior to tendering, along with properties and utility relocations.
With the assistance of senior staff, represents Halton Region at public consultations, presentations, open houses, and face-to-face interactions with the public, contractors, and regulatory agencies.
Researches into and recommends innovative technologies, techniques and materials in the design and construction of water, wastewater, stormwater and transportation infrastructure.
Ensures the full involvement and collaboration of client divisions and supporting departments throughout project delivery, including infrastructure & environmental services, water/wastewater operations, system services, development services, asset management, and road operations. This also includes coordination with internal ECTM groups such as surveying, inspections, and the Engineering Management Office (EMO).
Ensures that the works are designed and constructed in compliance with the RFP and tender contract documents.
Participates as a contributor in the value engineering exercises to ensure all infrastructure meets its intended functions in accordance with the project scope.
Ensures that any project inquiries received from the public or other relevant stakeholders are resolved in a timely manner.

Job Summary
Reporting to the Deputy Chief/Manager of Logistics, the Paramedic Services Logistics Superintendent provides leadership, oversight and strategic direction for the delivery of logistics services supporting frontline paramedic operations.  This position leads a team of Logistics Officers and is responsible for the effective management of procurement, inventory, equipment, medications and fleet support while ensuring operational readiness, regulatory compliance and service excellence.
Duties & Responsibilities
Leading and supervising a team of Logistic Officers responsible for the distribution of medical supplies, equipment, linens, medications, and controlled substances to 15 stations, 4 hospitals and over 50 frontline paramedic vehicles.
Providing leadership in workforce management and development, including scheduling, performance oversight, staff development, and the promotion of a safe and healthy work environment.
Overseeing the procurement of all necessary supplies, equipment, medications, and uniforms; collaborates with Supply Chain Management and Finance to support procurement processes and evaluations and vendor management.
Ensuring compliance with the Ministry of Health Land Ambulance Certification Standards, Health Canada requirements, the Controlled Drugs and Substances Act and other applicable regulations governing equipment, medications, preventative maintenance, and inventory security.
Collaboration with Energy, Fleet and Facilities, Architects, Contractors and other stakeholders to support in the design, oversight and construction of paramedic response stations, and logistical support facilities and explore energy savings/green facility initiatives including furniture and IT requirements.
Supporting and collaborating closely with the Paramedic Fleet Coordinator on vehicle-related matters and vehicle equipment, including procurement of vehicles, equipment, and the maintenance, installation and replacement of patient equipment and technology.
Duties and Responsibilities Continued
Providing operational advice, updates and recommendations to the Deputy Chief of Logistics.
Monitoring industry trends and making recommendations based on research regarding changes to vehicle and equipment design features, supplies, and paramedic station facilities.
Building and maintaining ongoing relationships with stakeholders and vendors, ensuring timely communication and addressing operational concerns.
Representing Halton Region on provincial (Provincial Paramedic Logistics Working Group) and divisional (Uniform and Equipment Advisory) committees and panels.
Responsible for the preparation, retention and submission of all equipment and facility-related information for the tri-annual Ministry of Health Ambulance Service Review.
Skills & Qualifications
Degree or Diploma in Supply Chain Management or an equivalent combination of education and three (3) to five (5) years of supervisory experience working in an inventory management, logistics or supply chain environment, preferably within a healthcare environment.
Strong leadership and organizational skills, including workforce scheduling, project planning, resource management, knowledge of procurement and evaluation processes, and budget and financial planning.
Demonstrated knowledge of supply chain management, inventory control, procurement processes, vendor evaluation and budget administration.
Experience coordinating equipment preventative maintenance and repair programs.
Proficiency with MS Office including Teams, Excel, Outlook, and Word.
Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal.
Strong time management skills and ability to manage workflow in order to complete work on time and as expected.
Excellent communication, interpersonal and relationship-building skills, with the ability to work effectively in both a team environment and independently.

Knowledge and understanding of the Ministry of Health Provincial Equipment Standards for Ontario Ambulance Services.

Job Summary
Reporting to the Manager, Engineering Management Office (EMO), The Project Manager III serves as a strategic leader within the Engineering Management Office, driving the successful execution of complex and transformative projects that advance the priorities of Engineering Construction and Transportation Division. This role is accountable for leading projects of significant strategic importance, advancing service excellence, and driving organizational performance through the development, implementation, maintenance, and optimization of project / service delivery frameworks, processes, tools, templates, and best practices for linear infrastructure capital projects and road operations. The Project Manager III oversees the Project and Service Delivery Management Systems, ensuring their effectiveness, continuous improvement, and alignment with divisional objectives, while promoting consistent application across the organization. The position also provides oversight, and assurance of compliance with established project delivery processes, governance frameworks, and best practices to drive successful, efficient, and predictable project outcomes. The incumbent fosters cross-functional collaboration, strengthens project governance, and enables the consistent, efficient, and successful delivery of linear capital projects and road operations.
Duties & Responsibilities
Lead, manage, and deliver complex, high-profile, and strategically significant projects and initiatives from concept through implementation, ensuring alignment with divisional objectives, approved scope, budget, schedule, risk, and quality requirements.
Provide project leadership and expert advice to multidisciplinary teams, ensuring effective collaboration, stakeholder engagement, issue resolution, and achievement of project outcomes.
Develop, implement, maintain, and continuously improve project and service delivery frameworks, methodologies, standards, processes, procedures, tools, templates, policies, and work instructions to support the consistent and efficient delivery of capital projects and operational programs.
Serve as the business owner and administrator for Project and Service Delivery Management Systems, ensuring system effectiveness, data integrity, continuous enhancement, user adoption, and alignment with organizational objectives and industry best practices.
Establish, maintain, monitor, and continuously improve project, program, and portfolio governance frameworks to ensure compliance with approved methodologies, standards, policies, procedures, and reporting requirements throughout the project lifecycle.
Lead compliance monitoring, quality assurance reviews, audits, and performance assessments to verify consistent application of established project delivery processes, governance practices, and organizational standards across Engineering Construction and Road Operations.
Review existing project delivery and operational practices, identify opportunities for improvement, and implement evidence-based solutions that enhance efficiency, effectiveness, accountability, and service outcomes while balancing the needs of diverse stakeholder groups.
Lead and facilitate cross-divisional and cross-departmental continuous improvement initiatives, business transformation projects, and process re-engineering efforts that support operational excellence and organizational maturity.
Establish, monitor, and continuously enhance project, program, and service delivery performance measurement frameworks, including key performance indicators (KPIs), dashboards, reporting processes, and performance monitoring systems.

Position / Responsibilities
Reporting to the CAO, the Fire Chief is accountable for the overall senior leadership, strategic direction, and coordination of all sections within Whitby Fire & Emergency Services. The Fire Chief ensures the Fire Department operations continue to deliver exceptional customer service in the areas of public education, prevention, suppression and rescue services to the citizens of the Town of Whitby. The Fire Chief also oversees all staff training, and overall emergency management. The Fire Chief appropriately balances the delivery of emergency services with taxpayers’ funding of services across the municipality.
This position is a member of the Senior Leadership Team which is responsible for moving forward the objectives of the CAO and Mayor and Council. In addition, the Fire Chief is required to ensure compliance and enforcement of all applicable statutes, by-laws and regulations related to the municipality and the fire service.
Finally, the Fire Chief is responsible for acting as the “Assistant to the Fire Marshal” with respect to the Fire Protection and Prevention Act; “Chief Fire Official” with respect to the Ontario Fire Code; “Authority having jurisdiction” with respect to applicable portions of the Building Code.
Overall duties and responsibilities of the Fire Chief must remain in alignment with requirements under various legislative bodies, including but not limited to the Fire Protection and Prevention Act, 1997, the Occupational Health and Safety Act, 1990, Employment Standards Act, 2000, and applicable collective agreements.
The compensation range for the role is $203,386 - $231,121 per year and this advertisement is to fill a vacancy.
Candidate Requirements
The ideal candidate will hold a Post Secondary Education Diploma/Degree in Fire Service(s), Business Administration, Public Administration or related discipline, or equivalent combination of education and progressively responsible work experience. They will be a graduate from the Ontario Fire College, with completion of all legislatively required training, including but not limited to the Company Officer Program and hold a Community Emergency Management Coordinator (CEMC) professional designation. Completion of executive Chief Fire Officer (ECFO) professional designation and Completion of NFPA 1021 – Fire Officer 4 are considered assets.
The ideal candidate will bring a minimum of twelve (12) years of progressively responsible experience in the fire service industry; and a minimum of five (5) years of senior leadership experience in the fire service working within a complex unionized environment. A combination of equivalent experience and education may be considered. Extensive and progressive training as a Firefighter, Training Officer, Fire Prevention Officer and/or Senior Suppression Officer in the fire service is required.

2. Market intelligence, economic analysis, and competitiveness research; and
3. Economic development marketing, digital engagement, and growth of the InvestMilton brand.

Leads meetings, event coordination and represents the Town at industry events, conferences, investment and trade initiatives, as required
Collaborates with the departmental and corporate internal staff to support inquiries and special projects
Market Intelligence, Competitiveness & Economic Analysis
Leads implementation of market intelligence plan and data strategy for division in alignment with Milton’s Economic Strategic Plan
Develops economic reporting dashboard leveraging PowerBI and other similar digital tools to support Milton Economic Development Advisory Board Updates, Council and internal memos, reports, presentations and events

Develops and contributes content, property information, key data and business stories for InvestMilton digital channels with help from departmental staff

Manages all website content with help from EDO’s, including property listings, community statistics/data, business support resources and digital mapping tools with help of departmental staff
Leads the development and implementation of annual Economic Development Action Plan and facilitates activities, initiatives, events and partnerships required to forward the goals of Milton’s Economic Strategy
Monitors and analyzes performance metrics to assess progress against the Economic Strategy and Action Plans, identifies opportunities for improvement, and adjusts activities as needed to achieve objectives
Project manages creation of the Economic Development Annual Report and supports development of other key marketing and digital promotional materials that advance divisional strategic objectives
Corporate, Strategic & Financial Support
Tracks and forecasts non-residential development in collaboration with Planning department to aid in determining the anticipated non-residential impacts for corporate budget and annual reporting

Minimum Qualifications
Degree in Urban/Economic Geography, Business, Marketing, Public Administration, Economics, Environmental Studies or Planning
7 years of experience in Economic Development or related field
Post-secondary training in Digital Marketing or Digital Data Tools and Analysis used in Economic Development considered an asset
Previous experience developing and implementing Economic Development strategies and action plans
Demonstrated business development and client relationship management experience, with the ability to establish, cultivate, and maintain productive relationships with business leaders, investors, developers, site selectors, industry associations, and community partners to advance Economic Development objectives.

The City of Markham is consistently ranked among Canada’s top municipal employers. Reporting to the Supervisor, Building Inspections and the Supervisor, Special Investigations, you will conduct site inspections of residential construction, including building, HVAC, plumbing and on-site sewage systems, to ensure compliance with the Ontario Building Code, Municipal By-laws and other applicable legislation. You will perform administrative duties related to the review, monitoring and closure of open building permits, investigate suspected illegal occupancy of new homes, issue field inspection reports, and support enforcement activities in accordance with established practices. The successful candidate will possess strong knowledge of residential construction and be capable of conducting inspections independently with minimal supervision to support the reduction of inspection backlogs and open permit inventories.

Investigate and conduct all Building Code construction inspections related to housing projects
Conduct inspections of on-site sewage (septic) systems to verify compliance with the Ontario Building Code and applicable legislation.
Review suspected illegal occupancies and issue Orders, notices and other compliance documents in accordance with applicable legislation and departmental practices.
Investigate open permits and issue Orders, notices and related compliance documents in accordance with the Building Code Act, Building By-law, applicable legislation and established departmental practices.
Qualifications
College diploma in Architecture, Architectural Technology, Civil Engineering Technology, Building Science, Construction Engineering Technology or a related discipline.
Eligible for membership in AATO or OACETT.
Minimum four (4) years of experience in municipal building services, building inspections, permit administration, code enforcement, or residential construction.
Possess a valid Building Code Identification Number (BCIN) with minimum qualifications in:
General Legal/Process
House 2012
Plumbing – House
HVAC – House
On-Site Sewage Systems
Part 3 Building Code qualifications are considered an asset.
Demonstrated knowledge of the Ontario Building Code, Building Code Act, applicable legislation and municipal by-laws.
Experience reviewing and facilitating the closure of open building permits.
Ability to conduct residential building inspections, issue Orders and compliance notices, and make code compliance decisions
Ability to read and interpret plans, specifications and construction drawings
Excellent communication, customer service and organizational skills.
Good computer skills.
Valid Ontario Class G Driver's license and use of personal vehicle for business purposes required. Monthly vehicle allowance provided.

Responds positively and professionally to change and helps others through change.

Communicates in a clear, professional and respectful way; demonstrates active listening.

Demonstrates ethical behaviour and accountability, aligns with City values, and abides by relevant policies and legislation.

the consistent delivery of high-quality efficient and customer-centric service that exceeds expectations.

Job Summary
The Health & Safety Coordinator is responsible for supporting the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of the City’s occupational health and safety programs and systems.
This role provides support to ensure compliance with applicable health and safety legislation, while advancing a proactive safety culture focused on prevention, risk reduction, and employee well‑being.
Working in a complex, multi‑site, project‑driven, and unionized environment, the Coordinator partners with the People Services team, City leaders, Employees, multiple Joint Health & Safety Committees, contractors, and external stakeholders to drive effective safety practices, manage workplace incidents and claims, and deliver impactful training and programs across the organization.
Key Duties and Responsibilities
Health & Safety Compliance
Support the development, implementation, review, and continuous improvement of the City’s health and safety programs, policies, procedures, standards, and safe work practices.
Contribute to the evolution of the City’s health and safety management system and overall safety strategy.
Ensure organizational compliance with the Occupational Health and Safety Act (OHSA), Workplace Safety and Insurance Act (WSIA), and related legislation.
Coordinate and support health and safety programs, including workplace inspections, hazard assessments, contractor safety, confined space entry, workplace violence prevention, and first aid compliance.
Conduct compliance audits and gap assessments to ensure adherence to OHSA, applicable regulations, standards, and corporate requirements.
Monitor legislative changes, emerging trends, and best practices, recommending program enhancements to maintain compliance and support continuous improvement.
Risk Management & Incident Prevention (Operational)
Conduct workplace inspections, audits, hazard assessments, and job hazard analyses across municipal facilities, operational worksites, and active project/construction sites.
Lead or support incident, injury, and near‑miss investigations, including root‑cause analysis and corrective action implementation.
Where needed, support leadership to verify contractor compliance with municipal safety expectations, project‑specific requirements, and regulatory obligations
Coordinate occupational hygiene and exposure monitoring initiatives (noise, chemical, biological, ergonomic, indoor air quality).
Support emergency preparedness planning, drills, and response activities.
Provide advice to leaders, project managers, and employees on hazard identification, risk mitigation, and safe work procedures.
Training, Education & Culture
Identify legislated training requirements and support organization‑wide compliance with mandatory training programs.
Develop, coordinate, and deliver health and safety training programs, including orientations, project‑site safety briefings, and instructor‑led sessions.
Promote a culture of safety through engagement, communication, and awareness initiatives.
Support continuous improvement of learning systems and training compliance tracking.
Committees & Stakeholder Collaboration
Provide leadership and coordination support to multiple Joint Health & Safety Committees (JHSCs), including inspections, meetings, and follow‑up actions.
Act as a technical resource to JHSCs and departmental leaders regarding legislative requirements and health and safety best practices.
Support departmental leaders in meeting their due diligence and health and safety responsibilities.
Build effective relationships with employees, unions, supervisors, contractors, and external partners.
Wellness & Organizational Support
Support programs related to psychological health and safety, workplace violence and harassment prevention, and employee wellness.
Reporting & Analytics
Maintain safety data, documentation, and records required to demonstrate legislative compliance and due diligence.
Track and report on leading and lagging health and safety performance indicators.
Monitor compliance trends and prepare recommendations to improve organizational performance.
Prepare reports, dashboards, and analysis to support decision‑making and continuous improvement.
WSIB & Disability Management
Support the People Services team and the Occupational Health & Safety Nurse to coordinate WSIB claims management, including reporting, documentation, and case management.
Support the People Services team and the Occupational Health & Safety Nurse to facilitate return‑to‑work and modified‑duty planning in collaboration with key stakeholders.
Analyze and report back findings to the People Services Team and the Occupational Health & Safety Nurse the WSIB trends and performance metrics to identify opportunities for prevention and improvement.

Health and Safety diploma or equivalent
Minimum 5 years of progressive experience in occupational health and safety.
Experience in a municipal sector, construction, or unionized broader public‑sector environment is strongly preferred.
Demonstrated experience in:
Leading inspections, audits, and investigations
Supporting or advising multi‑site Joint Health & Safety Committees
Developing and delivering health and safety training programs
WSIB claims management and return‑to‑work coordination
Supporting safety on construction or capital project sites
Strong experience applying Ontario health and safety legislation in a complex environment.

OHSA and applicable regulations

Human Rights Code and duty to accommodate

title: Project Manager, Information Technology (Temp up to 24 months)
description:
We’re looking for a Project Manager, Information Technology (Temporary up to 24 months) to join Clarington’s Finance and Technology Department!
Why Clarington?
Clarington is a community full of possibilities.
As one of the fastest-growing municipalities in Durham Region, Clarington is home to over 107,000 residents across four urban centres and 14 hamlets. With our population expected to double by 2051, Clarington offers a perfect blend of urban living and small-town charm. We’re known for our thriving energy and agricultural sectors, vibrant historic downtowns, and exceptional quality of life.
Our team thrives in a collaborative environment that promotes work-life balance and meaningful community impact. We value accountability, integrity, and respect, and we are deeply committed to fostering equity, inclusion, and diversity in the workplace. Together, we’re building a stronger Clarington — for today and for future generations.
The future is bright – and working with the Municipality of Clarington means you can help shape it. How will you make your mark?
About the Role
Vacancy Statement:
Unless specifically stated, all job postings at the Municipality of Clarington are to fill existing vacancies within our organization.
Work Model:
Hybrid
Reporting directly to the Chief Information Officer, with a dotted-line relationship to the Supervisor, Business Development and the Deputy CAO/Treasurer, this position is responsible for supporting the project lifecycle for Clarington’s implementation of a new Microsoft Dynamics 365 Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) solution, replacing the Municipality’s legacy finance and operations systems.
Key Responsibilities
Lead the full project lifecycle for Clarington’s implementation of Microsoft Dynamics 365, from charter and business case through design, build, go-live and post-implementation review.
Develop, participate and assist in procurement (NRFP/RFP or Cooperative Agreement, evaluation, assist with negotiations, contract logistics) in partnership with Municipality’s procurement team while following Clarington’s by-laws.
Serve as a point of accountability for scope, schedule, tracking and reporting on project budget, risk and quality, including budget submissions and financial reporting for each phase of the program.
Coordinate cross-functional teams spanning Finance, IT, Human Resources/Payroll, Procurement, operating departments, the implementation partner and vendor resources; chair steering and working groups; prepare Council and executive updates.
Oversee technical readiness (environment provisioning, integrations and interfaces, data migration and cleansing from legacy systems, cybersecurity, cut-over, testing, and contingency planning).
Manage functional workstreams across general ledger, accounts payable and receivable, budgeting, procurement, project and grant accounting, asset management and financial reporting, including business process re-engineering and the secondment of subject matter experts.
Ensure knowledge transfer to internal staff, producing robust documentation, SOPs and training that strengthen Clarington’s long-term ERP capabilities.
Embed continuous improvement, capturing lessons learned and identifying future enhancements (e.g., human resources and payroll, asset management, analytics).
Champion data-security and privacy by ensuring all project artefacts remain within Clarington-controlled systems.
Drive parallel finance modernization workstreams such as chart of accounts redesign, retirement of manual and spreadsheet-based processes, integration with the Dynamics 365 CRM platform, and reporting and business intelligence.
Coordinate technology dependencies pertinent to the ERP migration, including licensing, environments, server, storage and cloud services, working with Infrastructure & Security and Client & Application Services teams to minimize downtime.
Contribute to PMO best practices, creating templates, dashboards, and knowledge-transfer sessions that strengthen Clarington’s project-delivery maturity long term.
Advise departmental leaders on scoping, budgeting, and prioritizing future technology initiatives that align with the municipality’s IT Strategy (Strengthen, Innovate, Transform).
Develop change-management and training plans, ensuring end-users adopt new tools and workflows effectively across Finance & Technology and all operating departments.
Provide executive-level reporting, distilling complex schedules, risks, and financials into clear updates for Council, senior leadership, and internal stakeholders.
What you bring
University degree in Business Administration, Computer Science, Information Systems, Accounting, Project Management or related discipline.
Project Management Professional (PMP) Certification is required.
Minimum 3 years’ progressive IT project-management experience delivering complex, multi-stakeholder technology projects.
Proven success leading large-scale RFPs and contract negotiations in a municipal or broader public-sector setting.
Hands-on experience delivering ERP or enterprise financial system implementations, preferably Microsoft Dynamics 365 (Finance & Operations or Business Central).
Demonstrated ability to monitor project budgets and to work with leaders, executives and/or stakeholders.
ITIL, Agile/Scrum or Prosci Change Management certifications is an asset.
Microsoft Dynamics 365 certifications, or experience with ERP implementation methodologies such as Microsoft Success by Design, is an asset.
Expert grasp of project-management methodologies (Agile & Waterfall) and tools (MS Project, Teams, Azure DevOps).
Understanding of public sector procurement legislation, public-sector governance, and municipal financial processes and reporting standards (PSAB).
Excellent communication, written and verbal, facilitation and vendor-management skills.
Advanced analytical, risk-management and report-writing abilities.
Must be legally able to work in Canada and able to obtain/maintain a satisfactory Criminal Reference Check.

Key Responsibilities
Controlling the flow of traffic to allow for the safe, supervised crossing of students and pedestrians.
Communicating clearly and effectively using spoken commands and hand signals.
Instructing students and other pedestrians in safe crossing procedures.

Good Vision – you must be able to see vehicles, different colours (stoplights), children and signal indications from close and far distances.

Rate of pay: $557.36 bi-weekly (2026 rate)

Rain suit and other equipment provided.

title: Tree Planting Project Technician - Contract
description:
Reporting to the Manager, Environment and Climate, the Tree Planting Project Technician will support tree planting projects on Town-owned land, including along road rights-of-way and in parks. The Tree Planting Project Technician will bring their technical tree and environmental knowledge to identify and map potential tree planting locations, support tree planting contract management, conduct tree inventory data collection, and manage/analyze related spatial data.
The Technician will also play a key role in engaging with the public, businesses, and community groups to collaborate on tree planting initiatives, increase awareness of the benefits of trees, and share information on how the community can plant, care for, and protect trees. As needed, the Technician will support other environmental projects to help advance the Town’s vision as a nature-rich community and support implementation of the Town’s Strategic Plan. This role will spend about half the time working on-site and engaging with the community and partners, and the other half will be office.
Accountabilities
:
Comply with corporate and departmental policies and procedures.
Ensure a high degree of service for both internal and external customers in accordance with Town standards.
Identify and map potential tree planting locations on Town-owned land, primarily along road rights-of-way and in parks.
Complete site assessments of potential planting locations including assessing soil type, collecting soil samples, and checking for above- and below-ground conflicts, such as utilities.
Recommend suitable tree species based on site conditions.
Consult with other staff/departments as appropriate to confirm suitability of planting locations.
Engage regularly with residents, businesses and community groups/organizations to identify potential planting sites, share information about the benefits of trees, communicate upcoming tree planting & management activities, and promote best practices for tree planting and care.
Assist with planting contractor management, such as providing planting location instruction, follow-up inspections, and on- or off-site support as needed.
Collect inventory data for trees, other green infrastructure assets, and invasive species, as assigned, using a tablet and hand-held GPS receiver.
Manage spatial data and ensure data quality through data review and following up on deficiencies.
Support community groups leading naturalization plantings on Town land and maintain regular communication with the group lead.
Assess naturalization planting locations for required site prep and coordinate associated activities.
Support (on site) during naturalization planting activities/events, as needed.
Assist with the development of the Town’s Green Infrastructure Asset Management Plan as needed, such as support with asset inventories, mapping, data analysis, etc.
Assist with other environmental stewardship projects as needed, such as invasive species management projects, Privately Owned Tree Management Strategy actions, developing communication content, conducting research, supporting grant applications, biodiversity projects, etc.
Support environmental community outreach and engagement programs, as needed.
Perform other job-related duties as assigned.
Qualifications:
Post-secondary degree or diploma in Forestry, Urban Forestry, Arboriculture, Natural Resource Management, Forest Conservation, or a related discipline, or the equivalent in combined education and experience
ISA certified arborist is considered an asset
Minimum of 1 year’s work experience in urban forestry, forestry, arboriculture or a directly related field.
Excellent tree identification skills, knowledge of native tree species and common tree pests and diseases and understanding of tree biology.
Applied knowledge of tree planting and care best practices.
Knowledge and understanding of invasive species, soils, and ecology in Ontario.
Strong research and analytical skills.
Excellent organizational, project management, time management and problem-solving skills.
Ability to work independently, multi-task and prioritize work to meet project deadlines.
Working knowledge of computer software and techniques applicable to the areas of inventory databases, such as Access or ArcGIS to create and maintain an inventory database.
Experience working with the public or community groups through collaborative projects and/or engagement and outreach.
Proficient in the use of MS Office (e.g. Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook).
Class G Driver license in good standing and reliable vehicle to use occasionally on corporate business.
Compensation:
The compensation rate for this temporary contract position is $32.27 - $38.41 (35 hours per week). Duration of Contract is approximately twelve (12) months, with the possibility to extend.
Location:
This position allows a blend of working onsite and remotely based on the needs of the business, in accordance with the Town’s Work from Home Policy, and as subject to change. This position will also require some flexibility in the incumbent’s availability and work schedule.
Application:
Qualified candidates may submit a detailed cover letter and resume as a single document, sent in confidence to the Town by 4:30 p.m., October 16, 2026. Please quote
posting 202660
on your cover letter.
We thank all those who apply but advise that only those applicants selected for an interview will be contacted. The Town of Halton Hills is an equal opportunity employer. Accommodations are available for all parts of the recruitment process. If contacted for an interview, please advise the Human Resources staff of any measures you feel you need to enable you to be assessed in a fair and equitable manner. Information received relating to accommodation measures will be addressed confidentially.
Personal information is collected under the authority of the Municipal Act, 2001 (S.O. 2001, c.25) and will be used to select a candidate. Questions about this collection should be directed to the Director of Human Resources.

Reporting to the Maintenance Supervisor, this position is being offered as a full-time permanent staff compliment to the Transit Department (Maintenance Division). Duties will include but not be restricted to:
Lays out, builds, tests, troubleshoots, repairs and modifies developmental and production electronic components, parts, equipment, and systems, such as Smartbus technologies, destination signs, communication equipment, fare collection equipment and other Transit related equipment and systems.

Diagnose electrical problems and simulate conditions.
Repair test equipment as required.

description:
