Comprehensive health plan complemented with life and disability insurance
A progressive work environment that promotes a work/life balance and strives to be a great place for great people to do great things
What can I expect to do in this role?
Reporting to the Manager, Works Operations, the Supervisor, Works Contracted Services is responsible for providing expert guidance and contract oversight across the Town’s right-of-way maintenance operational contracts and small capital infrastructure rehabilitation initiatives, while ensuring these are delivered within approved scope, schedule, budget, quality and the Town’s safety requirements.
In this role, you will:
Oversees the successful delivery of the Town’s right-of-way operational contracts (i.e. Winter Control, loose-leaf collection, yearly sidewalk replacement program, etc.) and small capital rehabilitation projects (i.e. minor storm sewer replacements, retaining walls, bridge repairs and multi-use pathways) from planning through completion.
Ensures operational and capital budget delivery and compliance, and that projects stay within approved budget while following municipal rules, provincial laws, and applicable regulations.
Prepares and develops contracts, scope, drawings, specifications, and contract conditions.
Oversees procurement planning, prepares and awards tenders, prepares project award reports, and assists with tender documentation, scopes of work, contract negotiation and contractor evaluations.
Provides leadership, oversight, and support to staff undertaking contract administration activities, including contractor management, compliance monitoring, dispute resolution, change control, claims management, payment approvals and project closeouts.
Provides oversight and guidance on the review of engineering designs for Regional, Town, and external stakeholder projects (i.e. Metrolinx, developments) to ensure functionality, operational requirements, and operational maintenance standards can be met.
Oversees roadway patrol and sidewalk inspection programs to ensure compliance with Ontario Minimum Maintenance Standards (O.Reg. 239/02) and maintain accurate, defensible records for claims management.
Leads and develops a multidisciplinary team of Project Leaders, Inspectors, Operations Technologists and Infrastructure Technicians through strategic workload planning, performance management, mentorship including performance assessment, and career/skillset development initiatives.
Supports workforce planning through recruitment, onboarding, training, coaching, and maintenance of job documentation.
Provides operational leadership and technical support, including staff coverage, after-hours standby participation, acting for the Manager during absences, and representing the Town in claims-related matters.
Supports in identifying and implementing improvements to operational practices, contract delivery, and service performance, while maintaining industry partnerships and engagement.
Serves as a primary representative for Works Operations customer complaints, escalated service requests, Council inquiries and stakeholder concerns.
Performs other duties as assigned.
How do I qualify?
Diploma in Civil Engineering Technology, Construction Engineering Technology, or a related technical discipline, combined with a Certified Engineering Technologist (C.E.T.) designation. A Bachelor of Engineering (B.Eng.) or Bachelor of Architecture (B.Arch.) degree would be considered an asset.
Minimum 8 years of progressively responsible experience in municipal, provincial, or private sector infrastructure construction, maintenance, and rehabilitation program delivery, including contract preparation, procurement/tendering, contract administration, and design review.
Experience in managing right-of-way projects including asphalt applications, stormwater management, concrete surfaces and other municipal or infrastructure operations maintenance activities.
Experience with winter operations, loose leaf collections, or other operations and maintenance programs is an asset.
Experience leading teams responsible for infrastructure construction, maintenance or operational programs.
Proven ability to manage projects and supervise staff across all areas of infrastructure construction, maintenance, and operations.
Exceptional interpersonal, communication and customer service skills, with a commitment to delivering a positive customer experience, building trust with the public or other departments, and resolving complex issues in a respectful, factual, timely and professional manner. Effective stakeholder engagement is a key performance expectation of the role.
Experience managing the work of contractors, consultants and external stakeholders while supervising technical and operational staff.
Strong understanding of seasonal operational demands, safety standards, and regulatory compliance
Strong knowledge of municipal infrastructure maintenance, procurement and tendering practices, contract administration, service performance monitoring, Ontario Minimum Maintenance Standards (O.Reg. 239/02), and applicable legislation, regulations and industry standards.
Demonstrated ability to interpret engineering drawings, specifications, contracts and technical documentation.
Ability to apply technical expertise in support of legal proceedings, claims investigations and discoveries.
Knowledge of the Municipal Act, the Building Code (i.e. roadside asset portion), the Ontario Provincial Standards of Design, and the Ontario Provincial Standard Specifications.
Strong leadership, communication, negotiation, organizational, analytical and problem-solving skills.
Proficient use of software/technology such as Microsoft Project, Builterra or equivalent contractor management technologies.
Availability to participate in after-hours support as required for significant weather events or major emergencies.
A valid and unrestricted Ontario Driver’s Licence Class G is required with a driving record that demonstrates responsible and safe driving behaviour. Note: Applicants with 6 or more points are ineligible for consideration. Successful applicants will be required to provide the Corporation with a copy of their driver’s licence and a current driver’s abstract (no older than 30 days from their offer date) and will be required to pass a Town administered road test as a condition of employment.

Strategic Thinking
– innovating through analysis and ideas
Engagement
– mobilizing people, organizations, partners
Management excellence
– delivering results through action management, people management and financial and asset management
Accountability and Respect

The Toronto Police Service is looking for a candidate that shares our corporate values:
Service at our Core Do the right thing Connect with Compassion Reflect and Grow
The Toronto Police Service is the fourth largest municipal police service in North America. With over 5,000 officers and approximately 2,500 civilian employees, we are dedicated to delivering best-in-class police services, in partnership with our communities, by being where the public needs the Service the most, by embracing partnerships to create safe communities, and by focusing on the needs of the City.
The Opportunity:
Are you passionate about Human Resources, do you have strong organizational and customer service skills combined with the ability to work under multiple timelines? If this sounds like you, we have an excellent opportunity as an Employee Services Representative.
What can I expect to do in this role?
In this role, you will provide first point of contact support to Uniform and Civilian members of the Service for inquiries within the scope of payroll, benefits and human resources through written and verbal communication channels. The Employee Services Representative ensures that all members of the Toronto Police Service and external contacts receive Human Resource support, while prioritizing issue resolution via investigation, problem solving and collective agreement alignment to ensure a positive member experience.
Duties and Responsibilities:
Performs data entry and/or other administrative activities as required to process timely payroll, benefit and other HR related transactions to members or to ensure timely updates to the system.
Maintains up to date and accurate records related to member processing and relevant transactions, electronically, within applicable systems or online files, and/or in paper files, as required by appropriate policy, processes and procedures.
Follows up on paperwork and/or missing information.
Executes routine system and/or process steps, per pre-defined schedule to meet business objectives/requirements such as uniform and civilian reclassifications, promotions etc.
Generates/develops routine reports to various customers/clients.
Identifies and resolves basic, routine issues.
Actions and responds to routine customer/client inquiries and requests for service via phone, email and other means, ensuring service levels and performance standards are achieved.
Liaises/follows up with customers/clients as required to gather information, or communicate status, and/or issues.
Issues/distributes information, accesses systems/records, and generates responses based on defined policies or processes.
Collates information and reviews data as required to support routine administrative processes or responds to customer/client inquiries.
Escalates non routine issues as required based on protocol defined.
Updates and maintains call tracking logs as indicated by Unit specific procedures.
Performs administrative office duties:
Opens and sorts mail, files and purges records, creates, copies and distributes documents, scans paper files and documents.
Schedules and coordinates activities, events, correspondence, meetings as required to support Employee Service Centre service levels.
Generates and/or distributes routine correspondence to clients and customers.
Performs all other duties, functions and assignments inherent to the position.
Education & Experience:
A minimum of Grade 12 education, or an approved equivalent combination of education, training, and experience.
A minimum of 2 years in human resources, with experience supporting a Benefits and Payroll function.
Preferred requirements:
Post-secondary education (degree, diploma or certificate) in Payroll, Benefits or Human Resources
Experience working in a multi-union payroll environment.
Experience in the municipal/public sector.
Experience with Oracle/PeopleSoft Human Resource Management Systems.
Skills & Competencies:
Excellent administrative and organizational skills combined with good interpersonal skills.
Working knowledge of MS Office suite.
Good customer service and oral and written communication skills.
Ability to work in a team environment.
Works well under well-defined rules, processes, and under tight timelines and stress that can come from unpredictable support volumes.
Analysis and problem-solving skills.
Ability to adapt to changing priorities

Six (6) months.

description:
Posting Title: Special Constable
Job ID #: 8058
Status: Regular Full-Time
Salary: $89,320 - $102,278
Shifts: Rotating Shifts
Hours: 40.00
Location: City of Toronto (Location TBA)
Vacancies:
Several 2027 Intake
Job Code: C62S1Z Class 6 (40)
Opening Date: September 28, 2026
Must Apply By: October 16, 2026
The Toronto Police Service is looking for a candidate that shares our core values:
Service at our Core Do the right thing Connect with Compassion Reflect and Grow
The Toronto Police Service is the fourth largest municipal police service in North America. With over 5,000 officers and approximately 2,500 civilian employees, we are dedicated to delivering best-in-class police services, in partnership with our communities, by being where the public needs the Service the most, by embracing partnerships to create safe communities, and by focusing on the needs of the City.
We are hiring Special Constables:
The Toronto Police Service is now accepting applications for anticipated 2027 Special Constable hiring requirements. We are seeking dedicated, community-focused individuals who are committed to promoting safety, professionalism, and public trust across the City of Toronto.
About the Role:
Special Constables play an essential role in supporting public safety and enhancing community well-being. This position requires strong communication skills, sound judgement, and the ability to remain calm, effective, and respectful in fast-paced and dynamic environments.
What We re Looking For
We invite applicants who demonstrate:
Excellent interpersonal and communication skills
The ability to multi-task and remain composed under pressure
Professionalism, maturity, and integrity in all interactions
Strong decision-making skills and sound judgement
A commitment to fairness, respect, and community service
Motivation, reliability, and the ability to work independently
Why Join Us?
This is an excellent opportunity to build a meaningful career in law enforcement while contributing to the safety and well-being of Toronto s diverse communities. As a Special Constable, you will gain valuable experience, training, and development within one of Canada s largest and most respected police services.
What can I expect to do in this role?
As a Special Constable, you may be required to rotate in any of the following positions throughout your career:
Assigned to Court Services
, you will be responsible for but not limited to:
Maintaining security and control of persons in custody who must attend court
Transporting prisoners to and from detention centres, immigration facilities, medical facilities, hospitals, police divisions, court houses, arrest locations or other detention locations
Controlling, monitoring and escorting persons lodged in holding cells and escorting them to court
Maintaining security and order in courtrooms
Monitoring courthouse entrances via electronic screening
Executing arrests when required
Obtaining DNA samples from persons in and out of custody, as ordered by the court
Attending court and testifying as required
Assigned to the booking area
of a division, you will be responsible for but not limited to:
Booking of prisoners, including searching, fingerprinting and photographing persons in custody
Maintain the security and wellbeing of prisoners in custody
Liaise and communicate with various stakeholders throughout the division and the Service regarding prisoner status and management
Manage persons in emotional crisis and physical distress, using available resources such as MCIT, Emergency Medical Services or arranging transport to a hospital, as appropriate
Attending court and testifying as required
Assigned to a division
, you will be responsible for but not limited to:
Report writing, evidence collecting, canvassing and assisting in search of missing persons.
Enforcement of some City of Toronto parking by-laws
Attending and assisting in protecting secured crime scenes under on-scene police constables or supervisors
Maintaining a notebook containing an accurate and thorough account of up-to-date- activities
Prisoner transportation, prisoner security and prisoner management
Attending court and testifying as required
How do I qualify?
Minimum Requirements:
Successful completion of Grade 12 (OSSD or equivalent)
Have a minimum of one year of related experience (i.e. working with the general public or working in a customer service environment)
Must be Canadian Citizen or Permanent Resident
License and Certification Requirements:
Possess valid "G" driver's license (upon submission of application) with no more than six demerit points, permitting you to drive an automobile in Ontario with full driving privileges
Current certification in Intermediate First Aid (formerly known as Standard First Aid) from an accredited agency by the time an offer of employment is given.
Possess a valid O.A.C.P. (Ontario Association of Chiefs of Police Certificate) certificate.
Have a minimum of 20/40 (uncorrected) vision, with normal colour acuity.
Successfully pass the hearing and vision standards as outlined by the O.A.C.P.
Successfully complete the PREP (Shuttle Run: Stage 6 & Pursuit Restraint Circuit within 3 minutes)
For further information on obtaining an OACP Certificate of Results and/or testing, visit:
https://oacpcertificate.ca
Please Note: If selected to move forward, applicants will be invited to attend the PREP test at the Toronto Police College.
Skills/Competencies:
Ability to deal effectively with persons in crisis and to work in a stressful environment that requires problem solving, judgement, conflict resolution, communication, teamwork and co-operation
Possess strong interpersonal and communication skills in order to deal with members of the Service, persons in custody and the public in a professional and tactful manner
Motivated self-starter, able to work with minimal supervision
Must be able to endure prolonged physical activity associated to rigorous defensive tactics training, on a daily basis
Conditions of Employment:
Must successfully pass the required Toronto Police Service driving test to operate a police vehicle (TPS Blue Card)
Deemed medically fit for the position through a medical assessment
Meet all requirements to attain the status of a Special Constable as outlined by the Ministry
Successfully complete the Special Constable Training Program that consists of:
15 week training program at TPC (70 Birmingham Street)
Monday to Friday 7am - 3pm (may also include evenings and weekends)
Probation Period:
6 months

title: Communications Operator
description:
Posting Title: Communication Operator
Job ID #: 8029
Status: Regular Full-Time
Salary: $83,538 - $109,755
Shift: This position is assigned to a platoon-based rotational schedule. All employees are required to work a regular rotation of days, nights, weekends, and statutory holidays.
Location: Communications Services
Vacancies: Several
Job Code: C71CMZ Class 7 (40 hours)
Our Mindset ~ Our Connections ~ Our Impact ~ Our Development
Service at our Core ~ Do the right thing ~ Connect with Compassion ~ Reflect and Grow
The Opportunity:
Can you stay calm when others can t?
In moments of crisis, the voice of 911 becomes a lifeline to community members experiencing their worst day. Are you able to think clearly, listen actively, and make rapid, sound life and death decisions under pressure?
Do you listen to understand?
Can you pick up on what s said and what s not? Do you have the ability to hear urgency, fear, or confusion and respond with clarity and compassion?
Are you passionate about serving the city of Toronto and all its communities?
Are you a master of multitasking?
Can you juggle multiple calls, systems, and priorities without missing a beat? Do you thrive in fast paced environments? Are you seeking challenge and meaning in your career? Are you able to manage multiple on-going tasks and changing priorities?
Is your communication clear and confident?
Whether it s a panicked caller or a police officer in the field, can you deliver information calmly, accurately, and respectfully?
Do you have the resilience to handle tough situations?
Emergencies are unpredictable. Can you manage stress, maintain emotional control, and bounce back after difficult calls? Do you understand the importance of a health work-life balance and have mechanisms in place to cope with difficult situations?
Are you tech-savvy and detail-oriented?
Can you operate complex communication systems and databases while staying focused on accuracy and procedure?
Can you think critically under pressure?
Emergencies are dynamic.
Situations change in a moment as do the requirements of our communications operators.
Are you flexible and adaptable? Are you able to think critically through situations? Can you analyze situations and apply relevant policies and procedures?
Do you thrive in a team environment?
Can you coordinate with police, fire, ambulance, and other agencies to ensure the right help gets to the right place fast?
If You Answered Yes ...
You might be exactly who we re looking for.
The Toronto Police Service is seeking
exceptional individuals
to become
Communications Operators
the calm in the chaos, the voice of reason, and the first point of contact in emergencies.
What can I expect in this role?
In this role, you will be responsible for receiving, monitoring and assessing incoming emergency calls, and taking or expediting the required action in accordance with Service procedures.
This is a dynamic work environment. As a Communications Operator, you will:
Answer 911 calls from citizens in life-threatening and emergency situations.
Answer telephone calls on the non-emergency, dedicated and internal police lines and take the appropriate action.
Provide instructions and support to callers in distress, building rapport and valuing lived experiences.
Dispatch police officers and support units to emergency situations; coordinating with partner agencies such as Ambulance and Fire as required.
Monitor events and adjust priorities in real time based on updates and new information.
Monitor police pursuits and gather information to assist the supervisor and the police officer(s) involved. Liaise with other divisions or other police services to provide an appropriate response
Operate various computerized communications consoles and associated equipment to receive, assess and relay information to police officers in the field. Report major or unusual occurrences to supervisor
Operate Services databases (including C.P.I.C.) to check for and relay requested information to field personnel
Perform typical duties inherent to the position such as conducting follow-up calls to citizens, other police units or related agencies as required.
How do I qualify?
Mandatory:
Must have successful completion of grade 12 or an approved equivalent combination of education, training, and experience. Official
transcripts and diplomas will be required.
Note:
If you received your high school and/or college education in a province other than Ontario, or;
If you received your high school, college and/or university education in a country other than Canada, you
MUST
obtain official proof of equivalency from an accredited agency, such as the International Credential Assessment Services of Canada (ICAS) or World Education Services - Canada (WES Canada).
Educational equivalency documentation MUST be presented upon request.
Must have a minimum of two years of previous customer service experience in a fast paced and multi-tasking environment.
Must be available to work on-going, regular, rotating shifts, including days, nights, weekends, and statutory holidays as scheduled.
Ability to hear and readily relay information accurately with high attention to detail, while operating various methods of communication equipment (Computer Aided Dispatch, TTY, portable radios, telephones) despite constant interruptions and distractions.
Must successfully complete the medical approval process, including vision and hearing tests.
In addition, the Toronto Police Service values the following qualifications:
Completion of a recognized Public Safety Communication Course is an asset.
Experience in emergency response, and/or high-stress call centre environments is preferred.
Key Competencies:
Resilience:
High level of emotional stability and resilience under high-pressure situations, maintaining composure and sound judgment during times of high stress and high emotions over long term exposure.
Ability to navigate through dynamic situations involving a high level of stress and maintaining composure. Keep calm, collective and make quick life changing decisions.
Solid understanding of a healthy work life balance and reliable, healthy coping strategies to manage stress over the long term.
Multi-tasking in a fast-paced environment:
Strong multitasking skills with the ability to prioritize tasks and deal with critical and time sensitive calls for service.
Ability to confidently make emergency decisions and act on these decisions under strict and definitive policies and procedures.
Customer Service:
Strong customer service skills with experience to influence and de-escalate others emotions to provide service during emergency situations.
Ability to de-escalate conflict in a professional and tactful manner over the phone.
Problem Solving:
Ability to deal effectively with persons in crisis and work in a stressful environment which requires problem solving, judgement, conflict resolution, de-escalation, communication, teamwork and co-operation.
Testing Process:
Applicants must successfully pass a multi-level CritiCall testing process.
Phase 1 (CritiCall)
Candidates will be tested on CritiCall software which tests short term memory, keyboarding (typing speed), spelling, clarity and reading comprehension.
Call taking skills, such as computer-related multi-taking abilities, data entry skills, memory retention, prioritization, map reading, call summarization and performance under stress.
If selected, you will receive an email from TEST GENIUS where you will be provided with instructions. Please monitor both your inbox and junk/spam for this email.
Note:
Candidates will only be allowed one (1) attempt for CritiCall Testing per job posting. Duplicate applications will not be considered and will result in your removal from the job call process.
Only applicants who are successful in the Criti
C
all testing (Phase 1) will proceed to Phase 2 of testing.
Phase 2 (Perfex):
A telecommunications simulator test, measuring motor skills, eye-hand co-ordination, multi-tasking, memory retention and performance under stress. This test includes a hand-written component.
Candidates successful at Phase 2 testing will proceed to the following recruitment stages:
Interview
Background Checks (inclusive of a psychological assessment)
Job Shadow
Conditions of Employment:
Must pass medical assessment.
Must successfully pass the intensive training program:
Communications Operators must successfully complete a lengthy, intensive (paid) training program - comprised of 7 weeks of in-class call-taker training, followed by live environment coaching for 240 hours, and 5 weeks of in-class dispatch training, followed by live environment coaching for 240 hours. Training will include days, afternoons, midnights and weekends. You will be reporting to various locations during your training program, which will be provided to you on the first day of class. A minimum standard of 75% is required on tests and practical examinations to remain in the training program.
Communication Operators are assigned to a platoon and are required to regularly work weekends as part of their rotational schedule. All Communications Operators are also required to work statutory holidays as the rotational platoon schedule. Communication Services is staffed 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, 365 days year.
Communication Operators will handle emergency 9-1-1 and non-emergency calls.
The most serious emergencies include difficult and stressful situations such as violent crimes in progress, suicidal callers, fatalities, and traumatic events.
These calls are expected and regular daily occurrences.
Communication Operators are expected to be calm and make decisions methodically based on their critical thinking skills, TPS protocol and training.
Communication Operators will be exposed to difficult situations and require intense concentration for extended periods of time.
Due to the nature of the work, Communication Operators are restricted to their workstation, breaks and lunches are pre-scheduled and dependent upon workload.
Must be able to commit to the Communication Operators work schedule
.
Must be able and willing to commute to work location for the job. NO REMOTE WORK.
Must be able to understand the serious and stressful nature of the calls I may be required to handle.
Must be able to make sound and rapid decisions in a highly fast-paced and stressful environment
.
Probationary Period:
18 Months
As a condition of employment, you will need to successfully meet the minimum standards within the 18-month probation period.

[email protected]

The Toronto Police Service is looking for exceptional
Experienced Police Constables
who want to serve the city of Toronto and protect the community.
Modernizing the Toronto Police Service will be achieved by transforming how we relate to the public, how we deliver our service, how people access our services, ensuring the affordability and sustainability of our operations, and creating a culture of excellence. The Human Resources modernization plan will support our efforts by hiring members to support community-centric policing, diversity and inclusion. These are important principles because the ability of the Toronto Police Service to keep Toronto the best and safest place to be has always depended on the trust and support of the people we serve.
As an experienced officer joining the Toronto Police Service, your focus will be to protect members of the public, to prevent and investigate crimes and to assist victims. In joining us, you will work in partnership with communities and service delivery agencies to address crime, disorder, and community safety issues with an understanding of, and a sensitivity toward, the complex needs specific to each neighbourhood.
To learn more about the benefits of working for the Toronto Police Service, we invite you to watch the following video clips featuring members who joined as experienced officers (links will open in a new window):
Adrianne's Story
Paul's Story
Ennis' Story

Conducting full and thorough investigations of offences
Preparing for and attending court, hearings, or inquiries to give evidence
Providing support immediately after an incident which can victimize, traumatize, or create concern for a neighbourhood and its residents
Being proactive and using information, evidence, and insights from neighbourhood partners to identify issues and co-develop solutions, including referrals to appropriate community resources
Protecting life and property, and preserving the peace

Be physically and mentally able to perform the duties of the position, having regard to your own safety, and the safety of others
Have successfully completed police constable recruit training at the Ontario Police College, R.C.M.P. Depot, or other accredited facility

For a conditional discharge, this will be done automatically following three years if the conditional discharge is registered after July 24, 1992. Otherwise you must apply to have these records sealed)
Must not have any current charges pending before the courts
Must have a valid driver's licence with a good driving record, permitting you to drive an automobile in Canada with full driving privileges
Must have valid Standard First Aid and CPR level C certification from an accredited agency by time of offer
Must not currently be the subject of any disciplinary proceedings or any internal or external complaint/investigative proceedings
In addition, the Toronto Police Service values the following qualifications:
Completed post-secondary education
Demonstrated knowledge, understanding and appreciation for equity, human rights, and the importance of diversity and inclusion in all communities
Understanding of local community safety and justice-related issues

Demonstrated ability to work under pressure and make decisions in complex and potentially dangerous and stressful conditions

The Toronto Police Service is the fourth largest municipal police service in North America. With over 5,000 officers and 2,000 civilian employees, we take pride in our diversity and in our dedication to keeping Toronto the best and safest place to be. Our well-earned reputation as a world leader in policing is a reflection of our commitment to excellence, innovation, quality leadership, and ongoing professional
development.
A career in policing is primarily about working with people to ensure public safety through crime prevention and law enforcement. Police work requires the building of relationships in the community, and sensitivity towards the needs of people from all races, cultures, and backgrounds.
The Toronto Police Service is currently hiring. We are looking for exceptional people who want to serve the city of Toronto and protect the community as a cadet in-training to become a Police Constable.
Modernizing the Toronto Police Service will be achieved by transforming how we relate to the public, how we deliver our service, how people access our services, ensuring the affordability and sustainability of our operations, and creating a culture of excellence. The Human Resources modernization plan will support our efforts by hiring recruits to support community-centric policing, diversity and inclusion. These are important principles because the ability of the Toronto Police Service to keep Toronto the best and safest place to be has always depended on the trust and support of the people we serve.
The fundamental role of a police officer is about commitment to public service. As a new constable or an experienced officer joining the Toronto Police Service, your focus will be to protect members of the public, to prevent and investigate crimes and to assist victims. In joining us, you will work in partnership with communities and service delivery agencies to address crime, disorder, and community safety issues with an understanding of, and a sensitivity toward, the complex needs specific to each neighbourhood.
A police constable's job is a complex one. Some of the key responsibilities include:
conducting a full and thorough investigation of offences;
preparing for and attending court, a hearing or inquiry to give evidence;
